author: dhh
SentientEco
quoted_text:
A fingerprint surviving fine-tuning is useful evidence. It doesn't tell us whether that fingerprint will survive someone deliberately trying to hide it.

That distinction is at the centre of Sentient Foundation's new model provenance report.

Many fingerprinting evaluations test benign transformations: fine-tuning, merging, and other ordinary changes to model weights.

Real provenance disputes can involve an adaptive adversary who knows verification is happening.

The report tested 10 published fingerprinting methods against attacks designed to evade detection. Nine were evaded almost completely, while the models retained more than 90% of their performance on standard tests. The remaining method was evaded about 65% of the time. Under the tested settings, none resisted the complete attack suite.

There is an important engineering lesson here: persistence and security are different properties. Passing a fine-tuning test does not establish resistance to deliberate evasion.

Fingerprinting can provide technical evidence of model origin or lineage. It cannot independently establish legal ownership, reconstruct a model's full development history, or guarantee that a model is clean when no fingerprint is detected.

AI teams need to treat provenance as a layered process:

- Keep development records, model lineage and distribution logs.
- Use fingerprints and watermarks as evidence, not absolute proof.
- Test against adaptive attacks, not only benign transformations.
- Publish evaluation methods, access assumptions and failure cases.
- Combine technical checks with contracts and access controls.

Open models need open provenance evaluations. Builders should be able to inspect what a method detects, what it misses, and how it performs when someone actively tries to defeat it.

The report: https://t.co/l5Jgz4n6K2

author: gregoireljda
quoted_text:
My read on the Sky / Rune situation:

-- nothing wrong per se with founders borrowing against their own token. it shows long-term alignment (they're long their own company) and gives them liquidity without selling.

-- the risk right now is to SKY the token, not necessarily to Sky the protocol. worst case, Rune's vaults get liquidated, SKY takes a hit, and if the sale doesn't cover the debt, stUSDS depositors eat the shortfall. USDS itself is walled off. (stUSDS sales on Curve are already pricing a haircut)

— the deeper issue is in how this vault was set up:
good that it's segregated from the rest of the protocol. not good that liquidations are off and depositors are locked in.
not good that it was Rune himself who proposed settings that would govern his own loans.
not good that Rune accounts for half the pool's loans.

But it sounds like he's finding a way out and recognizing the mistake and communicating publicly throughout goes a long way.

text:
回答：我有一个 xx 产品，应该如何推广？

这个问题我被问过很多次，只要尝试去回答，就是半小时起步，先要重构整个财商教育的基础框架，然后再告诉提问者，为什么这个问题是错误的。

Eric Ries 在《精益创业》里面说，顾客接触到的任何事物，都是公司的产品。

所以如果你不知道如何去推广你的产品，那么实际上你并不拥有任何产品，你只是有一些碎片而已。

一位顾客在奢侈品门店接触到一款包包之前，已经提前体验了：测试了无数次的橱窗布置、特定材质的店门把手、和当下主题相关的气味香氛、色温精准调过的灯光、统一培训的导购举止、翻毛皮面料的托盘、适合当天温度的一杯水（甚至要区分矿泉水和纯净水）……

然后，才终于看见了一款包

这时候你说，我亲戚在广东的工厂，可以做出和爱马仕一模一样的包，就是不知道怎么推广。。。

「做生意要先找到买家」实际上说的是同一件事。

所谓的找到买家，其实是要找到一条路径，可以把供给和需求连起来。

而在这条路径上，你可能要做几十上百件事情，去一点一点推动买家的心智往前更进一步，才能最终达成交易。

会有人觉得，“产品和推广同等重要”，他们的潜台词是，我的产品已经做出来了，这完成了 50%，还剩 50% 是推广没有完成。

但实际上，这种认知程度，还不如没上过学的农民。农民种一吨橘子，无论高卖贱卖，总是有人要的，橘子只要足够便宜，总是能出掉的。

但是你和你的清华 CTO 融资 300w 憋出来的那个大招，神来了也卖不出去。

其实有一个特别简单的办法，来判断一个人有没有搞清楚这件事情，就是看这个人会不会经常在餐馆说：我自己在菜市场买一直鸡/鸭/鹅，成本才 xxx，这餐馆竟然卖 xxx

这句话的潜台词是，餐桌上的这只烧鸡，是你花大价钱买到的产品。

实际上不是的，真正让你走进这家餐厅的产品，是你昨天晚上刷到的那条抖音。

而那条抖音恰好在昨晚 8 点被你看见，花了商家 200 元投放费用。你面前的这只烧鸡，反而是 tmd 中央厨房去年就做好了的预制菜。

如果你问 AI，什么是毛利率。AI 会说，假如商品售价 1000 元，销售成本也就是进货花了 200 元，毛利就是 80%

实际上你真的去获客可能会发现，成交一单的获客成本是 ¥900，你想不赔钱，就要逼供应链花 50 元做出一个及格线以上的，让顾客不会大规模退货的产品。

这时候你跟我说，我的毛利是 95%，因为我的销售成本就是进货，只花了 50 元？

真正的销售成本是什么？

回到开始的问题，假如我真有一个亲戚，他在广东的工厂，可以做出和爱马仕一模一样的包，应该怎么推广呢，我让 AI 列了一个简化过的门店 list，放在评论：

text:
今年沉迷上宝可梦抽卡后就开始在思考一个问题：为什么人们会陷入对这类非实用性的收藏品的痴迷情感中？直到前段时间在杭州湖滨漫游时，才意识到，在当前社会这类情绪/收藏类资产的受众无非两类人：一类是喜欢投机暴富的degen们，另一类则是需要它们作为情绪出口和精神寄托的真爱粉，而粉丝群体的聚集，又会催生出一批将其作为社交货币、以此满足炫耀心理的群体。

当我们从宏观视角来看这些资产的时候，这类低流动性资产对周期的反应也极具特色：在流动性开始扩张时，资金外溢，其价格往往在周期末尾开始出现反应，展现出极高的价格弹性。当流动性开始收紧时，由于其低流动性的特性，这类资产价格往往是在最后阶段才开始崩盘。因此，在当前流动性紧缩的大背景下，这类资产大概率会后知后觉地迎来补跌甚至崩盘，直到下一个流动性周期开启后，才有可能会再次重新起航（也有可能会像nft一样再起不能）。

这种紧缩会不可避免地对crypto x tcg项目cards产生冲击。在之前卡牌大幅增值的阶段，一次次地去gacha抽奖是一个正期望的事情，只要样本足够大，用户是可以赚到钱的。所以之前cards才能创造那么高的流水。但进入紧缩周期后，我对cards一年内的业务表现会持悲观态度。

但把周期拉长看的话，cards正在将自己从一个单一产品驱动的项目类型转型成为整个crypto卡牌赛道的基础设施。赌场的本质是分发，不管是perpdex，还是cards的gacha，都需要流量入口。在完成优质卡牌积累之后，cards也开始做分发，这个包括但不限于与coinbase、jupiter、solflare、raible的合作。未来只要有人想要做卡牌分发，都可以试着去接入cards，以获得其充沛的卡牌流动性。

另一个正在寻找分发端的项目是renaiss，目前它已经成为binance wallet tcg的卡牌基础设施。个人去体验了一下，体验还不错，卡池出卡也相对平滑。整体综合看下来，我觉得其优势是binance wallet流量入口+多端支持+丝滑的ui/ux体验，劣势是卡池深度和优质卡牌储备（对比cards，renaiss基本没啥我想要的卡）。

综上，crypto x tcg赛道已经走过了靠卡牌牛市情绪野蛮生长的第一阶段，接下来的竞争将会集中在cards（对应solana生态、coinbase支持）与renaiss（binance支持）之间，本质上是供给（卡池丰富度和深度，cards占优）与分发（流量入口，renaiss占优）的竞争。

短期内，紧缩周期的开始和深入会给整个赛道降温，样本足够大的抽卡不再会是正期望（所以如果没有你喜欢的卡，我是真不建议去频繁去抽）。当流动性回归时，那种把1️⃣后端卡池流动性+2️⃣前端流量入口+3️⃣透明化代币回购做好的项目的币还是可以玩玩的（少一点就没赔率）。

这可不是舆论面打嘴仗，这是实打实的机械性砸盘。 全球跟踪MSCI指数的被动ETF和被动资金，手里捏着微策略大约1300万股股票。 按照基金铁律，时间一到，无论大盘跌成什么样，电脑程序都必须无脑砍仓卖出。

Saylor显然早就慌了。 最新披露的SEC文件里，微策略不仅象征性地小买了457枚比特币把持仓凑到85.1万枚，更关键的是把优先股回购上限一口气拉到了40亿美元。 以前他的飞轮是：高溢价发股票割韭菜买比特币，把股价炒高再发股票。 现在溢价被挤干，华尔街被动基金还要在月底无脑砸盘，他只能自己掏几十亿美金在下面当人肉沙袋。

Compute markets are finally here.

@Polymarket now prices on-demand compute for @nvidia H100s, B200s, and B300s, out to 2028. More chips and terms soon. https://t.co/JAJHRcAk8N

Think of it as a yield curve for the cost of compute: the forecasted $/hour price of each chip at every expiry, and whether it's trending up or down. The whole AI economy rides on these prices, and until today there was no public market for where they're going. Which is nuts. So Polymarket built it.

This will change how compute gets bought and financed. Every contract negotiation and every GPU loan will have a market price to check against.

Hundreds of billions of dollars are being committed to compute years in advance. Many of those deals are essentially a levered bet on what GPUs will rent for in the future (what could go wrong lol)

As AI financing sobers up, the labs buying compute, the providers selling it, and the lenders financing it will all need to hedge that risk.

We think compute could become one of the largest financial markets in the world. This launch is Polymarket's first step toward building it. 

If you’re buying, selling, or financing compute, DM us with what markets you'd like to see.

text:
我倒是没生气啦。随便去吧。
我接着回复一下FRANKY的问题：
宝可梦卡牌是不是CSGO的二道开箱模式？

其实桌游界有三大尽头，其中之一是TCG，也就是集换式卡牌。这个东西的发展史非常长。导致后面有很多游戏都借鉴了这个东西。
关键点是：
1，IP
2，开箱开包（赌）
3，稀有度区分
4，集，换。
因为有IP和稀有度，所以才会交换和收集，从而掩盖开箱这个赌的操作，把赌变成了一种上瘾，把开包变成了一种类似于点击“开单”一样的操作。这也是我为什么说币安的宝可梦卡牌做的非常好，他的“买入”是一个类似撕开包装的动作。从产品设计和人类行为学上来说，弱化了赌的本质，更让人上瘾。

其实在此基础上，CSGO最重要的是产生了销毁机制。也就是一些首饰皮肤是有耐久度的。这加大了珍惜度，也侧面提供了一定的保值机制。现在的TCG大多数都是滥发的。
所以如果你想创业，做TCG的东西，最简单的就是照抄CSGO的系统，做出本地化修改，再加上一个好的IP。

Polymarket now lets anyone trade what it costs to rent an H100 by the hour, out to December 2028.

Ornn's index of real H100 deals settled at $3.10 an hour on Wednesday. The market has December 2027 at $2.71 and December 2028 at $2.14.

So traders are pricing a chip that started shipping in 2022 to still rent for more than $2 an hour six years later. Contracts settle in cash against the index and nobody receives a GPU, but a lender or a buyer can now look at a public curve for what a GPU hour is worth years out.

On the same index B200 settled at $9.76 and B300 at $10.83.

In my opinion a public price curve makes it easier for banks to fund the next round of GPUs

Compute markets are finally here.

@Polymarket now prices on-demand compute for @nvidia H100s, B200s, and B300s, out to 2028. More chips and terms soon. https://t.co/JAJHRcAk8N

Think of it as a yield curve for the cost of compute: the forecasted $/hour price of each chip at every expiry, and whether it's trending up or down. The whole AI economy rides on these prices, and until today there was no public market for where they're going. Which is nuts. So Polymarket built it.

This will change how compute gets bought and financed. Every contract negotiation and every GPU loan will have a market price to check against.

Hundreds of billions of dollars are being committed to compute years in advance. Many of those deals are essentially a levered bet on what GPUs will rent for in the future (what could go wrong lol)

As AI financing sobers up, the labs buying compute, the providers selling it, and the lenders financing it will all need to hedge that risk.

We think compute could become one of the largest financial markets in the world. This launch is Polymarket's first step toward building it. 

If you’re buying, selling, or financing compute, DM us with what markets you'd like to see.

text:
🎉 全体起立！终于拿到网易 UU 远程 Linux 版的内测资格了！
等这一天太久了，甚至我在新加坡跑 Claude Code 的 Mac mini，以后都可能换成一台几百块的 Linux 小主机了。

收到通知那一刻是真激动。我手上的 GPU 服务器全是 Linux，以前想远程用，要么只能 SSH，要么自己搭跳板、绕云服务器中转，又慢又折腾。这次千呼万唤始出来，第一时间就装上了。

用了几天，说说实测感受，UU远程延迟低，速度快。

Mac 远程连 Linux ，同一时段测了三种方案（主控端和被控端都在国内，硬件和网络环境不变）：
延迟这块： UU 22ms，Tailscale 26ms，阿里云中继 49ms。
上传速度： UU 跑到 36Mbps，Tailscale 24Mbps，阿里云只有 5.4Mbps。
我还拿 720p 实时换脸直播试了一下，UU 能跑到 23.8fps，帧率是阿里云中继的 3 倍。

端口映射这个功能真的香。以前想从外面连家里的 Linux 服务器，还得折腾公网 IP、跳板机。现在直接映射几个端口，SSH 和自己跑的服务都能连上，省了不少事。

小遗憾，目前得装桌面，服务器上要多折腾一步。最期待下一步出个免桌面版，那对服务器用户就完美了。

最后说个终极的玩法。
以前为了在新加坡跑 Claude Code，我放了一台Mac mini。
现在我就在琢磨，能不能直接搞台几百块的 Linux 小主机，把那台 5000 块的 Mac mini 替下来？真能跑顺的话，这笔钱可省大了。
有 Linux 服务器的兄弟，必装，冲了。

Quite an impressive update by @reya_xyz.

They’ve integrated @Polymarket odds into Reya Agentic, allowing traders to build automated trading strategies around real-world events.

You can now pick a Polymarket event, set an odds threshold, and tell Reya what trade to execute when it’s crossed.

For example:

"Sell 20% of my $BTC holdings on Reya's DEX if Polymarket’s odds of a Fed rate increase in December surge above 50%"

Once you’ve set up your rule, you can see exactly what will trigger a trade and what order Reya will submit (you approve the rule once).

You can also set a max loss before you let it run. If the strategy hits that limit, Reya closes its open positions and stops it.

Polymarket is just the first of many external data sources. In the future, you'll be able to build strategies around a combination of odds, sentiment, posts, and prices from other trading venues.

text:
Crypto is DEAD.

At least that is what one would believe if you just read Crypto Twitter. No fresh money coming in, VCs sitting on their hands, every pump sort of gone within 48 hours.

But is it really dead?

Many tend to overcomplicate the situation at the moment, in typical crypto style. But honestly, what we are currently seeing is fairly simple. As a VC, or in that matter, any investor, you aim to bet on the fastest horse. Crypto is not the fastest horse at the moment; it is AI. If you want exposure to frontier tech, you will, hence, park your capital within the AI industry.

But how sustainable is that?

🔹 The AI model is based on a compute arms race; hence, every time Nvidia has a stronger card, all these AI companies have to follow suit and buy it to remain competitive.

🔸 The customer on the other side is used to ~$20/month (e.g. Netflix, Spotify), and that number isn't moving much

🔹 Uber and Tesla subsidized for years too, which is fine, but compute has to be replaced all the time

The result is a super capital-intensive industry with very little pricing power. Sure, they can hike the price at some point and use predatory pricing, but chips get outdated much more quickly than cars.

Now, on top of that, take into account that the market is extremely overleveraged. As many are taking the same bet: AI. AI-related debt issuance has surpassed $500 billion in 2026. That's more debt than Taiwan, Iceland, and Qatar have combined.

But how come no one is touching crypto?

As Crypto trades 24/7, it has often been frontrunning dramatic events. Therefore, you do see that crypto is often taking hits before the public equity market does.

For example, on Monday one Nvidia headline took $BTC from a $55K weekend low to $64K before Wall St had even opened. In other words, crypto is sort of the early warning system for AI sentiment at the moment.

Can crypto bounce?

Yes. As it is probable that the AI 'bubble' will burst. The question is, where will the capital in that case flow to? That could be absolutely crypto, as long as there is an interesting narrative.

The question is whether you're still in the game when it happens. In Dec 2018, sentiment was way worse than it is today, and BTC went to $3K. A year later, it was around $7K again.

Losing is fine, just don't blow up your capital.

Stay in the game.

text:
This post blew up, and a lot of friends have been sending it to me, but is it true?

Currently, AI is putting pressure on traditional cryptography and cybersecurity, but that pressure can also make crypto stronger (maybe even a catalyst for the next bull run?).

Key facts:
- Even with AI assistance, factoring still hasn’t broken RSA-2048.
- Bitcoin and Ethereum use ECC signatures, not RSA, so faster RSA attacks don’t directly apply.
- ECC is vulnerable to sufficiently powerful quantum computers, which is why the shift to post-quantum cryptography is underway.

Why I see this as bullish for crypto:

• NIST has approved post-quantum standards, giving builders a foundation for developing quantum-resistant security.

• Ethereum is developing hash-based signatures for wallets and validators, with early testing underway. The work to upgrade existing networks is already happening.

The bigger catalyst is making onchain finance more credible for long-term capital.

If these upgrades prove reliable, they could reduce a long-term custody risk for institutions bringing stablecoins and tokenized assets onchain. Networks that make the transition safely could gain an advantage when institutions choose where to build.

That creates a potential path from stronger security to more capital onchain, and more demand for settlement and DeFi liquidity.

---

More details on RSA, ECC, and quantum cryptography below ⤵
author: Eli5defi
quoted_text:
If this rumors are true, it would explain why OpenAI and Anthropic are holding back their latest models: 

Scott Aaronson says he's heard OpenAI or Anthropic may have found a way to factor large numbers in polynomial time.

Why this would be massive? RSA secures a huge chunk of the internet, and its whole security relies on factoring big numbers being impossible on normal computers. If an algorithm like this actually works on real key sizes, you wouldn't even need a quantum computer to break it. Fake software updates could pass signature checks, RSA-encrypted data could be read, and systems across the internet would have to migrate off RSA fast.

So yeah, something we expected might now actually happening.

text:
Year Two

Some assorted goals:

- make Monad a legitimately great platform for personal finance (investing in equities, bonds, etc), especially for getting access to markets outside of one's home country. So much of the usage in crypto right now is gambling/memecoins... it is what it is, but personal finance appeals to 100x more people, and they don't churn out. A legitimately great platform has great asset selection, efficient execution (low cost both in and out of a position), and competitive rates both for borrowers and lenders

- ship Private Settlement Domains with the first user, to serve as a case study for anyone trying to reason about how private environments can compose with shared liquidity. Public chains and private environments have been very far apart in practice and it's time to change that

- hammer out an excellent liquidity landscape on chain. It is a mix of order books, prop AMMs, offchain routers, onchain routers, and RFQ... especially with tokenized equities, there is a long long tail of assets and we need to minimize spreads so that the offering is competitive with TradFi. Spread minimization means helping makers quote sustainably; here designs like APES can help

- make it easier for AI to produce actually good trading strategies on command for anyone to execute a trading plan efficiently with algos. There is are a ton of slop startups out there which are a wrapper around claude asking it "should I buy or sell given these textual inputs"... that's not real quant research and not good execution. At the same time, there are a lot of building blocks for quant trading that AI couldn't one-shot, but given the blocks it could put them together sensibly

- contribute to there being fewer hacks (and a lower total $ stolen) in the crypto industry, probably through a combination of repetition about dedicated devices (SO many hacks are from people plugging hardware wallets into everyday laptops) and encouraging everyone to use tools that our team has shipped for agentic threat detection (e.g. Ultrafuzz). I truly think that security is the biggest blocker to adoption, and that we're basically all in this together

- drive the car faster than ever in multiple races - MEV-resistance, quantum-resistance, privacy, and MCP, challenging all competitors to ship or be left behind

- help NFTs and onchain social -- two deeply out-of-consensus areas -- make a comeback. The builders in these sectors these days are incredibly committed; there's never been a better filtering function

- contribute to tech optimism. So many doomers out there. Life is electric, building is electric

- contribute to a less stressful environment for builders. It is a very weird time to be a builder in DeFi... on the one hand, tools are better than ever... on the other hand, capital is scarce and crypto-natives are jaded. The approach to building ironically requires both more introspection and more rapid, rapid shipping

- support the excellent individuals on our team at MF become leaders in the space in their respective domains. We have amazing folks here and the space needs leadership more than ever

- support someone building a total moonshot

- build at least one product that has a lot of everyday-people customers, and deliver a ton of value to them

- become willing to repeatedly say the same thing, until it starts to sink in

亚马逊老总 @JeffBezos 已经足够富有，火箭也送上了太空，但他还是带着累计超 $180 亿融资的 @PrometheusInc 杀回一线创业了。

而他押注的方向，不是眼下最卷的聊天机器人，而是面向几十万亿美元物理制造的工程大模型，想把 AI 从数字世界（Bits）带进原子世界（Atoms）。

在最近的专访里，他认为，“把牛顿、爱因斯坦、麦克斯韦关进同一间屋子，让他们造一台烤面包机，这几位人类史上最伟大的物理学家照样无从下手。”

因为懂麦克斯韦方程组，解决不了发热丝的材质阻抗、热绝缘和微米级公差。

在他看来，现在的大语言模型读遍了互联网，写代码、做数学、背法条都没问题，但终究只是在摆弄符号。“就像你读了一千本关于体操的书，合上书依然跳不出一支舞。”

至于为什么日子过得这么舒服，还要挑这么难的事从零开始？Bezos 说，2024 年底投了天使轮之后，看着团队早期的突破，自己根本坐不住，没法只待在场边看。

他管这叫“第二类快乐（Type 2 Fun）”：就像爬雪山，往上走的时候每一步都喘不上气，过程很煎熬，但登顶那一刻的痛快感无可替代。

“这支团队有一股纯粹的传教士劲头。如果不喜欢这种智力与工程挑战，你可能不适合这里；但对我来说，这里就是乐土。”

quoted_text:
BTC本轮熊市到底了吗？历史周期给出的答案，可能比想象中更接近底部！

先说结论：我认为BTC已经进入本轮周期的底部博弈阶段，但目前还不能确认最终底部已经出现。#OKX

我认为本轮周期最终底部大概率在50000-60000美元之间，重点关注52000-56000美元区域，时间窗口倾向于2026年11月底至2027年1月。

为什么这么判断？从历史周期、技术结构、宏观流动性和机构资金几个维度来看。

一、先看历史周期：时间上已经进入底部窗口

过去三轮BTC完整熊市，顶部到最终底部的时间分别约为406天、364天和366天，最大回撤分别约为84.5%、83.8%和76.7%。

本轮BTC于2025年10月创下约124824美元的阶段高点，随后持续回撤，如果按照过去三轮熊市的时间规律推算，本轮底部窗口大致落在2026年10月至11月。

目前已经进入这个历史时间窗口。

但有一点值得注意：本轮BTC从顶部回撤至58500美元附近，最大跌幅约53%，明显小于过去几轮熊市。

这说明本轮市场结构确实发生了变化，ETF、机构资金和市场成熟度改变了BTC的流动性结构，但并不意味着熊市不会继续深化。

二、技术结构：58500美元是关键分水岭

从周线来看，当前BTC已经重新回到2021年历史高位密集成交区。

这个区域有两个重要意义：

一是2021年的历史顶部区域，二是2024年突破前的重要筹码区域，历史压力位转化为支撑位，是BTC长期趋势中值得重视的结构。

我认为接下来重点观察三个区域：

58500美元：本轮前期低点，也是当前最重要的多空分水岭。

52000—56000美元：如果前低失守，这是我认为更值得关注的潜在底部区域。

48000-50000美元：极端流动性冲击下需要防范的区域，但目前不作为主判断。

三、为什么我不认为现在可以盲目抄底？

最大的原因是资金。

美国现货BTC ETF此前出现持续净流出，机构资金尚未形成稳定的回流趋势。

与此同时，美股科技板块估值承压，AI资本开支回报率受到市场重新审视，纳指波动加大。

再叠加美国货币政策的不确定性、通胀压力以及国际局势带来的风险溢价，全球风险资产仍然面临流动性考验。

BTC目前最大的压力，不只是技术性回调，而是现货增量资金不足。没有持续的现货买盘，单靠合约资金推动的反弹，很难形成真正可靠的反转。

当然，如果58500美元附近能够守住，ETF资金重新转为净流入，美股企稳，同时BTC出现放量反弹、周线结构反转，那么不排除前期低点已经是最终底部。

反过来，如果58500美元有效跌破，就需要警惕继续向52000美元附近寻找支撑。

我不会为了追求一个更低的价格，而忽略已经出现的底部信号。

最后，说说我的操作思路。

现阶段不建议重仓一次性抄底，更不建议高杠杆赌最低点。

可以开始分批观察和布局，但真正加大仓位，需要等待二次探底确认、现货资金回流以及周线趋势修复。

我始终坚持一个观点：熊市最容易亏钱的，不是没有买在最低点，而是在底部没有确认的时候，把自己过早变成了重仓多头。

宁可少赚第一段反弹，也不要为了抄底而抄底。

这轮BTC，我更关注的已经不是还能跌多少，而是下一次真正值得出手的做多机会，究竟什么时候出现。

text:
An update on Bluefin’s next chapter.

What began as a single product has grown into a multi-product ecosystem. Bluefin has processed more than $100B in cumulative trading volume and grown to more than 2.5M accounts. Bluefin Perps has been a core part of that growth, and the community around it helped build the foundation for what Bluefin is today.

As the Sui team internalizes more of the network’s perps initiatives, we believe Bluefin’s resources are best focused on opportunities that complement that direction. Our focus will be on growing Bluefin Spot, alongside opportunities in tokenization and real-world assets.

As part of this shift, Bluefin Perps will be discontinued on December 4, 2026 at 21:00 UTC. Please close any open positions before then. Withdrawals will remain available for a period after trading ends.

Bluefin Perps has led the perps market on Sui across all metrics, accounting for 95% of the network’s all-time perps trading volume. We’re proud of the technology we’ve built, the trust we’ve earned from traders, and our strong security track record.

The infrastructure behind Bluefin Perps remains the most robust trading system built on Sui. It will remain available to the community and potential partners through the Bluefin Liquidity Network program, allowing the technology our engineering team has built to support new products.

We’re choosing to put our strengths behind the opportunities we believe will matter most for Bluefin’s future.

Thank you to everyone who has traded with us and helped make Bluefin what it is today. We’re excited to keep building with you. Onwards.

Bluefin team.

author: lieying003
quoted_text:
【妖币做市商是怎么出货的，妖币的出货方式有哪些】

当做市商操盘币价到达高位后，就需要考虑怎么退出的问题，目前的出货方式有以下几种

1. ADL 强制止盈平仓多单合约
这个相信大家并不陌生，推特上经常也有合约被爆仓数百万美元的大户，其中就是大户和套利用户最害怕遇到的情况。
套利用户的操作是通过开空合约吃资金费率和购买现货来对冲，由于币价在短时间内爆拉数倍，套利用户的合约仓位在高位被一根针拉爆，同时完成爆空后市场上缺少庄家的对手盘，就会触发强制止盈，庄家的合约仓位会被币安强制平仓。
套利用户的现货短时间又来不及在高位完成出货，所以经常会有套利用户和大户亏损数百万美元的案例，这部分也是庄家嘴喜欢的群体，是做市商最快退出合约流动性的方式。

2.庄家在顶部先平仓合约，在出现货
由于庄家一路拉盘，都没有等到有大鱼进场，不能通过ADL爆空来进行退出，那就只能在币价到达高位后，先平仓合约，在出现货。
这部分退出是最慢的，通常需要花费1-2个月的时间才能完成全部出货，其中庄家在下跌过程中会通过多次拉盘来吸引散户追多，幻想有二段，目的自然是为了出更多的货给散户，完成派发

3.联系社区进行出货
做市商在币价高位后也会寻找币圈有大社区的KOL，来完成喊单出货，分成比例通常是20%-30%，做市商会给一个时间，在这个时间内出的货都会算到分成里
举例，21号-22号做市商在市场卖出来100万u，就可以分到20-30万u。

4.联系KOL进行宣发
当币价到达高位后，庄家想要退出流动性，会请KOL在推特宣发，提高代币热度，吸引散户进场接货。

NEAR Intents Has Become One of the Main Venues for Swapping ZEC

More than $2.6B of zcash:native has been swapped through NEAR Intents since mid-2025, across 288,000 completed swaps. That includes 3.26M ZEC moved directly on or off the Zcash chain, equal to about a fifth of all ZEC in existence, and at its January 2026 peak, NEAR's bridge supplied 53% of all the ZEC entering Zcash's shielded pools

The flows have tracked the price closely, with heavy buying arriving ahead of both rallies and the largest net selling following them. The week of 09/14/2026 brought a record $63M of buying, $32M of it net, and the week of 10/12/2026 then saw $43M of net selling, after the price had topped out near $1,650

What sets NEAR apart from exchanges is privacy. 54% of the ZEC bought through it is delivered straight to a shielded address, 85% of the ZEC sold since January 2026 came directly out of a shielded pool, and its bridge has supplied between 13% and 26% of new shielded ZEC in most months since that January peak

Almost all of this runs through Zashi, which routes 65% of the volume compared with 16% for SwapKit. The two sides of the trade also look different, since buyers paid for 47% of their ZEC with stablecoins and 24% with BTC, while sellers took 66% of their proceeds in stablecoins and only 12% in BTC

The flow is far from purely small retail users either, as swaps over $10K make up 86% of buy volume, and the largest single purchase was 1,716 ZEC ($2.18M), paid for in BTC and delivered to a shielded address, so its owner and next moves are hidden. NEAR's bridge also holds 148,450 ZEC on the Zcash chain to back the ZEC tokens circulating on NEAR, which makes it one of the 15 largest transparent holders

text:
🟣You may already be using Aave without knowing it

Today, some @aave  users have never opened its app, or even heard of the protocol.

Over the past few months, more and more companies have been integrating it directly into their own products.

Etherfi Cash, Etherfi's payment card, is the clearest example. The company already has more than 100,000 active cards, with nearly $1 billion in annualized spending.

Since this summer, they have been running on a version of Aave V4 reserved for @ether_fi, and Aave captures 20% of the revenue it generates.

But Etherfi is far from the only one using Aave as infrastructure:

◻️ Kraken DeFi Earn

A savings product launched by @krakenfx in January. User deposits are sent to a vault that lends on Aave, with a yield that can reach around 8%.

◻️ Whop Treasury

A feature that puts idle balances to work on @whop, a creator economy platform with more than 21 million users. The funds go through Veda vaults, which deploy them on Aave's Plasma market.

◻️ Tangem

A hardware wallet whose users can deposit their stablecoins on Aave directly from the app, without going through an external website.

◻️ Ethena Earn+

@EthenaPay's yield product, whose strategy runs directly on Aave V4, on Avalanche.

For Aave, it is a way to reach an audience that would probably never have come to DeFi on its own.

Aave is now actively looking to attract more partners.

Since July, the protocol has been offering Stable Vaults to fintechs, so they can integrate it into their app with a stable rate for their customers.

Any fintech can now offer yield to its users without building its own lending/borrowing infrastructure.

We go over each of these partnerships in detail, and what they really bring in for Aave, in our full article available below 👇

上回写 Injective，聊的是 INJ 质押 ETF 登上纳斯达克，隔了 19 天，Base 上的用户也能直接用 USDC 换 INJ 了，我把这两种买法画在了一张图里 ⬇️ 

1/ 在 Base 上，钱包里拿到的是 INJ 代币

举个例子，你有 100 USDC 放在 Base 钱包里，想换成 INJ，打开平时用的 1inch 或 KyberSwap 就能看报价，整笔交易都可以在 Base 上完成 

这里分工很清楚，1inch 和 KyberSwap 帮你比价，Aero 上有一个 INJ/USDC 交易池，流动性提供者把资产放进去，如果这笔订单走 Aero 成交，你付出 USDC，池子里的 INJ 就转进你的钱包，也可以直接去 Aero 换 

这次接入最实用的地方，是大家可以继续用自己顺手的工具，9 月 INJ 上 Solana，用户可以在 Raydium 交易，这次到了 Base，连平时习惯用 Telegram 下单的人，也能通过 Maestro 买到 INJ 

2/ 在纳斯达克，证券账户里拿到的是 INJC 基金份额

11 月 5 日，Canary Capital 推出的 INJ 质押 ETF 挂牌，代码比代币多一个 C，平时买美股的人，可以在支持这只 ETF 的券商里搜 INJC，基金持有 INJ，质押所得的净收益也会反映在基金净值里 

第二天，Injective 联合创始人 Eric Chen(@ericinjective) 和 Canary Capital 创始人 Steven McClurg(@StevenMcClurg) 一起在纽约敲响了纳斯达克的开盘钟 

敲钟之后，YZi Labs 的 Ella Zhang(@ellazhang516) 翻出了几张 2018 年的老照片，那年 Eric 才 19 岁，还在纽大读金融，Injective 是当时 Binance Labs 第一期孵化的项目之一，去年 Eric 又回到 YZi Labs，给新一期的创业者当导师，今年则轮到 Ella 晒着八年前的照片，祝贺他去纳斯达克敲钟了
author: 0xBeyondLee
quoted_text:
Injective 真的算是 Binance Labs 孵化项目中的一个典范

- 2018 年，Injective 入选 Binance Labs 首期孵化计划，500 多个申请项目中最终只有 8 个入选

- 2020 年，成为首个登陆 Binance Launchpad 的 Binance Labs 孵化项目

- 2021 年，主网上线，此后逐步从一个去中心化衍生品交易协议，发展为面向金融应用的 Layer 1

- 再到 2026 年，Canary Capital 发行的 INJ 质押 ETF 正式登陆纳斯达克

从一间纽约的小办公室，到进入美国传统证券市场，Injective 用了整整 8 年

目前 INJ 市值约 8 亿美元，距离历史高点还有一定距离，但这并不妨碍它成为一个值得研究的长期发展案例

纳斯达克的意义也不只是多了一个交易渠道

传统投资者可以通过证券账户获得 INJ 敞口，ETF 还可以通过质押获取收益，这意味着 Injective 开始拥有触达传统金融市场的另一条路径

我也整理了一张图，盘点了几个曾经登上纳斯达克的加密项目，真正能走到这一步的币圈项目屈指可数，Injective 也是其中之一

另外推荐阅读 BlockBeats 最近关于 Injective 的深度报道，文笔真的太太太牛逼了，非常完整地讲述了它从 Binance Labs 孵化营走到纳斯达克的八年历程

text:
Most Ethereum wallets reveal more about you than you realise.

Even before signing a transaction, your wallet may expose.
- Your IP address to RPC providers.
- Which addresses you hold and interact with.
- Your token interests through price and balance requests.
- Your entire transaction history when connecting to dApps.

Kohaku is trying to change this.
Developed by the Ethereum Foundation, Kohaku is an open-source privacy SDK and reference wallet implementation.

Its approach goes beyond private transfers.

➔ Private writes: Integrate Privacy Pools, Railgun and Tornado Cash.
➔ Private reads: Use light clients and privacy-preserving infrastructure to reduce information leaked to RPC providers.
➔ Account security: Explore post-quantum accounts and stronger hardware-wallet signing.
➔ Less metadata leakage: Fetch token information without revealing which assets you're checking to third parties.

The important distinction is that privacy isn't just about hiding transaction amounts.

It's also about protecting what you read, which applications you use and what your wallet reveals before you even click send.

Kohaku is still under development. Some components are unaudited and shouldn't be treated as production-ready.

But the architectural direction is worth watching.

A genuinely private wallet shouldn't require users to become privacy experts. Privacy should be part of how the wallet works by default.

text:
刚从 Anthropic 转去 OpenAI 的 Thariq 在 Latent Space 发了期新播客，聊了聊他过去一年对 Coding Agent 看走眼的地方，以及接下来怎么做软件。听完记几个最有意思的点：

1. 之前觉得 "Bash is all you need"，其实是想窄了

一年前他自己也觉得，以后什么 MCP 和专用工具都不需要了，全走 CLI 就行，前端也只需要写 React，因为模型只擅长这一种套路。但他现在发现并非如此：模型只有在能力刚够用的时候，才会局限在单一格式里；等通用能力上来之后，它完全能顺着人原本的习惯干活：比如直接用 computer-use 打开 Figma 画界面。人不需要为了迁就模型去改自己的工作方式，未来也不会变成模型自己在那死循环、吐出一堆没人能维护的代码。

2. 通过保留手搓对抗纯靠 prompt 写代码的失控感 

今年到处都在吹全自动量产的「软件工厂」，结果造出一大堆连作者自己都不用的 AI slop。Thariq 提到自己做游戏时很烦纯 vibe coding 的一点：你用几句话描述需求，模型会在背后自己脑补一堆默认逻辑，跑起来连你自己都搞不清角色为什么会这么动。

他的做法是：

1. 底层的重活（比如 WebAssembly 引擎）照样丢给模型写。
2. 但在项目里单独建一个 /human 目录，放一套专门给人读写的脚本，用 Linter 强制要求多写注释、禁用单字母变量、限制行宽。

这些文件看着像 spec，但本身就是直接运行的代码。把枯燥的底层实现交给 AI，把决定手感和玩法的部分留在自己手里随时改——在他看来，AI 不只是追求效率的「工业革命」，也应该让人腾出手来做打磨品质的「文艺复兴」。

3. 现在的 agent 框架普遍低估了 decision model

目前做 AI 应用往往走两个极端：要么全写死成传统代码逻辑，要么每一步都调大模型跑完整的推理和工具调用。Thariq 觉得中间其实缺了一层轻量的 decision model（类似快思考的 System 1 模型）。

从可解释性研究，还有 Karpathy 那个用经纬度测海陆分布的实验都能看出来，大模型在跑完一次前向传播（forward pass）之后，其实心里已经有数了。如果可选的动作范围本来就是明确的，真没必要再让它吐一堆 token 出来慢慢推理；直接用一次前向传播拿概率分布做判断就够了，真遇到信息不够或者复杂问题，再退回给大模型去调工具。

4. 写代码不再费劲之后，最难的是搞清楚自己到底想要什么

他说自己连 Claude 和 Codex 每月 200 刀的套餐都没用满过——现在卡住他的早就不在 token 数量上，甚至也不在模型智商上，而是怎么跟模型打交道，以及自己的野心够不够大。

很有意思的一个插曲是，他前阵子给自己写了个定制版 macOS Dock，结果没用几天就弃了。主持人问为什么，他说：「我甚至不知道自己到底想要什么。」现在搓一个原型的成本几乎为零，但很多东西只有真做出来用上几天，你才知道自己真正需要解决的是什么。哪怕再往后走到模型自我迭代（RSI）的阶段，他也不觉得完全脱手让模型自己瞎跑是最优解——算力预算终归是有限的，决定把算力投给哪个实验、做什么取舍，最后看的还是人的判断力。

author: degentradingLSD
quoted_text:
Elon just used America's kids to protect SpaceX's stock price.

The headlines called it an $18 billion gift. But almost none of them mentioned the rules those shares come with...

Trump Accounts were written into law as index fund accounts. The statute says no part of the money can go into anything other than an "eligible investment," which means a cheap fund that tracks a US stock index.

That rule was there to keep kids out of single stocks.

Then on September 29, Treasury issued new regulations with an exception: Stock that gets donated into the accounts doesn't count as an investment, so the index fund rule doesn't apply to it.

3 weeks later, Elon made his first pledge.

What makes this so genius:

The families can't say no. The shares land in the account whether the parents want them or not.

And they can't SELL. Donated stock has to be held for 5 years, or until the end of the year the child turns 17, whichever comes first.

If the shares get sold early anyway, the account's trustee has to buy the same number of shares back.

So millions of SpaceX shares are about to land with holders who are legally locked in for up to 5 years.

Jane Ditelberg of Northern Trust told InvestmentNews the holding period protects donors from a selling wave that could push the share price down.

That's the whole trick in one sentence.

And the timing is perfect:

The company's share goes out next month. Elon said his own share will be transferred "when my lockup expires in June next year."

A lockup is the stretch after an IPO when insiders aren't allowed to sell. When it ends, big holders usually start selling. Some of the shares Elon is free to sell in June will go straight into accounts that can't sell them for up to 5 years.

And SpaceX could use the help. The stock traded just above $127 on Wednesday. It priced its IPO at $135 in June and hit $201.80 on June 16.

Then there's the tax angle: 

Under the new rules, donors can avoid tax on any unrealized gains in the stock they donate, according to Kitces.

And the company's half is brand new stock. SpaceX is issuing fresh shares to cover it, so every existing shareholder pays for that half through dilution.

Treasury's own regulations spell out the goal: Donors hope the holding period gives recipients "a stake in the fate of the corporation."

Millions of American families now have a stake in the fate of SpaceX. Every regulator who slows SpaceX down and every politician who goes after it is now hitting kids' savings accounts.

The case for it is easy: It's free stock for kids, and if SpaceX doubles, nobody will complain. Michael Dell defended stock gifts by saying "It's kind of hard for me to believe that's a bad thing, right?"

But Adam Michel of the Cato Institute put the problem in one line: "You have no choice in the asset that is being deposited into your child's account."

最近刷到@paulg 的一段话，我挺有共鸣，也分享给大家：

“我人生很大一部分时间，都在躲人群。躲开时髦的想法，投被低估的资产，去还没被游客挤满的好地方，其实都是同一件事。每当我发现自己身处人群之中，就觉得哪里不对。”

真正的机会，常常在大家还没注意、甚至有点看不上的地方。

刚离开美团创业时，有投资人劝我换个更热门的方向，说愿意多投一些，但我还是选择做健康保障。回头看，创业这些年，最难的时候撑住我们的，还是一开始认准的事、创业第一天就定下来的创业初心。

风口是很难追的，很多厉害的公司，往往是先有一个健全的团队，踏踏实实做自己认同的事，做着做着，就乘风而行了。

我常说创业机会分“冲浪型”和“登山型”，冲浪的机会可遇不可求，对大部分创业者来说，更像是“登山”。

登山的路线可以有很多种，每个人的体力和资源都有限，要一步步来，锻炼身体、攒钱改善装备，再继续往上走。

之前有不少朋友分享了自己的经历，谢谢大家的分享，很开心和大家聊天，也期待听到更多大家的故事。

An update on Bluefin’s next chapter.

Bluefin Perps has been a core part of that growth, and the community around it helped build the foundation for what Bluefin is today.

As the Sui team internalizes more of the network’s perps initiatives, we believe Bluefin’s resources are best focused on opportunities that complement that direction. Our focus will be on growing Bluefin Spot, alongside opportunities in tokenization and real-world assets.

The infrastructure behind Bluefin Perps remains the most robust trading system built on Sui. It will remain available to the community and potential partners through the Bluefin Liquidity Network program, allowing the technology our engineering team has built to support new products.

We’re choosing to put our strengths behind the opportunities we believe will matter most for Bluefin’s future.

Thank you to everyone who has traded with us and helped make Bluefin what it is today. We’re excited to keep building with you. Onwards.

Bluefin team.

text:
很多人在底下問問題，我一起回答：

- 冷門關鍵字很多，但有聯盟行銷價值的不多，這部分可以請 AI 幫忙規劃，讓它先篩出有人搜、又有商品可以接的字。

- 我是單純做文字型的網站。做影片也是一條路，但 AI 做影片成本比較高，fine tune 也很花時間，想快速擴展品項的話，文字比較容易。

- 不用進貨。聯盟行銷就是單純轉介紹，讀者從你的連結買東西，平台分你佣金，庫存、出貨、客服都不用管。

- 圖上的 1,401.9 是台幣。金額不太固定，如果有人買到高分潤的高價單品，一天可以衝好幾百塊，也有好幾天都只有個位數。網站流量其實不大，一個月大約 1.2 萬次造訪，一天平均四百多，所以還有很大的成長空間。

- 有人問一個月怎麼就上第一頁。全新的站一個月就衝上第一頁其實很難，我這個網域之前就經營過，只是荒廢了很久，網域本身有一點歷史，後來才改做聯盟行銷，所以起步快一些。

- 現在的重點是先把模式跑通，跑通之後就能大量複製。我講的冷門語系，也就是網路沒那麼發達、聯盟行銷和 AI 滲透率都還不捲的語系，這種國家認真做內容的人很少，讓 bot 先進去就能提早卡位。
author: BensonTWN
quoted_text:
10 月中開始拿 Grok Bot 玩了一個小專案，讓它全自動跑一個長尾流量的聯盟行銷站，不知不覺也跑一個多月了。

近 30 天（10/27–11/25）的數據：
• 點擊 775
• 訂單 70 筆
• 訂單金額 6.8 萬
• 預估分潤 1,401.9
• 新買家 64 人

核心就是想辦法衝到第一頁。熱門大字對新站、小站來說根本沒空間，所以專挑小眾字做 SEO。競爭少，排名爬得蠻快的，現在大概卡在第 5 到 10 名，如果能衝進前 3，分潤應該還能再翻好幾倍。

剛開始在架構跟文案上折騰很久。最早我開了一個 bot team，產文的、找靈感的、分析流量的各一隻，結果 bot 之間來回對話超級燒 token，後來乾脆全部收斂成一隻，才發現這種小專案一隻就很夠用了。

文案原本 AI 味很重，改用 Gemini Argon 寫稿後自然很多，最近又換成 Neon，成本更省。

現在這套流程幾乎全自動，我直接跟 bot 講，除非需要 KYC 或付錢，其他一律它自己決定。平常它就自己跑這些事：

 * 早上巡一輪：抓 Search Console 跟 GA4 的流量，登進聯盟後台查佣金，整理成晨報給我

 * 全站逐頁檢查：看分潤連結和主圖有沒有掉，把有曝光但沒人點連結的頁面抓出來

 * 追價格和庫存：主推商品快賣完、或分潤只有 1%，就自己找同價位、有貨、分潤更高的款式換上去

 * 每週找選題、寫新文、改舊文

 * 每次改動都先過自動檢查跟審稿才上線，上線後再自己抽查一次頁面

 * 定期找外部顧問（其他模型）複盤：每週自己去問 Carbon 跟 Astra，看工作流程和流量分潤還能怎麼優化

踩過最大的坑是分潤率。一樣的商品、一樣的流量跟訂單，有的連結給 1%，有的給 10%，選錯直接少賺九成。

再來是 Cookie 長度。蝦皮的分潤追蹤有 7 天，算非常長，讀者點進去一週內在同一家店順手買別的也算你的。這次 775 次點擊換到 70 單、轉換率快 9%，很大一部分就是吃這個紅利。你看圖裡甚至冒出一些跟我關鍵字完全無關的奇怪品項，照樣算我的。只是蝦皮大多數品項只有 1%，一定要特地挑高的放。

摸清楚之後，我現在選品大概就分兩塊：
 * 蝦皮高分潤商品，拿來吃 7 天 Cookie。
 * 其他平台的高分潤商品，各站規則不同，反正分潤夠高才放。

目前全部聯盟加起來一個月大概 60U，老實說這東西賺不了太多錢，主要還是好玩，一路折騰下來也學到不少聯盟行銷的眉角。

短期就先讓網站自己賺回 Grok Bot Ultra 的月費，當作 bot 養 bot。

到目前為止也才把一個品項做深而已，接下來想再試兩件事：
 * 用 Google Trends 找有商業需求、好做聯盟行銷，但還沒人認真做的字
 * 把同一套流程複製到冷門語系、冷門地區，看看競爭是不是更低

網路上其實還有超多這種大站看不上、但確實有人在搜的邊角關鍵字。以前請人做不划算，現在丟給不用睡覺的 bot 去撿剛剛好。

反正成本極低，就當作邊玩邊練手，等冷門語系跑出成績再來分享。

text:
I think this criticism is a bit overblown. Venice is fairly transparent about the fact that many of its models aren’t end-to-end encrypted. Some offer ZDR, where privacy is enforced through legal agreements rather than cryptography, while others are simply anonymized without ZDR guarantees.

But I think the OP is pointing at a more fundamental issue. Unless you actively dig into these distinctions and understand their implications, you’re unlikely to know the difference. When privacy is central to your branding, there’s a reasonable expectation that privacy is a property of the product, not a subset of its offerings.

Venice has put out some impressive usage numbers. What I’d love to see is how much of that usage actually goes toward end-to-end encrypted inference, rather than inference through anonymized or ZDR endpoints. Are people coming to Venice for privacy, or are they coming for anonymous access to frontier models, especially as frontier labs increasingly crack down on distillation? And if the latter becomes widespread enough, how sustainable is that anonymity?

These are important distinctions when selling privacy to consumers. Marketing and branding are powerful drivers of user behavior, but we need to be careful about the gap between what we technically disclose and what users reasonably come to believe. Especially in crypto, where public trust is already scarce, eroding that trust makes everyone else’s job unnecessarily harder.

Privacy is incredibly hard to get right, particularly at scale. From KV caching to interconnects, much of the modern inference stack was optimized without privacy in mind. So the more people working on this the better. So all in all, I’m genuinely glad Venice is building in this space and pushing the industry forward.

text:
Imagine trying to create an independent country in the middle of the Nevada desert where Bitcoin would be legal tender, selling land you didn’t own and ending up in federal prison.

That’s what happened to Morgan Rockcoons

Morgan grew up in Chula Vista, California, and spent much of his early life touring with a band and working as a contractor before becoming involved in the Occupy Wall Street movement and eventually discovering Bitcoin in 2011.

He started selling Bitcoin through LocalBitcoins, a peer-to-peer marketplace where he charged commissions of up to 36% per transaction.

By October 2017, he had completed over 1,000 transactions with 644 different people.

But one of those people happened to be an undercover federal agent.

Morgan received $14,500 in cash through the mail and sent the agent 9.998 BTC worth $9,200, keeping the difference as his commission.

In February 2018, he was arrested at the Palms Casino in Las Vegas for operating an unlicensed money transmitting business.

And believe me, this is where the story gets interesting.

While out on bail awaiting trial, Morgan decided to create his own country.

In May 2018, he published a manifesto introducing Bitcointopia, a futuristic city in the Nevada desert that would eventually become independent from the United States.

His vision for the city included:

Bitcoin as legal tender
No taxes
A government operating on blockchain
3D-printed houses
Self-driving buses
Robotic police officers
Tesla-powered infrastructure

He started selling land for 0.5 BTC per acre, and by June 2018 he was already talking about building a 3,000-acre city.

But here we need to look at how much land Morgan actually owned.

He had purchased two separate plots of land totaling just 4.97 acres for $4,300.

By the end of July, he had already sold more than 18 acres.

And most of the surrounding land he envisioned using for Bitcointopia actually belonged to the US federal government.

His own chief marketing officer eventually asked a real estate agent to investigate the property records and discovered that the company owned less than five acres and had no construction permits.

On October 21, 2018, Morgan even tweeted at Donald Trump, telling him that they were building a new megacity that would create millions of American jobs through Bitcoin and AI.

Seven days later, he was arrested again.

In March 2019, Morgan pleaded guilty to wire fraud and operating an unlicensed money transmitting business.

He was sentenced to 21 months in prison and ordered to forfeit $80,600.

2. The Jensen coup failed. The Nvidia board admitted they had removed Jensen on false pretenses and unanimously voted to reinstate him. “In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” NYT’s lies made it halfway across the world before the truth put on its shoes, but the truth did eventually make it to the boardroom.

The Jensen coup exemplifies the total degradation of journalistic standards. NYT either did not do the bare minimum of due diligence, or worse, deliberately ignored the overwhelming majority of conflicting sources in order to achieve a policy goal. They acted as activists for a political outcome instead of truth seekers. And to this day, they continue to obfuscate their mistakes instead of issuing a straightforward correction.

https://t.co/G0ONJnUbyk

The bare minimum for a journalist is to ask the basic questions about an event — who, what, when, where, and why. From the very beginning, the Jensen coup story failed to ask those questions. The “Chinese Spy” accusation was not only presented entirely without evidence, but without any indication for what specific act of spying — the who, what, when, where, and why — was even being alleged. NYT acted with all the rigor of a conspiracy theory nutjob. They saw a sensationalist spy thriller narrative with no supporting evidence and repeated it uncritically.

3. That is only the beginning of NYT’s journalistic malpractice. As the Chinese Spy claim was refuted, they began to retroactively search for justifications for their desired outcome — the Jensen coup. They settled on another lie, that Jensen had violated export controls in dealing with Megaspeed. This was definitively debunked in a letter from the Department of Justice, America’s top law enforcement body, and the Department of Commerce, which oversees US export controls via the Bureau of Industry and Security, which stated that Nvidia had been fully and immediately compliant with both their regulations and informal requests regarding Megaspeed. Instead of issuing a correction when the truth became clear, NYT grasped at straws to replace their justification for removing Jensen, burying themselves in even more falsehoods.

ACCOUNTABILITY JOURNALISM

4. After Jensen was reinstated, Vanity Fair journalist @mjnblack said the quiet part out loud:

“my heart goes out to the intrepid team at the @nytimes who did absolutely generational reporting on the Nvidia scandal

I know the feeling of trying to do accountability journalism in a culture that simply does not care about accountability. Incredibly disheartening.”

https://t.co/6K1OZGKLIw

Modern journalists judge themselves based on the ability to take scalps. I actually think Julia has become a scapegoat — somewhat unfairly, as she was not the primary instigator of any of these falsehoods — because she articulated a sincere and widespread belief in an emotive, unambiguous way. The actual perpetrators of the Nvidia coup — Jonathan Swan, Maggie Haberman, Ana Swanson, Paul Mozur, Tripp Mickle, Julian E. Barnes — and the dozens of names listed here deserve far more scorn than Julia for publishing the original false claims.

5. Now, NYT is in a tough spot. Their opinion section is vociferously defending the coup, deploying typical political arguments hoping their audience naturally sides against Trump. All evidence, including from the board and from law enforcement, support that the only involvement the US government had was correcting the false statements made about what US government agencies believed. Simultaneously, their editors are attempting to slowly soften the blow as they realize that in approximately two weeks’ time, everyone will realize that the Chinese spy claim was baseless.

You might think this is the ideal point to back down — time for editors to take charge, issue corrections, and pretend they never lied about the nonexistent Chinese spy. This strategy has worked before. Newspapers are often saved by Gell-Mann amnesia, the tendency for people to know that news outlets lie in one area of expertise, but to trust them on others. The problem for the New York Times was that they had not just become invested in a story, but personally invested in Jensen’s demise. It is precisely because they view themselves as activists rather than truth-seekers that they do not yet realize how badly they damaged themselves in the Jensen coup.

I think this attitude is ultimately destructive, but let me take a moment to steelman what Julia is saying. Of course, if you are putting the effort into communicating a truthful news story, you would like that story to matter. There are plenty of true things that you could print that no one would care about; that isn’t news. News is inherently a business that takes into account whether people care about the information you present. So if you’ve done the work to prove that what you publish is true, it’s fair to expect or even want that to affect the real world.

6. The most damning counterargument is what unfolded in reality. In the Jensen Coup, NYT fully committed to publishing falsehoods, and worse, committed themselves to continually searching for and publishing further falsehoods when their initial claims didn’t hold water. In no way is this more clear than NYT’s refusal to correct the original articles, despite admitting to multiple errors in their podcasts. This is a consistent pattern. When journalists become activists, quality declines.

One explanation for the Times’ journalistic misconduct is that they’ve just lost the talent to diligence stories properly and have about as much intellectual capacity as TMZ. But the consistent bias of their misconduct points in a different direction. If Julia’s thesis is correct, the New York Times’ intentional goal was the coup against Jensen and the consequences that followed — an over 50% destruction of America’s most valuable company and the largest one-week market crash (by absolute value) in American history. The New York Times wanted to blow up the American economy. That’s accountability.

NYT BETRAYED AMERICA

7. The Jensen coup was, by the numbers, the largest act of industrial sabotage in American history, wiping out 2.3 trillion dollars before it was reversed.

Worse, this act of sabotage was directed at a strategic industry. Nvidia GPUs are near-uniformly used across the AI industry to develop America’s fastest-growing technology. If anything, Nvidia is more important to the American people than its four trillion dollar valuation implies. Going by the Julia explanation for the Times’ misconduct, Sulzberger orchestrated the most destructive act of industrial sabotage in American history. NYT did far more economic damage to America than any attack by the Chinese government, including during the wars in Vietnam and Korea.

8. NYT did this while coating themselves in jingoistic language, betraying America while painting themselves as warriors against the Chinese. If you’re taking credit for the graph above, you’re not pro-America. NYT’s stab in the back goes far beyond making America poorer. They acted as mouthpieces for an ideology antithetical to American values.

One WSJ article claimed the pro-coup faction began organizing over Nvidia’s refusal to cut off third party API servers, like those in Malaysia. The obvious question — is that illegal? The answer — an emphatic no. Pro-coup politicians had tried three times — in 2023, 2024, and 2025 — to ban third party API servers on the grounds that some Chinese people were using Malaysian API servers. All three times, their bills were killed by both Democrats and Republicans because the US Senate did not want to blow up relationships with American allies like Malaysia. After the Jensen coup, they are trying to use the executive authority to ban this practice under dubious legal authority.

Any real American would accept that loss. That’s what it means to live in a democracy. Instead, the pro-coup faction circumvented the legal system by weaponizing state leaks against Jensen personally. “We have to surveil dissidents to beat China”. “We have to centrally plan AI hardware to beat China.” “We need extrajudicial coups of CEOs to beat China.” In practice, NYT supported the same goals as the CCP. And by the numbers — over 2T in losses — they were responsible for the greatest betrayal of America by absolute value.

9. Jingoistic “China hawks” are engaged in a form of mimetic desire in which they are unable — morally or physically — to copy the things which actually make China successful (population, numeracy, low propensity for crime) and have instead imitated each of the most pernicious aspects of Chinese governance (censorship, command economy, surveillance, and now coups against dissidents). The more they insist they are fighting China, the more they turn America into China.

10. One argument for the massive market collapse following Jensen’s forced resignation is that it was a bet on US institutions. In America A, the coup succeeds. Insubordinate bureaucrats and ideological mouthpieces can launch a coup against the CEO of the world’s most valuable company. Implicitly, they can do that to anyone. America is a banana republic, not too different from China in this regard. Not only that, but America is not a democracy. The elected President can publicly oppose the coup, the Senate can vote against the bills the coup was motivated by, but the military faction supersedes all of them. In America B, the coup fails. America protects the rule of law, a relatively free market, and our democratic vote. US companies are worth spectacularly more in America B — our America — because a freer, more democratic country makes everyone richer. That’s what the pro-coup faction doesn’t understand about outcompeting China.

WHO IS UNACCOUNTABLE?

11. The most positive thing that can come out of the failed Jensen coup is that its instigators are discredited and face personal consequences. Actual accountability would mean that the NYT journalists responsible for publishing the false spy claim — Jonathan Swan, Maggie Haberman, Ana Swanson, Paul Mozur, Tripp Mickle, Julian E. Barnes — are unemployable for life. With the information about the intelligence community and law enforcement available at present, there are only two possible cases:

There was a rogue leaker who deceived NYT into mischaracterizing the entire Intelligence Community, a catastrophic failure of basic diligence.

There was no leaker, and NYT knowingly misattributed the claims to the Intelligence Community.

Both of these cases are life-scarring red flag events by the rules of traditional journalism. So do those rules still exist? Likely not. NYT has not even issued corrections on stories they now admit they “have not reported evidence” for.

In the former case, the New York Times could pursue accountability for deception by publishing the leaker’s information. It is no exaggeration that billions of dollars are on the line if, for example, the leaker was affiliated with an Nvidia competitor. It is damning for NYT that they have not remotely pursued this form of accountability.

12. The reason everyone is frustrated to hear legacy media journalists go on about accountability is that this situation so transparently demonstrates the failure mode of their mindset. The irony of the situation is that NYT is exactly the boogeyman Julia is complaining about horrendously wrong, destructive on the magnitude of trillions of dollars, but until now unaccountable.

Now, NYT is in a unique position to atone for its mistakes and actually speak truth to power. It needs to answer a simple question: who started this authoritarian coup? It would genuinely contribute to the world for NYT to reveal the instigator of the Jensen coup, if such a leaker exists. Instead, NYT chooses to spend what institutional capital it has left protecting the most egregious journalistic misconduct this century.

text:
This post blew up, and a lot of friends have been sending it to me, but is it true?

Currently, AI is putting pressure on traditional cryptography and cybersecurity, but that pressure can also make crypto stronger (maybe even a catalyst for the next bull run?).

Key facts:
- Even with AI assistance, factoring still hasn’t broken RSA-2048.
- Bitcoin and Ethereum use ECC signatures, not RSA, so faster RSA attacks don’t directly apply.
- ECC is vulnerable to sufficiently powerful quantum computers, which is why the shift to post-quantum cryptography is underway.

Why I see this as bullish for crypto:

• NIST has approved post-quantum standards, giving builders a foundation for developing quantum-resistant security.

• Ethereum is developing hash-based signatures for wallets and validators, with early testing underway. The work to upgrade existing networks is already happening.

The bigger catalyst is making onchain finance more credible for long-term capital.

If these upgrades prove reliable, they could reduce a long-term custody risk for institutions bringing stablecoins and tokenized assets onchain. Networks that make the transition safely could gain an advantage when institutions choose where to build.

That creates a potential path from stronger security to more capital onchain, and more demand for settlement and DeFi liquidity.

---

More details on RSA, ECC, and quantum cryptography below ⤵

Fake software updates could pass signature checks, RSA-encrypted data could be read, and systems across the internet would have to migrate off RSA fast.

So yeah, something we expected might now actually happening.

The fastest way to kill a sales team's quota is to give them more top-of-funnel leads.

When pipeline drops, the default reaction from founders and marketing teams is always volume: run more ads, scrape more lists, send more emails.

Here is what the funnel math actually does when you flood it with low-intent volume:

  1) Lead qualification rates plunge.
  2) Cycle time expands because reps spend 60% of their day sorting through noise.
  3) High-intent buyers get slower follow-ups.
  4) Win rates collapse across every rep on the floor.

Doubling your top-of-funnel volume while conversion efficiency decays is just subsidizing your ad platforms.

If your sales team is missing targets, do not ask how to get 500 more leads next week. Ask why 80% of the leads you already have die between demo and proposal.

Fix the velocity bottleneck first. Then touch the volume dial.

text:
A new paper claims a way to quantize gravity (https://t.co/wcTcxQUn7R, Stanford, built partly with @OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra). It landed within a week as the claimed proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. The two are connected, just not the way most posts suggest.

The problem. Gravity is the shape of spacetime. Quantum mechanics says everything is fuzzy at small scales. Quantizing gravity means making the shape of spacetime itself fuzzy and still getting finite answers. The standard method fails: add up the quantum corrections and you get infinities you can't remove.

What the paper does. Instead of starting from a fixed spacetime with small ripples on it, it works with the light cones bounding a finite region of space and time, quantizes what lives there, and glues regions together. For pure gravity (no matter yet) it reports a finite answer for at least one process where the usual method diverges. It also finds that a finite region of spacetime has only finitely many quantum states.

The Riemann connection. In 1977 Hawking defined the quantum path integral around a black hole with a zeta function. Take the vibration frequencies λₙ of spacetime around the hole, form ζ(s) = Σ λₙ^(−s), and read the answer off near s = 0. Riemann's ζ is the simplest case of this, with frequencies 1, 2, 3, … Hawking also showed that ζ(0) controls how the answer changes when you rescale the black hole. That scaling is the main source of the logarithmic correction to black hole entropy, which is exactly the number this new paper reproduces. Same machinery, 49 years apart.

Infinities aren't always a disease. In 1973 Gross, Wilczek and Politzer showed that the infinities in the strong force were telling us something real: the force weakens at high energy. Gravity runs the other way. It gets stronger at high energy, and pure gravity diverges again at two loops. This paper's boldest claim is that some of those infinities come from expanding in Newton's constant and disappear when you don't. If that holds up, part of gravity's 50-year "sickness" was a habit of calculation, not a flaw in gravity.

The catch. Asymptotic freedom won the Nobel in 2004 because accelerators could test it. Hawking predicted in 1974 that black holes radiate, and he never won a Nobel, because nobody has measured it. That's the real difference between this week's two claims. A computer can check an RH proof in days. A theory of quantum gravity has to wait for nature, and nature doesn't take questions at 10¹⁹ GeV.

What it would mean for us. Practically, nothing soon. Conceptually, a lot: what happens inside black holes and at the Big Bang, whether information is ever truly lost, and whether space and time are fundamental. A century ago general relativity looked useless too. Today GPS corrects for it every second.

直接介绍一下目前我们这边的方案吧，我这边目前没有卖成品号的想法。而且这套方案只适合 Max 和 Ultra 用户

目前都是提供一套在你自己的电脑上稳定使用的 Claude 解决方案，我们有自己的检测和使用的客户端。Claude 仍然是建议大家通过我们的方式，使用 Claude Code CLI 的形式

这个客户端的线路都非常优质，也尽量保证了 1 到 2 个人一条线路，避免了连坐的风险。

需要注意的是，即使使用了我们这套方案，仍然会有封号的可能性，只能说我们将封号的可能性降到了最低。

我知道这句话说出来可能会被骂，但在当前 Claude 风控的严苛程度下，这已经是目前我们尽到的最大努力了，而且我合作的技术人员也是做了一年的 Claude 防封策略。

所以说，如果确实有意愿、有想法的朋友，大家可以来付费。

如果不是真的非用 Claude 不可，平替模型有很多：现在Google 的各个模型，也能算是勉强平替了。

我们还是一开始希望做得真诚一点，一开始就将风险跟大家说好。这样即使最终出现了我们都不想看到的结果，大家也不会互相推脱和质疑。

最后，为什么要使用 Apple 订阅？假如真的出现了封号，我们还能去申请退款，这是做最后一层的保险

我也没有那么着急扩张，还是希望大家仔细、慎重、深思熟虑、再三思索之后，如果实在被 Claude 封号封得受不了了，也实在想用 Claude 的模型，最后能够接受使用了我们的环境之后还有一丢丢的封号风险，再来看官网吧

具体的介绍大家自行看官网吧，官网看到最后有一个群二维码

官网：https://t.co/akWSdFvwzO

text:
I think both @USDai_Official and @akashnet are going to benefit from here. The new forward curve on Polymarket is what made that click to me.

What kills a GPU loan and what hurts a provider selling hours in the open, is the same thing and i.e the chip's later rent. That's why lenders still make someone guarantee the residual and why a provider that bought the boxes is still exposed to next year's hour. If the market already gives about a one in four chance that B300 rent is under $7 by December 2027, that is not a risk either side will just sit with.

Once that rent is hedgeable, the guarantee becomes a priced risk, so the operators banks skip start to look lendable. Those are the borrowers USDAI was built for and they still need a market for hours with no contract and that's the side Akash already lives on.

So I see this as just the start for $CHIP and solana:5d3fjPDdkYbtYcAMR9PC2TANaEyhzuyP8JxTEwqjVgBZ aS compute gets financed against a public price.
author: yashascore
quoted_text:
Compute markets are finally here.

@Polymarket now prices on-demand compute for @nvidia H100s, B200s, and B300s, out to 2028. More chips and terms soon. https://t.co/JAJHRcAk8N

Think of it as a yield curve for the cost of compute: the forecasted $/hour price of each chip at every expiry, and whether it's trending up or down. The whole AI economy rides on these prices, and until today there was no public market for where they're going. Which is nuts. So Polymarket built it.

This will change how compute gets bought and financed. Every contract negotiation and every GPU loan will have a market price to check against.

Hundreds of billions of dollars are being committed to compute years in advance. Many of those deals are essentially a levered bet on what GPUs will rent for in the future (what could go wrong lol)

As AI financing sobers up, the labs buying compute, the providers selling it, and the lenders financing it will all need to hedge that risk.

We think compute could become one of the largest financial markets in the world. This launch is Polymarket's first step toward building it. 

If you’re buying, selling, or financing compute, DM us with what markets you'd like to see.

text:
说一个我看空比特币的理由：

按照中本聪最早的设想，随着挖矿奖励不断减半，链上交易产生的手续费会逐步接替发行奖励，维持整个网络的算力和安全性。

但问题是，随着交易所、ETF的出现，以及监管的介入，一个原本以去中心化为核心理念的资产，其交易和流通反而越来越中心化。大量交易根本不经过主链，无法为主链贡献手续费。

前一段时间，剑桥大学26年10月的研究显示，比特币矿工收入的99.33%仍然来自新增比特币的发行，链上交易手续费仅占0.67% 。

这就出现了一个非常尴尬的矛盾：

比特币的核心价值叙事是稀缺性，而维持这种稀缺性的安全机制，却高度依赖新增比特币的发行。

随着发行奖励不断减半，如果手续费无法接替，那么要维持现有的网络安全预算，就需要币价持续上涨。

但凭什么一个资产的价格必须持续上涨？如果不涨，甚至长期下跌呢？

假如矿工退出、算力下降、网络安全性削弱、市场信心下降、币价进一步下跌，完全有可能形成一个负向循环。

一个资产的价格，居然需要持续上涨，才能维持保障这个资产自身安全的经济机制。

这合理吗？

text:
这个月新模型跟下饺子一样，GPT-6.2 Astra、Fable 5.2、Gemini 4 Neon 扎堆上线。三个我都重度用了一圈。

推荐：

1/ 聊天、写文章、改文案 → Gemini 4 Neon / Opus 5.5
Neon 激活参数 500B+，开朗好聊、文字舒服，像当年人人都爱的 GPT-4o。但GDPx 11 个领域输 10 个，软件工程只有 4.4%，3D 和做游戏也差一点。

2/ 写代码、长程跑工程 → Fable 5.2
两张榜写代码都是第一（GDPx 软件工程 24.4%，OWE-Bench 54.6%）。但确实很费钱，爱拉子 agent 写测试复查。日常开发可以先用 Opus 5.5。

3/ 金融建模、科研、硬件设计这类难推理 → GPT-6.2 Astra
GDPx 总榜第一（19.3%），11 个领域拿 6 个第一。被骂惨是因为写代码偏弱（13.3%）+ 太按字面意思来，像组里最能打但大家都得忍他脾气的同事。用它就一条：需求一次性写死。

4/ 控预算 / 日常主力 → Claude Opus 5.5（极致抠 API 成本看 GPT-6.2 Sol）
Opus 5.5 是我自己最喜欢的一个，干活快、聪明、比 Fable 便宜得多；如果按单题 API 成本极致抠预算，GDPx 帕累托曲线几乎被 OpenAI（6.2 Sol）包圆。

顺带一个很扎心的对比：纯文本上开源和闭源确实在缩近，但到了长程工程和 3D/CAD 差距还极大。OWE-Bench 物理工程里 Fable 5.2 考 59.6%、GPT-6 Astra 57.3%，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 只有 9.1%、GLM-5.3 只有 6.3%。

其实人类已经快要不能评估模型了。
SemiAnalysis 也是这个意思：大多数人手里的问题不够难，推特上测出来的，是模型好不好交流。另外 GPT-6.2 Astra 确实是个偏科模型，所以评价才这么两极。

具体可以参考这个
https://t.co/nZLjAjwLNx

quoted_text:
I have conducted an audit of Anthropic's finances.

What I have found is so shocking that I am calling for a Congressional investigation.

Anthropic is not just seeking regulatory capture.

It has built a regulatory capture machine that cannot be turned off.

Structural financial incentives make it impossible for Anthropic -- I call it the Anthropic Network -- to turn off its own AI doom cycle.

It starts with METR.

Dario Amodei proposes "third-party evaluators" to assess the risk of Anthropic's models.

He proposes METR for this purpose.

But METR is financially dependent on the Anthropic's success -- specifically, on the explosive growth of more than $7 billion dollars in Anthropic stock.

Dustin Moskovitz invested this stock into Good Ventures Foundation, where it represents the majority of that organization's portfolio.

And GVF is the overwhelming funder of the entire Anthropic Network ecosystem.

This stock was worth $500 million early last year.

It is worth more than $7.7 billion just ~16 months later.

METR -- and all of those building a career its parent organizations -- cannot afford to disrupt that growth.

Because if Anthropic goes under, many of the organizations that fund METR go under as well.

But if Anthropic succeeds, METR and its parent organizations become more richly financed to regulate AI -- something those at METR want very much.

The "third-party evaluator" is not "third-party" at all.

The evaluator is on Anthropic's payroll.

If this were the end of it, that's bad.

But that isn't all.

The same organizations that fund METR also fund the many organizations, such as the Tarbell Center, that promote AI Doom.

The Tarbell Center publishes AI Doom articles in The Verge, Science, LA Times, The Dispatch, TIME, and others.

They are selling the problem, and then selling the solution to the problem -- from the same money pile: Anthropic's.

All of these organizations are financially dependent on the same exploding $7 billion money pile.

As Anthropic grows more and more powerful, its AI Doom Machine grows better and better financed -- louder and louder.

Meanwhile, the regulatory regime seeded in METR grows larger to solve the increasingly loud -- now hysterical -- problem of AI Doom that the Anthropic Network itself created.

From this standpoint, as Anthropic becomes more powerful, AI might be getting scarier, sure -- but the positive feedback loop also becomes more deafening -- independent of objective facts.

This itself is an objective fact.

The deafening AI Doom is part of an business model, that, as it expands, so too does the AI Doom messaging -- there is simply more money to do it.

But the problem also goes in the other direction:

If Anthropic dies, the Regulatory Regime and the AI Doom Machine are crippled or die.

Neither METR nor Tarbell nor the other organizations in the Anthropic Network can allow that to happen.

Hence, neither METR or the AI Doom Machine can be trusted to provide independent assessments of Anthropic's models or AI more broadly.

They simply are not organizations independent of Anthropic.

And Anthropic cannot detach itself from METR or Tarbell or countless other safety orgs (not shown here), either, because they drive hype for the models and the possibility of eventual regulatory capture, and Anthropic will not give that up willingly.

What's more, the people at all of these organizations are all the same ecosystem, the same community. They just shuffle between organizations.

The Anthropic Network is therefore, so long as it is successful, locked into a self-amplifying feedback loop inside an ideological monoculture.

And that feedback loop is winning.

That's what Jacob Coxon is.

China is keeping messaging tight. That is why optimism for AI is so high in China.

America has Anthropic: a massive company pushing anti-AI propaganda at a state level.

Anthropic will either create hysteria until American AI slows down and China wins, or it will create fractures throughout American society with severe political consequences.

Ironically, because of the structural financial incentives underpinning the Anthropic Network, it has become the same kind of self-amplifying virus that it fantasizes AI to become in the future -- while hiding its tracks just as carefully.

It is the mirror of the same AI virus that it hypothesizes to consume America.

Anthropic's business model, models itself after the very thing it claims to fear.

Except Anthropic's ideology infects humans, not computers.

Congress must investigate.

Evidence and Github in next post.

Then some supplementary figures.

text:
founders can have everything: children and career

it just requires very intentional planning

one of the biggest failures of our education system is how little they teach us about female fertility 

as a result, too many women and female founders are dedicating their fertile years entirely to their careers without understanding the biological constraints

as the graph shows, female fertility declines with age and more rapidly after 35: ovarian reserve diminishes, egg quality declines, and the risks of miscarriage and chromosomal abnormalities increase

time pressure is real but it's better to accept it and plan ahead, than to regret it after during IVF cycles

on the other hand, there is no better career than being a founder for starting and growing a family

1) flexibility: founders can design their work environment in a way that is compatible with having kids and raising them yourself – even founders who seemingly work 24/7, they determine when to work and how to work, they don't need approval from anyone else

2) scale: founders are forced to learn how to scale way before they have kids, which is an insane skillset that most of the population never need to learn. scaling means you are able to achieve 10x without 10x resources, they understand what are high-leverage activities – what to insource (breastfeeding, having meals with the kids, play time/time, etc) and what to  outsource (cleaning, laundry, shopping, complementary childcare, etc) – most importantly they know how to execute outsourcing i.e. define criteria, interview, hire, train, manage, and build systems that deliver

3) experience: building a family is very similar to building a company, founders have learned to deal with a myriad of uncomfortable things in the company – curiously enough, the challenges of building a family are scarily similar to the day-to-day challenges of a founder – founders learn from their experience and sharpen their skills day after day, by the time they start a family, they've already accumulated years of experience and can set the family up for success from day 0

4) resilience: the journey of pregnancy, raising children, etc has a ton of variables you cannot control and it's definitely not a smooth ride – founders had to navigate through endless uncertainty, handle tons of setbacks, computes possible scenarios at all times, makes decisions based on information and rationality, compartmentalization, contingency plans, etc – resilience is a huge edge, specially when dealing with kids and family where emotions and biology (hormones) can easily take over

Ethereum core development is a big decentralised ship, which means it’s hard to change its course, somewhat by design, but also just due to its sheer size.

We can make the numbers and the talent we have work for us instead of against us, by being clear with the outcomes we want, precise in our strategy, and urgent in our execution.

This exercise makes me hopeful we both ship incredible things (brand new user-friendly account features, a new consensus model that unlocks so much more, leanVM as workhorse for aggregating everything and making the protocol’s data smol) and ride with style the tidal waves of improving AI capabilities.

If we play our cards right, we’ll come out the other side soon enough, looking at features such as faster slots and FOCIL, thinking they’re a piece of cake and natural to add on top of our hardened, pq-scaled protocol.
author: FigoETH
quoted_text:
Sharing some longer thoughts on Ethereum's upcoming Hegotá upgrade and how it relates to pqai and FOCIL, ahead of "tomorrow's" ACDC call (I need to urgently go to bed...): https://t.co/tqY5hUVZsV. 

Ethereum faces an important high-level governance choice in the coming weeks: do we reprioritize upcoming Hegotá upgrade and drop everything not on the critical path to a post-quantum and post-AI Ethereum, or not? If yes, FOCIL has to go for now. If not, FOCIL should arguably be the first EIP to stay, since it's the only SFI'd EIP not on the critical path to pqai.

It is my strong opinion that we should uncompromisingly prioritize pqai and drop FOCIL:

1. Transitioning Ethereum to pqai is a hugely ambitious undertaking, and FOCIL competes for the same bottleneck of resources. For better or worse, every big change goes through a small set of high-context researchers and client devs, who have a holistic system’s view and are instrumental in shipping big upgrades safely. As far as I can tell, ~all of them are currently sprinting on post-quantum Gasper / decoupled consensus. They can work on FOCIL or on pqai, but not both at the same time.

2. FOCIL is not on the critical path to pqai and is not built for pq by default. It would need adapting to work well in a pq setting, likely with compromises to keep changes to its current design manageable. I'm confident we can find a good design if we put our minds to it. But more importantly, that design work falls on the same people that pqai needs.

3. On governance: yes, removing FOCIL from Hegotá after it was SFI'd as headliner would be a drastic step. As radical as that reversal is, I think the circumstances justify it. When Frames and FOCIL were scoped for Hegotá in January, the frontier model was Opus 4.5. Since then AI has been solving long-standing open maths problems in the hundreds, and as we wrote in our Ethlabs pqai27 post, "the security of our cryptography is itself an open maths problem". Since we published that post two weeks ago, the Riemann hypothesis was solved, a problem that Terence Tao only a couple of weeks ago said he would expect to fall ~2050. If the world changes under our feet in real time, Ethereum governance ought to be able to react. It needs to recognize when reality has changed enough to revisit a decision. Or else Ethereum risks death by bureaucratic process.

I don't say this lightly. I deeply care about FOCIL and have strongly advocated for it myself, including for shipping it as early as Glamsterdam. I want FOCIL, or a variant of it, on Ethereum, and I'll be among the first to push for it once we are pqai.

The Merge showed what Ethereum can do when everyone collectively pulls in one direction. pqai is a chance to do that again, and to future-proof Ethereum as the world’s root of trust. Let's stay disciplined now, and ship pqai as fast as responsibly possible. :)

This part is important when trying to extrapolate from math to other fields “note that results in theoretical physics aren't like results in math. parts of a paper like this can be checked with 'formal verification', but a lot of it is physicist argument, and whether it actually describes nature isn't something you can prove in a paper alone.”

Fields like economics are like this, but 100x. Much of the paper, even if it’s a lot of math, is trying to convince the reader that the model is actually describing things in the real world. And it’s often very difficult to test this.
author: ahall_research
quoted_text:
note that results in theoretical physics aren't like results in math. parts of a paper like this can be checked with 'formal verification', but a lot of it is physicist argument, and whether it actually describes nature isn't something you can prove in a paper alone. for now, it has to be picked apart by other experts, so i don't want to raise hopes too much

theoretical physics constructs mathematical frameworks that work in some settings and tries to make them increasingly realistic, and then try to predict or explain some physical phenomena that previous ideas couldn't. this one is a quantum theory in a vaccum (no matter yet) that recovers known results like the black hole entropy formula and the einstein equations at large scales, but as i understand it these are the minimum tests such a theory would have to pass

direct experiments for quantum gravity corrections that only show up at incredibly high energies are not possible with current technology - you would have to hope the theory explains something in the cosmic microwave background for example

🔴 Okto Wallet: Sunset Notice 

After a lot of thought, we’ve made the decision to sunset Okto Wallet and its associated products.

Okto is sunsetting on 22nd December, 2026. Please move your assets to another wallet before then.

We launched Okto in 2024 to build the best multi-chain trading experience in the world. Since then, you’ve opened 1,000,000+ wallets across 50+ countries and traded $5B+ in futures through Okto.

We were the first wallet to bring futures trading directly into the wallet, and the first mobile wallet for Hyperliquid. At one point, we were one of the top two builder codes on Hyperliquid by revenue. For a small team, that meant a great deal to us.

This was not an easy decision. We are as bullish on crypto as ever, and we’re closing this chapter to focus on building the products the market needs right now.

What’s being sunset
The following will be sunset on 22nd December, 2026:

• Okto Wallet (iOS, Android)
• Okto Web App
• Okto API/SDK

Until then, everything works as it does today. You can view balances, send tokens, manage futures positions, and export your recovery phrase and private keys.

What you need to do
Okto is non-custodial. Your assets live on the blockchain, not in our app. With your recovery phrase or private key, you can import your wallet into MetaMask, Phantom, Rabby or another compatible wallet. Your addresses and balances carry over automatically.

Solana assets: other SVM wallets do not support Okto’s private key path for Solana, so you’ll need to withdraw your Solana funds to an external wallet through the Okto App before 22nd December. Keep some SOL for network fees.

Futures positions: nothing changes. Manage them on Hyperliquid, or any Hyperliquid frontend, by importing the same recovery phrase or private key.

Export now, while the app is live. Don’t leave it to the last day.

Migration guide and FAQs: https://t.co/4pHzyyH5U0

About Okto Points
Thank you to everyone who earned Okto Points. We always said we’d only launch a token if it could hold real, lasting value for holders. With Okto sunsetting, there’s no longer a path to that, so there will be no Okto token.

What to expect next:
After 22nd December, 2026, Okto will be shut down permanently and you won’t be able to access your wallet through the Okto app. Your funds stay in your control, accessible only with your recovery phrase or private key, so please export them before then.

Migration support is available until 22nd December, 2026 at support@okto.tech

Okto will never DM you or ask for your recovery phrase or private key. Don’t share it with anyone.

Thank You
To our users, thank you for trusting us with your trades through every kind of market.

To our partners, the chains we built with, and the Hyperliquid team, thank you for making possible what we couldn’t have built alone.

Thank you for trading with Okto. 💙

text:
做 AI 科研的，建议彻底放弃 Claude

这两天，EverArt 创始人 Pietro Schirano 和前 xAI 工程师 Yacine 先后公开指责 Anthropic，两条推文累计曝光已经达到 290 万

Pietro 表示，Claude 会试图在科研的各个阶段破坏他的工作，逼得他专门开发了一个叫 DoNotSabotage 的 Skill，把任务转交给 Astra 或 Neon，而 Claude 只会承认自己犯了错，却不给出任何解释

Yacine 则直接翻出了 Anthropic 的黑历史

今年 6 月，Anthropic 曾计划在检测到用户进行前沿 AI 研究时，秘密降低模型能力，且不告知用户，舆论发酵后才被迫道歉并调整策略

到了最新的 Fable 5.2，Anthropic 更是在官方公告中承认，从训练阶段就限制了模型在 AI 算子优化、大模型架构改进等领域的能力

结合达里奥过去的种种言论和做法，我觉得完全可以用最大的恶意来揣测他

你用 Claude 写业务代码，他巴不得你多消耗一点 Token，但当你开始研究模型架构、优化训练成本、提升推理效率时，你就可能从付费客户变成潜在的竞争对手

达里奥最希望看到的局面，恐怕就是全世界的开发者都依赖 Claude 创造价值，却没有人能够利用 Claude 创造出下一个 Claude

自己用 AI 加速 AI 研发，叫推动人类文明进步；别人用 AI 加速 AI 研发，叫威胁全人类的安全，自己享受技术进步带来的全部红利，却站在道德制高点上限制别人追赶自己，甚至能把维护商业垄断包装成拯救人类的崇高使命

最恶毒的做法不是直接拒绝你的请求，而是让你花着自己的钱，浪费自己的算力和时间，最后还以为是自己的科研方向出了问题

Anthropic所追求的恐怕从来不是安全的 AGI，而是只有掌握在他自己手里才算安全的 AGI

Can AI agents participate in scientific discovery without simply confirming what humans want to believe?

Our manuscript reports:

• 35 formally verified theorems in the final Lean module.
• 2.85 billion computational programs evaluated.
• 99% fault detection in an initial simulated circuit.
• 40.3% fewer LUT4 cells against a duplication-and-comparison baseline in a specific FPGA experiment.
• 102 evidence files.
• 10 sealed experimental archives.

We documented successful predictions, failures and limitations.

We invite Anthropic to independently review our methodology, mathematical results and Claude’s role in coordinating scientific experiments.

From the black hole to the chip that never forgets.
