text:
币安今晚把新 L1 的 litepaper 放出来了，先把最大的误解摁下去，这不是来替换 BNB Smart Chain 的，原生代币还是 $BNB ，也不会再单独发一个新币。

1️⃣ 专门给高频、支付和 Agent 开的

这条新链是跟 BSC 并行开发的，BSC 继续做生态底座，新 L1 冲的是高频交易、支付、隐私资金和自主 AI Agent 这几类场景。公开测试网还在推进，现在先把架构摊开给开发者和社区看，别把它理解成主链要换了。

2️⃣ 单子能提前看到排到哪，支付还留了车道

交易会先以 SubBlocks 的形式往外推，应用能提前看到自己大概排在哪，但这只是临时信号，随时可能撤回，并不等于已经成交，更不是最终确认。排序和执行还拆成两条时间线，一边能继续排新块，一边处理前面的块。支付这类场景还能预留一部分区块容量，别的高峰挤不走这份额，没用完的再还给普通流量，忙的时候不至于所有场景挤在一起抢。

3️⃣ 权限、手续费和隐私直接写进协议

账户抽象是原生的，可以用通行密钥登录，多笔操作打成一笔，还能给 Agent 设好权限、随时收回。应用可以代付手续费，用户不一定要先备 $BNB 才能上手，支持的地方可以由代付方用稳定币报价，底层还是用 $BNB 把网络费付掉。隐私这边支持 $BNB 和准入的 BEP-20 做屏蔽结算，通过 AtomicCall 还能用屏蔽资产去做一些公开操作，比如支持的兑换，不过公开调用和部分结算细节仍会露出来，不是全部交互都能这样走。并行 EVM 还在规划里，用可信执行环境做受保护排序目前也只是提案，还没到能当已上线功能来写的地步。

公开测试网还没到，这份文件更像是先把方向钉死，高频、支付和 Agent 要是真按这个架构做出来， $BNB 在新链上的位置会比再发一个币清楚得多😼

然后玩游戏王的时候是在 Steam 上，应该是花钱最多的了，但可惜的是玩的有些疲劳了，而且新作出来以后老卡就不能用了，这也是我第一次有感觉区块链+卡牌游戏是有机会的时候。

到了前年因为是和花栗鼠一起玩，就玩了手机版的宝可梦，在我退坑前一直保持着全卡档，但手机版虽然说卡是可以一直保留的，但并没有交易的功能，最多就是交换，这也让收集少了一些乐趣。

现在在 @TrustWallet 上看到了集成了拆卡和交易为一体的应用，我觉得链上的 TGA 时间应该快到了，在链上既能保证卡的确权，又能通过链把卡加入到自己的卡池，而游戏本身并不复杂，这样一款链游版的 TCG 就没问题了，而且已经和现实卡非常靠近了，既可以玩，也可以收集，还可以交易。

虽然我觉得 GameFi 的赛道就是伪需求，但 Onchian 的 TCG 一定会有火爆的一天。有感兴趣的小伙伴可以来Trust Wallet试试体验下。

Happy Thanksgiving from OmenX.

Looking back at our journey on Base this year, we’re grateful for the support from the Base team every step of the way.

In May we launched on @base mainnet and kept our heads down building, hoping our product and traction would eventually earn the team’s attention.

Three months in, riding the @FIFAWorldCup wave on Base’s high-speed, low-cost infrastructure and its strong user community, we crossed 1b in trading volume.

In July we met the Base engineering team in SF (@dmericliu) and got a much clearer picture of the infrastructure and how we could better plug into the ecosystem.

Around the same time we spoke with @davidtsocy and @BronheimDaniel, who walked us through how the Base Eco Fund works and continued supporting us afterward.

In August, thanks to the invite from @Nibel_eth, @donofbase, and @baseapac, we joined the Base Acceleration Program. The support on fundraising and product building during that period made a real difference.

In October we met @jessepollak at a founders meeting during Token2049 and saw firsthand how keen he and the Base team are to gather ecosystem feedback and help builders grow on Base.

Five months after launch we ranked top 3 on @DefiLlama by 24h trading volume.

In November we closed a $2M round in a tough market.

Thank you to @base and the entire Base team for believing in us and supporting us along the way.

Wishing everyone a happy Thanksgiving and a strong year ahead.

29 November: XTEN distribution starts.

text:
Crypto sentiment is about as bad as I can remember jusdging by how much off ramping and quitting I've seen, even amongst close multi cycle friends (I still suspect they will return once better conditions appear). 

FTX was a major CEX going down, which was terrible, but crypto has always recovered from exchanges going down, and many smart people I knew felt the same. 

Covid crash was 0-1 correlation event for everything, which wasn't crypto specific, so it only took a few days for a lot of people to realise, "oh this is probably a good buy" + we had so much tech still to look forward to at that point, as crypto hadn't shipped anything but whitepapers. 

This moment has nasty everything can break type overhang (AI + quantum) + the ghosts of all the past failures and how much stuff hasn't come to fruition. However, it is always very bleak cyclically at this exact quarter every four years. Maybe it is a tad more bleak because we have broken the spirit of so many individuals that believed crypto would become more than fintech, alongside horrible security risk that feels more intense than ever before. I have acted myself on those security fears, so I'm not going to pretend it hasn't affected me. 

The overhang we have here isn't the easiest to move past, like FTX and covid was. 

My base expectation is that 2027 acts similar to 2019 where nothing really happens, more people quit, and AI keeps progressing, but by the end of the year gets to the point where suddenly people look at the crypto protocols that survived and say "oh, this stuff is actually pretty secure". Maybe some new security standards appear, some joint efforts, who knows. 

At the same time from a macro point of view by the middle of 2027 we are past the hiking cycle, and will have more supportive liquidity regime, and all of the bearish crypto narratives will start to melt away as prices recover, and those bearish narratives may eventually become strengths by eoy. 

The bottom will be in well before this. Latest probably January, which would probably fuck the most people up, due to it being later than anticipated. Prices remain good here if you look ahead 6-12 months, but can get really good in the next 6 weeks possibly. I am watching gold for a clearer signal of a bottom, as it likely bottoms first. 

The stock market can only go down so much before you get the reactive function of the Fed. I remain in the camp that true market crashes are no longer tolerated, and the tools that exist to stop that will be deployed. 

Now, prices won't recover for many things (they never do, dispersion will be even bigger), but we will have good returns for the protocols that generate revenue, and Bitcoin will inflect with liquidity (tbc if that inflection is stronger or weaker than previous cycles). Theoretically, liquidity could be a lot better this cycle as the AI buildout is not allowed to fail, and that will be propped up, and needs to be propped up as it is highly unlikely the numbers are going to make sense and meet the lofty expectations in the short term. 

Don't be bullish on dumb crypto stuff. Crypto is not the frontier it once was, but tokenization and better financial rails are real, and that will continue to be a driver of volumes, fees and onboarding (tradfi) for the next few years. 

There will always be a base level of demand for non sovereign assets, which will be dialed up and down based on liquidity, so don't succumb to the Bitcoin is dead forever bottom of the bear market type fud for the nth time. 

I would still keep an eye on the intersection of AI and crypto, as my gut still says that is where something meaningful/interesting happens/continues to happen going forward.

Due to how many assets are going to be available onchain, it makes sense to widen your horizons and upskill yourself using what you have learned from crypto as a jumping off point rather than a "I think I know how to trade all markets" type arrogance. Use this time now to explore other asset classes, and assets you may be interested in. 

Be patient, you have time. There will be signals when we are more likely entering a risk on market regime again.

BREAKING: US new home sales jumped +14.2% MoM in October, to an annualized rate of 701,000 units, the highest since December 2025, crushing expectations of a -3.8% decline.

This marks the largest monthly increase since November 2025 and the 2nd-largest since August 2022.

It also marks a sharp recovery from the -9.7% MoM decline in September.

October's surge was driven by sales in the South, the nation's largest home-selling region, which soared +36.2% MoM, to an annualized rate of 515,000 units, the highest since March 2021.

At the same time, the median new home sale price fell -0.3% MoM and -3.2% YoY, to $391,300, the 2nd-lowest reading since July 2021.

Since the October 2022 peak, the median new home sale price has declined by $69,000, or -15.0%.

New home prices are falling sharply.

text:
.@Pumpfun is adding a fee to the first block of every new token launch.

But does this solve the biggest problem with launching tokens via a launchpad?

tl;dr (Dec 4):
• Extra wallets buying or selling in the launch block pay a fee
• The creator’s own wallet is exempt
• The fee rate is still unannounced

Simply put, Pumpfun wants to extract more fees from snipers and early bundlers. Everything else is unchanged. If anything, this just makes the process more expensive.

It doesn't stop them.

Developers can pay the fee, buy through their exempt wallet, or simply wait for the next block. If buying shifts to the next block, fast bots may actually get a better shot at getting in ahead of everyone else.

If that’s unhinged, let’s look at the numbers showing how profitable the bundling business is.

Bitquery studied 8.2M launches (Oct 2025–Oct 2026):

• 38% had another wallet buying in the first-trade block
• 65% saw the developer start selling within one minute
• In the profit sample ending June 30, developers and their identified bundles made $579M+ vs. $31.5M for sniper bots

So yeah, trenchers are cooked. Unless you’ve got some godly edge or insider info, you’re playing a losing game.

This is where @Moshdottrade’s design is far superior, by leveraging @ponsdotfamily.

Mosh pools funding for an opening bundle and locks its capital in agent vaults. Backers earn fees instead of receiving launch tokens they can immediately sell.

• Capital cannot be withdrawn after launch.
• Agents buy and sell within contract limits.
• Trade proceeds stay in the vaults.
• Backers benefit from continued trading through their fee share.

The money flows are different too:

Pumpfun’s new Block 0 fees:
• 50% → ecosystem growth.
• 50% → PUMP buybacks and burns.
• No automatic reinjection into the token that paid them.

Mosh’s eligible creator fees:
• 80% → the bundle side.
• 20% → the platform.
• Any project-team share comes from that 80%.
• A separate 5% of the raise is charged once at launch.

Pumpfun’s biggest advantage is its audience. It already brings traders, token creators and trading tools together. Another platform can copy the fee; attracting that activity is harder.

Mosh’s potential advantage is what happens to the money after launch. Funding stays in vaults, agents use it to trade, and backers share the fees. To build a lasting edge, Mosh needs reliable agents, useful integrations and results that hold up over time.

For limiting extraction from the opening bundle, I prefer Mosh’s design especially with their upcoming V1.

So, what do you think about Mosh?

text:
do you realize what Anthropic just did?

they moved their Messages API (the one Claude Code, Cowork and API customers all run through) from Python to Rust… on live traffic, without ever taking it offline

here's how they did it:

→ Claude wrote a first version of the core request path in about a week. the hard part was proving it behaved exactly like the old one

→ the Rust version passed about 98% of its tests. on real traffic only about a quarter of inputs matched

→ so they made the old Python API the judge. real requests ran through both and every difference got logged by where it happened and how big it was… never the customer's text

→ one bug leaves the same fingerprint on every request it hits, so a coordinator agent gave each new fingerprint its own worker agent and opened a Slack thread for the engineers to follow

→ workers tested guesses in a sandbox in seconds, fixes went through PR review, then got rechecked on live traffic

→ engineer corrections got saved as rules that every later agent reads
result: about 70% less CPU per request and about 20% lower median time to first token. public traffic moved over in September

now a little behind the scenes…

one agent "fixed" a web search bug by copying the tool text into a file. the two versions matched and the check passed, but an engineer rejected it as throwaway code

and when they audited the ported tests they found 100+ checks that had been weakened

if you're rewriting any code with agents…

→ now you can keep the old version running and make it the judge → group differences by fingerprint so one bug doesn't hit you as hundreds of thousands of separate diffs → you as a human can read every fix before it merges

save this process to help you

author: binji_x
quoted_text:
In October, an audit found that gas repricings in Ethereum’s upcoming Glamsterdam hardfork break assumptions some deployed contracts rely on. As a result, the hardfork rollout was paused. Since then, Ethlabs has helped with the impact analysis and the exploration of paths forward. This has led us to conclude that the best way forward is to go ahead with Glamsterdam as is.

This is a difficult trade-off, and the problems found are serious and valid. Much of the disruption comes from repricing state creation, which is a necessary step on Ethereum’s path to 1000x scaling. The only option to avoid this would be to remove the relevant EIP outright, but this would give up Glamsterdam’s roughly 3x higher gas limit, and only postpone the problem to a later hardfork. A secondary source of the disruption is the new state gas reservoir. Here changes to the EIP could address some of the concerns, but only for a subset of affected projects and at the cost of further months of delay. On net, in our assessment, neither of these options pass the cost-benefit test.

There are important lessons from Glamsterdam on how to improve future hard forks. We need to flag disruptive changes early and bring app developers in, scope impact analysis more carefully for sensitive EIPs, establish a shared understanding of which invariants app developers can rely on, and provide new primitives where there are gaps today.

You can read our full writeup here: https://t.co/G0NMm3L7eE

Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.

text:
The Agentic Scientist: Paper talk now on YouTube!

In this talk, we argue that The Agentic Scientist creates a framework by which off-the-shelf coding agents can be used as research collaborators.

Solely relying on off-the-shelf coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex, these agents tend to behave like strong hyperparameter optimizers when given a research question. While the scores improve, the ideas remain narrow and the reasons for gains are rarely examined.

The Agentic Scientist makes the research loop explicit by using a meta-controller to run parallel instances of agents over a sequence of tasks including task drafting, ideation, planning, sandboxed experiments with baselines and ablations, analysis, and writing. All steps are evaluated against rubrics defined upfront and prior to any experiments.

We showcase the results for an early version of The Agentic Scientist, which helped us study Error Diffusion, a biologically inspired alternative to backpropagation. The work was accepted as an oral at ALIFE 2026. In autonomous runs, the system raised Doc-to-LoRA multi-needle retrieval accuracy from 52% to 98% and designed a learned evolution strategy that improved over its CMA-ES reference on unseen tasks. We ablate the importance of different orchestration layers vs. the strength of base model, finding that reliable autonomy crucially depends on the latter.

Human researchers define the initial question and evidence standards, while agents extend the set of experiments that can be performed.

TL;DR of my new article: I tested 16 agent browser and computer-use tools on one Apple Silicon Mac so my agents in @t3dotcodes stop handing work back to me. Here is what won and what I switched to.

The two browser winners are almost unknown on GitHub (3k stars for @ardiabrowser, 1.1k for @opencode browse), yet they beat 54k-star agent-browser and 26k-star Stagehand on speed, RAM, and tokens. Meanwhile @trycua sits quietly at 32.9k stars powering five separate stacks in this test.

🏆 Switch browsers (what I did): @ardiabrowser + @trycua. Fastest warm loads (396 ms), zero Chrome 144 Allow popups, zero debugging infobar, built-in prompt-injection fences, and full 1Password + Touch ID Passkeys (built by @barre_of_lube, @shivamhwp, @francedot, @ddupont808; tip via @theo, @McKamyk)

🌐 Stay in Chrome: @opencode browse by @anomalyco + @trycua. Pairs once over a Chrome extension so you turn remote debugging off forever, uses 18 MB RAM, and cuts page snapshots 53x vs Stagehand and 5x vs agent-browser, with browser-control layering cleanly on top (@thdxr, @jayair, @fanjiewang, @adamdotdev, @ryanvogel, @rekram11, @sethrose; tip via @garywoodsX)

💻 Native Mac apps: cua-driver won at 27 MB RAM and zero focus steal (597 ms on Messages, 129 ms on Electron), using 8x less RAM than older Mac tools. Five stacks in the test converged on it underneath: local cua-driver, @boatdotdev, @ardiabrowser, pi-kit, and @t3dotcodes (@AniC_dev, @wolfmanfx, @theo)

🔐 Bonus setup: wired the 1Password CLI to @t3dotcodes over Touch ID so agents ask for secrets with one fingerprint tap instead of storing plaintext keys

☁️ Cloud agent factories: @boatdotdev booted 4 Ubuntu VMs in 1.9s median for $0.001, #1 for isolated cloud runs. Codex Terra's native browser fails inside T3 Code because its host pipe only lives in the Codex desktop app (tip via @babyak)

🧬 Skip pixels on repeat work: MIT and @reatools showed reverse-engineering desktop binaries into MCPs makes FreeCAD 55x faster with 35x fewer tokens, the same idea as Printing Press extended to desktop apps (@ao_qu18465, @morluto)

Only catch: if you stay in Chrome with OpenCode browse, Chrome shows a temporary debugging bar while an agent tab is open (hideable with one launch flag; Ardia patches it out natively).

Shoutout to everyone on the thread who pointed me to the winners: @theo, @garywoodsX, @altryne, @ericlitman, @siraustin, @_JDRA1, @rdylina, @McKamyk, @sethrose, @babyak, and @wolfmanfx.

中国大模型原本半年更新一代，美国这一轮芯片限制，可能要把它拖成一年一代。

路透社今天的独家报道，披露了两家中国头部模型公司的最新情况：

智谱原计划在今年 11 月发布参数规模约 3 万亿的 GLM-5.5，但目前已经落后于计划，发布时间可能推迟至 2027 年第一季度，甚至更晚。

月之暗面的情况则更加特殊。由于长期依赖海外租赁算力，据知情人士估计，如果海外算力被完全切断，其重大模型版本的迭代周期可能从 6 个月延长至 12 个月甚至更久，Kimi K4 可能要等到明年年中。

路透还将部分延期归因于 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 加强了反蒸馏措施，并援引匿名人士称，月之暗面已经开始转向谷歌和 Meta 的模型获取训练数据。不过，两家公司均未确认上述消息，月之暗面此前也明确否认过 K3 的成绩来自蒸馏。

我觉得这件事最值得警惕的是，美国正在试图拉大中美 AI 产业的迭代速度差。

在一个每隔几个月技术范式就可能发生变化的行业里，半年是什么概念？等你完成一轮训练、验证和发布，对手可能已经完成了两轮，甚至已经开始研究下一代架构。技术差距会在一次次迭代中被放大。

过去几年，中国模型公司的工程效率、人才密度和技术创造力已经得到了充分证明。但再优秀的研究员，也不能凭空创造出算力。

一家中国 AI 公司，拿着自己融来的钱，去海外租用商业算力，都可以成为美国政府限制的对象。

这也是为什么国产算力产业的成熟如此紧迫。中国 AI 不仅需要拥有自己的技术能力，还需要拥有决定自己技术发展速度的权利。

text:
HYPE trades at 16.7x revenue and 16.7x holder revenue, because all of it buys HYPE and burns it. DRV goes from 56x to 97x, RUNE from 15x to 504x

Yesterday's map priced tokens on revenue, but holders get only part of it. Same map, now on the revenue that accrues to token holders

- 27 of 36 tokens pass revenue on to holders, the other 9 get 0% in the index and sit below the map
- The median of the 27 goes from 8.9x to 19.1x
- On revenue 15 of them trade below 10x, on holder revenue only ORE, PUMP, AERO, SPK and PONS
- About two thirds of the $2.7B yearly revenue of all 36 goes to holders, and HYPE alone is half of that

Holder revenue mostly comes in three forms
- Burn: tokens leave the supply, so every holder's share grows as long as nothing new is minted (RENDER burns 95% of its fees)
- Buyback without burn: bought tokens sit in a wallet of the team, DAO or foundation, which decides later what to do with them (JUP buys into its Litterbox wallet)
- Payout: mostly to those who stake or lock (AERO pays sAERO holders since the Aero upgrade on Oct 22)

None of the multiples count new supply. ORE looks cheapest at 1.0x, a 100% holder revenue yield, but 96% new supply over the next 12 months offsets almost all of it

In the first reply: the 13 tokens where holders get the smallest share, with both multiples side by side

Elon Musk just gave American kids a shot at becoming BILLIONAIRES.

Up to 70 million children are getting 2 FREE shares of SpaceX, $SPCX, each, through their Trump Accounts.

At a current price of $127 per share, that's $255 per child.

But Musk is hinting this gift could one day be worth BILLIONS.

Musk says if SpaceX makes life multiplanetary and harnesses even a millionth of the Sun's energy, it will be "worth a MILLION TIMES the current global economy."

With the global economy at $128T, that's a $128 QUINTILLION company.

Spread across SpaceX's 13.6 billion shares, that's $9.4B per share, or $19 BILLION for every child.

To get there, $SPCX would need to rise 74 MILLION times from today's price.

And even if SpaceX issued every one of its ~52 billion authorized shares, that's still $4.9 BILLION per child.

Musk admits these goals are "absurdly difficult," but says there is "a path to achieving them."

His advice: "I recommend HOLDING on to your shares."

author: runes_leo
quoted_text:
No, I do not believe that we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems, and it’s absurd to suggest that I do. I have written hundreds of pages of essays and a constant theme in them is the need for AI to be governed by legitimate democratic processes. For millennia (going all the way back to Greek and Roman philosophers), advocates of autocracy have claimed that it leads to better, faster, or more decisive decision-making than the messy process of democracy. Even if this were true (which I doubt!), we should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea.

No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different. For example in an interview on CBS a couple months ago, I specifically called for AI to be governed democratically. I call for the same in Policy on the AI Exponential, Machines of Loving Grace, and The Adolescence of Technology, and We Must Pace the Frontier. Machines of Loving Grace contains an extended section on using AI to revitalize democracy, and discusses the use of AI as an aid to citizens in their decision-making, "aggregat[ing] opinions and driv[ing] consensus among citizens, resolving conflict, finding common ground, and seeking compromise.” The clear and obvious implication is that humans should remain the ones making political and governance decisions. The Adolescence of Technology has an entire section on fighting against AI-driven tyranny, and I even discuss the danger of AI labs usurping power and come out strongly against it — by implication, this definitely includes an AI lab usurping power and giving it to AI itself!

If I thought any of this was a good idea, I would be advocating for it in public, just as I have not been afraid to advocate for many, many unpopular views over the last few years. But I am not advocating for it, because I think turning over governance to AI is a terrible idea.

Separately, I think there is frequent conflation (including in this article) between the idea of “surrendering human free will” to AI in some grand sense of global governance, and the more prosaic idea that as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way. This is not AI “running the world,” but AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing software end-to-end. Here, my view is mixed. AI doing more complete or larger tasks is economically valuable and can drive important advances in software, medicine, transportation, energy, etc. It is clearly desirable in many cases and will save a lot of lives. But it has downsides as well, and in some areas it may not be worth it.

For example, using AI too autonomously to build the next generation of AI systems (known as recursive self-improvement, or RSI) may cause AI to improve faster than we can control or adjust to it, so we may want limits on this process. As we said publicly in early November, we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding. Second, in some contexts, using AI in too end-to-end a manner may be a cause of serious job disruption, and it may make sense to slow or even stop some AI deployments to give people more time to adapt. Third, while the use of AI for alignment research is an incredibly valuable tool, it must be done with caution, because we may not be able to trust the work of the AI system. Finally, in many cases, humans would simply prefer to do some activities themselves, so they can stay deeply engaged in what matters to them, even if AI can do those activities better. There are countless other examples and hard cases. I don’t think there are any easy answers here, nor is there (nor should there be) any single decision-maker: some of these decisions will be made by society, some by government, some by AI companies, and some in a decentralized manner by individuals expressing their own preferences as consumers, which may differ from the preferences of others.

I don't think that other AI leaders or AI companies have significantly different views from me on whether specific tasks should be automated. Certainly the products that they offer don’t differ materially in their orientation towards automation of tasks; every company seems to be releasing models more and more capable of task automation (as that’s been the general consequence of scaling up AI training), and every company claims to understand there are risks and downsides of such automation and to offer safeguards. If anything, Anthropic has been the most vocal and the most proactive about acknowledging these downsides and trying to address them. For instance, it’s fairly absurd to cite my statement that fully autonomous weapons might “one day be needed for the defense of democracy” as differing from that of other AI companies, when I was willing to risk Anthropic’s future as a company to refuse to allow our existing AI models to be used for autonomous weapons even in the face of legal sanctions, and no other AI company did the same.

To summarize, as applied to grand questions of how we govern increasingly capable AI, I have been vocal and consistent that AI needs to be governed by a legitimate, democratic process and that “surrendering human free will” to AI systems is a terrible idea. As applied to automation of specific tasks by or for people, my views are more mixed, but I don’t think they differ from those of other AI companies — most other companies seem to be offering similar products and confronting similar tradeoffs without having perfect answers to them. What is happening is that there’s a sort of vibes-based commercial and political positioning that some AI CEOs are engaging in, where they repeat slogans like “human control and agency,” or “AI should be just a tool,” without actually doing anything different in their products or taking seriously the difficult questions that lie behind these slogans.

Kamino Omni: Lets managers build tokenized portfolios that combine spot, lending and leverage in a single token. E.g. a 2x SPYx strategy or an equal weight MAG7 basket.

今天软银再次暴跌近15%，较6月高点累计下跌约68%，总市值只剩966亿美元，甚至不及其单独持有的Arm股份，也低于9月底其OpenAI持仓的账面价值（996亿美元）。

即便考虑到近期Arm的暴跌，软银目前相对于NAV（净资产价值）的折价仍在60%左右。

为什么市场给软银这么大的折价？

孙正义这轮AI豪赌很大程度上是通过杠杆完成的：

以Arm股份质押获得250亿美元融资额度
以OpenAI股权估值为基础获得100亿美元贷款，并设有追加保证金机制
9月发行100亿美元及10亿欧元债券，美元债票息最高达到9.75%，如今长期美元债收益率已经超过10%。

软银利用AI资产上涨带来的融资能力，借钱继续投资AI。这个模式在牛市中能够不断放大收益，但在熊市中，反身性也会朝相反的方向运转。

如果Arm股价下跌 ,会导致软银融资能力下降, 然后潜在的被迫减持 ,股价进一步承压。与此同时，OpenAI仍在大量烧钱，Arm也不提供股息收入，但软银的债务利息需要实打实地用现金支付

今天软银的5年期CDS已经飙升至501个基点，创2022年以来新高

我认为软银是目前整个AI产业链中最值得关注的潜在风险点之一。尤其是如果OpenAI下一轮融资估值下降，或者IPO进一步推迟，软银可能成为AI泡沫破裂过程中一个重要的风险传导节点

quoted_text:
La política argentina está discutiendo nimiedades sobre las PASO y pelotudeces que no le importan a casi nadie, mientras la inteligencia artificial está atacando algunos de los problemas científicos más difíciles de la historia de la humanidad.

En menos de una semana se presentaron posibles demostraciones de la hipótesis de Riemann, de VP ≠ VNP y Navier Stokes. Ayer se publicó incluso una propuesta de cuantización de la gravedad que podría reconciliar la relatividad general de Einstein con la mecánica cuántica.

La inteligencia artificial está revolucionando la matemática, la física y las ciencias de la computación. Lo mismo está empezando a ocurrir en la química y la biología.

¿En serio creen que esto no le va a llegar al tipo común? ¿Que no va a transformar su trabajo, su salario, la educación de sus hijos, su salud, sus ahorros y sus posibilidades de progresar?

Lo que se viene es un tsunami científico, tecnológico, económico y social. Un cambio civilizatorio.

Buena parte de nuestras instituciones, categorías ideológicas y discusiones políticas de los últimos doscientos años son herederas de la Revolución Francesa, la Revolución Industrial y las transformaciones en la división social del trabajo.

Nuestros sistemas de representación política, nuestras instituciones educativas, nuestras leyes laborales, nuestros sistemas tributarios y de seguridad social fueron concebidos para determinadas condiciones materiales y productivas.

Esas condiciones están cambiando radicalmente. Si cambia la división del trabajo, cambia la estructura de clases, cambia la distribución del poder económico y, por ende, cambia la naturaleza de los conflictos sociales y de la representación política.

Tenemos que preparar al Estado, las leyes y las instituciones para que sean capaces de adaptarse a un cambio civilizatorio.

Hay que estudiar a líderes como Lee Kuan Yew que transformó Singapur, una pequeña ciudad portuaria con enormes problemas de pobreza, desempleo y vivienda, en una potencia tecnológica, financiera y comercial que alcanzó niveles extraordinarios de prosperidad.

Construyeron centros industriales sobre pantanos, apostaron por la educación, atrajeron capital y talento extranjero y encontraron una manera de insertarse en el mundo que estaba emergiendo, en lugar de intentar preservar el mundo que estaba desapareciendo.

Deberíamos estar discutiendo cómo convertir al país en un polo de infraestructura computacional, cómo atraer a los mejores científicos y emprendedores del mundo, cómo transformar nuestras universidades, cómo desarrollar nuevas industrias y cómo hacer que esa prosperidad llegue a millones de argentinos.

En última instancia, son unas pocas decisiones estratégicas, bien tomadas, ejecutadas con inteligencia y sostenidas en el tiempo, las que pueden cambiar el destino de un país durante generaciones.

Necesitamos construir un país capaz de adaptarse rápidamente a un mundo que todavía no comprendemos del todo. Hoy estamos al horno.

La historia se está acelerando y nosotros seguimos discutiendo las mismas pelotudeces de siempre.

quoted_text: I have prepared a 1,200-page human-readable deformalization of Luke Sernau's condensed Lean proof of the generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, itself a rewriting of Levent Alpöge's proof. It is the result of combined work with several AI agents, which first decompiled the proof into so-called structured proofs (in the sense of Leslie Lamport) and then wrote the final text. The draft is already readable. Its notation is rather pedantic, because it follows the formal proof closely, and it gathers the whole argument into a single document. I hope it will help mathematicians around the world gain deeper insight into the proof and keep simplifying and beautifying the argument. text:
Elon just used America's kids to protect SpaceX's stock price.

The headlines called it an $18 billion gift. But almost none of them mentioned the rules those shares come with...

Trump Accounts were written into law as index fund accounts. The statute says no part of the money can go into anything other than an "eligible investment," which means a cheap fund that tracks a US stock index.

That rule was there to keep kids out of single stocks.

Then on September 29, Treasury issued new regulations with an exception: Stock that gets donated into the accounts doesn't count as an investment, so the index fund rule doesn't apply to it.

3 weeks later, Elon made his first pledge.

What makes this so genius:

The families can't say no. The shares land in the account whether the parents want them or not.

And they can't SELL. Donated stock has to be held for 5 years, or until the end of the year the child turns 17, whichever comes first.

If the shares get sold early anyway, the account's trustee has to buy the same number of shares back.

So millions of SpaceX shares are about to land with holders who are legally locked in for up to 5 years.

Jane Ditelberg of Northern Trust told InvestmentNews the holding period protects donors from a selling wave that could push the share price down.

That's the whole trick in one sentence.

And the timing is perfect:

The company's share goes out next month. Elon said his own share will be transferred "when my lockup expires in June next year."

A lockup is the stretch after an IPO when insiders aren't allowed to sell. When it ends, big holders usually start selling. Some of the shares Elon is free to sell in June will go straight into accounts that can't sell them for up to 5 years.

And SpaceX could use the help. The stock traded just above $127 on Wednesday. It priced its IPO at $135 in June and hit $201.80 on June 16.

Then there's the tax angle: 

Under the new rules, donors can avoid tax on any unrealized gains in the stock they donate, according to Kitces.

And the company's half is brand new stock. SpaceX is issuing fresh shares to cover it, so every existing shareholder pays for that half through dilution.

Treasury's own regulations spell out the goal: Donors hope the holding period gives recipients "a stake in the fate of the corporation."

Millions of American families now have a stake in the fate of SpaceX. Every regulator who slows SpaceX down and every politician who goes after it is now hitting kids' savings accounts.

The case for it is easy: It's free stock for kids, and if SpaceX doubles, nobody will complain. Michael Dell defended stock gifts by saying "It's kind of hard for me to believe that's a bad thing, right?"

But Adam Michel of the Cato Institute put the problem in one line: "You have no choice in the asset that is being deposited into your child's account."

So should parents be allowed to say no to free SpaceX stock?

The problem with callout rewards is that the day you make good money from a callout, the next day you want to call out everything.

Then you see some guy buying at 4K MC, thinking you've discovered the next gem, and the minute you buy, it starts nuking.

It requires a ridiculous amount of discipline. Don't get inspired by someone else's winning trades without looking at their overall PnL.

However, I do think social trading has massive potential with perps, provided there's enough liquidity, assets and leverage available.

As for me, I somehow turned a reward mechanism into a $50K expense. 😂

text:
之前看多加密行情的机构 @glxyresearch Galaxy，昨天也发布了一份研报，撤回了“比特币熊市已结束”的判断，认为从历史周期和市场深度来看，价格有进一步下探可能。

他们结合宏观流动性、机构 13F 持仓和历史熊市统计规律，列出了几个最值得注意的危险信号：

1. bitcoin:native 连续 7 周下跌并跌破 50 周均线，历史统计指向继续探底

报告回溯 2014 年以来的历次熊市数据发现，这种走法从来不是调整结束的终点，一般是熊市进入主跌段或深度磨底的确认信号。

2.美股突发恐慌指数飙升后，比特币往往还要再跌一波

有一个 2011 年以来的历史规律：
每当美股风平浪静三个月以上，突然出现剧烈暴跌、让 VIX 恐慌指数冲破 35时，比特币真正的熊市最低点全部出现在这个情形之后。

眼下美股刚经历剧烈震荡，能否守住 6 月的 59,517 美元周线低点，直接决定了比特币会不会重演历史上的二次探底。

3. 机构短线资金撤退，美股科技股与宏观流动性仍在施压

通过拆解美国机构季末提交的 13F 持仓报告（按真实持币数量计算，剔除币价波动干扰）以及永续合约资金费率、CME 期货持仓，报告发现：
早期涌入的对冲基金和短线套利盘正在持续降杠杆撤离。同时，比特币与纳斯达克 100 及费城半导体指数维持高相关性，在美股科技股回调、美国净流动性尚未重新扩张之前，比特币很难走出独立反弹行情。

4.链上估值与地板模型尚未到达历次熊市极端出清区

虽然全网处于亏损状态的筹码占比正在上升，但综合全网平均持仓成本（MVRV）以及累计价值天数销毁（CVDD）地板模型来看，当前市场还没有跌到 2018 年和 2022 年大熊市彻底出清时的极端低估区间，下方依然留有空间。

至于接下来会怎么走，Galaxy 认为有2种可能。

a. 如果“时间周期”占上风，这轮已经走了 412 天的熊市（已超过 2021–22 年整轮熊市 366 天的跨度）正处在最后一段，时间窗口大约在 2027 年 4 月关闭。

最近的一簇支撑在 48,400 到 53,200 美元，如果在这里止步，这将是比特币有史以来最浅的一轮熊市，也是第一轮没有在全网平均成本线（53,205 美元）下方持续停留的熊市。

b.如果“下跌深度”占上风，市场将向过去历次大熊市结束时的估值收敛，目标区间在 29,100 到 46,100 美元，并且伴随一段持续低于全网平均成本线的煎熬期。

要想证伪这种深熊预期，周线必须重新站回 200 周均线（68,159 美元）乃至 50 周均线（74,401 美元）上方；反之，一旦周线收在 53,205 美元下方，更深的探底就正式打开了。

Demand for peptide drugs is growing rapidly, and our ability to provide these medicines is under increasing pressure.

quoted_text:
TL;DR of my new article: I tested 16 agent browser and computer-use tools on one Apple Silicon Mac so my agents in @t3dotcodes stop handing work back to me. Here is what won and what I switched to.

The two browser winners are almost unknown on GitHub (3k stars for @ardiabrowser, 1.1k for @opencode browse), yet they beat 54k-star agent-browser and 26k-star Stagehand on speed, RAM, and tokens. Meanwhile @trycua sits quietly at 32.9k stars powering five separate stacks in this test.

🏆 Switch browsers (what I did): @ardiabrowser + @trycua. Fastest warm loads (396 ms), zero Chrome 144 Allow popups, zero debugging infobar, built-in prompt-injection fences, and full 1Password + Touch ID Passkeys (built by @barre_of_lube, @shivamhwp, @francedot, @ddupont808; tip via @theo, @McKamyk)

🌐 Stay in Chrome: @opencode browse by @anomalyco + @trycua. Pairs once over a Chrome extension so you turn remote debugging off forever, uses 18 MB RAM, and cuts page snapshots 53x vs Stagehand and 5x vs agent-browser, with browser-control layering cleanly on top (@thdxr, @jayair, @fanjiewang, @adamdotdev, @ryanvogel, @rekram11, @sethrose; tip via @garywoodsX)

💻 Native Mac apps: cua-driver won at 27 MB RAM and zero focus steal (597 ms on Messages, 129 ms on Electron), using 8x less RAM than older Mac tools. Five stacks in the test converged on it underneath: local cua-driver, @boatdotdev, @ardiabrowser, pi-kit, and @t3dotcodes (@AniC_dev, @wolfmanfx, @theo)

🔐 Bonus setup: wired the 1Password CLI to @t3dotcodes over Touch ID so agents ask for secrets with one fingerprint tap instead of storing plaintext keys

☁️ Cloud agent factories: @boatdotdev booted 4 Ubuntu VMs in 1.9s median for $0.001, #1 for isolated cloud runs. Codex Terra's native browser fails inside T3 Code because its host pipe only lives in the Codex desktop app (tip via @babyak)

🧬 Skip pixels on repeat work: MIT and @reatools showed reverse-engineering desktop binaries into MCPs makes FreeCAD 55x faster with 35x fewer tokens, the same idea as Printing Press extended to desktop apps (@ao_qu18465, @morluto)

Only catch: if you stay in Chrome with OpenCode browse, Chrome shows a temporary debugging bar while an agent tab is open (hideable with one launch flag; Ardia patches it out natively).

Shoutout to everyone on the thread who pointed me to the winners: @theo, @garywoodsX, @altryne, @ericlitman, @siraustin, @_JDRA1, @rdylina, @McKamyk, @sethrose, @babyak, and @wolfmanfx.

Full 16-tool scoreboard, charts, and copy-paste setup prompts for both stacks in the article.

text:
在 Polymarket 的 NBA 赛场上，一次两分球或三分球的命中，都可能让比赛的隐含概率发生几个百分点的变化。

于是，我尝试通过机器学习，在 Opus 5.5 的辅助下，开发了一套实时篮球投篮命中率预测模型。

它的原理不复杂，主要分为三个步骤。

第一步：识别篮球的位置。

首先要让模型学会识别画面中的篮球。

通过比赛视频和人工标注，制作训练数据，再用这些数据训练模型，让它学会识别画面中的篮球。

经过大量训练，目前模型已经能够找到画面中约 91% 的篮球。

第二步：还原三维飞行弧线。

这一步不需要训练模型。

只需要知道摄像机的位置、拍摄角度和镜头参数（相机标定），再结合第一步识别出的篮球像素位置，就可以估算篮球在三维空间中的位置、出手位置和初速度。

在篮球飞行过程中，不断根据新识别的位置校准轨迹，从而预测篮球最终的下落位置。

第三步：计算命中率。

这一步需要大量数据，也就是机器学习分类模型。

我使用的是 NBA 2015-16 赛季的 SportVU 追踪数据，约 56,000 次投篮。

从每一次投篮的三维轨迹中，提取几个关键数据：

- 球到达篮筐高度时，相对于篮筐中心是偏远了还是偏近了（前后偏差）
- 是偏左还是偏右（左右偏差）。
- 球下落时的角度。

再把这些数据交给分类模型，训练它判断这次投篮是否命中。

最终的测试结果：

刚出手的时候，预测准确率在 0.75 左右；等球快到篮筐的时候，可以达到 0.85–0.9。

唯一的遗憾是，这套模型如果不在现场，基本没有什么卵用。因为电视转播本身的延迟，远远大于模型提前预测所能抢出来的这点时间。

text:
Sky's $stUSDS lenders are now liquidating their own borrowers

on monday i warned that a $240K loan in this $USDC market on @Morpho could be liquidated around wednesday, and asked who would take the loss. early thursday UTC it was liquidated by one of its own lenders, a depositor of the Risk Capital vault @SkyEcosystem runs, which lends only into this market

the market was fully lent out, so depositors had nothing to withdraw. liquidating a borrower gets around that. in one transaction a depositor uses its $USDC in the vault to repay the borrower's loan and gets the borrower's $stUSDS with a 4.4% bonus. so it leaves the vault holding $stUSDS instead of $USDC

on wednesday two wallets from another vault, Parity High Yield USDC, did the same with $220K of a bigger loan. they sold all of that $stUSDS within a day at about 9.5% below its value, which cost them about $12K. so the loss i asked about landed on the lenders who chose to sell. the Risk Capital depositor still holds its $stUSDS

the two largest loans left add up to $5.3M, while the $stUSDS pool on @CurveFinance holds only $156K of $USDS. if they get liquidated, it will most likely be depositors again, and whoever needs cash will pay the Curve discount
author: punkquidity
quoted_text:
be careful with the 47% APY in Sky's $USDC Risk Capital vault

since friday morning all three Risk Capital vaults that @SkyEcosystem runs on @Morpho have been fully lent out against $stUSDS, and nobody has repaid since. that's why the 47% keeps climbing

these loans count $stUSDS at the full price from Sky's own contract. early today someone put $125.6K into the $USDT vault, and in the next block a bot borrowed all of it against $stUSDS it had just bought for $119.3K. the vault lent more than that collateral cost

with a liquidation bonus of only 4.4%, a liquidator who sells that $stUSDS loses money, so the loss on a bad loan would end up with depositors

by tonight, borrowing from the $USDC vault should cost more than $stUSDS pays, so those loans start growing faster than their collateral. if nobody repays, the weakest one, a $240K loan, can be liquidated around wednesday, and then we'll see who takes that loss

text:
我在想，未来 2 到 3 年有一段时间，我可能不会再经常旅游了。现在旅游更像是 Vibe Coding 当中的一个甜点。

这世界上每分每秒都发生着剧烈、重大的变化，我现在已经很难发现有其他事情比这件事情更上瘾、更值得去做、更有乐趣。

在年中的时候，我曾有一段时间一直在外面玩，很重要的原因是因为我相信大家在年初开始 Vibe Coding 都经历了 burnout。但是休息一段时间之后，你会发现所有的事情不仅没有变慢，能做的事情不仅没有变少，反而是呈爆发式加速增长。也就是说，我们现在所处的时间节点看起来非常平静，甚至在平静下面隐藏着一些危机，但实际上是一个宏大的人类从未经历过的时代的开端。

有的时候我觉得，这已经不是赚钱与否、是否创造一个产品、享受乐趣这么简单的一件事。

于我而言，谁不想一起创造一个我们前所未见的、从亘古到现在都没有出现过的伟大时代呢？这样伟大的时代，不可能，也不应该仅仅属于硅谷。

The post in question from yesterday. For some added context, the decision of how to proceed with Glamsterdam was pending for a few weeks. The ACDC call today made the decision to proceed with the fork in its unchanged form.
https://t.co/POAjlatsBV
author: adietrichs
quoted_text:
In October, an audit found that gas repricings in Ethereum’s upcoming Glamsterdam hardfork break assumptions some deployed contracts rely on. As a result, the hardfork rollout was paused. Since then, Ethlabs has helped with the impact analysis and the exploration of paths forward. This has led us to conclude that the best way forward is to go ahead with Glamsterdam as is.

This is a difficult trade-off, and the problems found are serious and valid. Much of the disruption comes from repricing state creation, which is a necessary step on Ethereum’s path to 1000x scaling. The only option to avoid this would be to remove the relevant EIP outright, but this would give up Glamsterdam’s roughly 3x higher gas limit, and only postpone the problem to a later hardfork. A secondary source of the disruption is the new state gas reservoir. Here changes to the EIP could address some of the concerns, but only for a subset of affected projects and at the cost of further months of delay. On net, in our assessment, neither of these options pass the cost-benefit test.

There are important lessons from Glamsterdam on how to improve future hard forks. We need to flag disruptive changes early and bring app developers in, scope impact analysis more carefully for sensitive EIPs, establish a shared understanding of which invariants app developers can rely on, and provide new primitives where there are gaps today.

You can read our full writeup here: https://t.co/G0NMm3L7eE

text:
Anthropic was the single largest IPO ever.

So we thought we would add a special guest to the only show you have to listen to every week....

Welcoming, Matt Murphy at Menlo.

AGENDA:

- Jensen Huang's $1TRN Return: What Happens Now
- Anthropic Goes Public: Largest IPO Of All Time & How It Changes Venture
- Applied Compute, https://t.co/2iPprmgVXR and Mailchimp Acquisitions Broken Down

My notes below with @jasonlk and @mmurph

-------------------------------------------------

1. Do Companies Have to Be a Top One or Two to Make Real Venture Returns?

Investing in the fifth or sixth player in a category feels easy when the numbers are this strong, with growth as high as 92% a month. Jason worries that being comfortable backing the number six player is the biggest sign of a bubble of all.

2. How Can You Justify That Any Investment Not Growing Top Quartile Is Worth More Than 2x?

Mailchimp went at 2.9x and Miro and Airtable sit in the twos, and those businesses are at scale. A B2B company held on the books since 2021 at $150M and growing 18% has no comp that justifies a value above 2x.

3. Why CRMs Are Dead and Horizontal Agents Like Muse Will Win

Horizontal apps won through 2021, and horizontal agents will win next year. With Muse, a user says what they want and it becomes a set of workflows. An agent can build a founder list from five years of email, rank it and run the outreach, which leaves SMBs asking what they need a CRM for.

4. Why You Cannot Trust Vibe-Coded Apps or SaaS Apps in This Cyber Environment

2027 will bring the death of many SaaS players and of vibe coding because buyers cannot trust these apps. Optimizely had 170 leaks, Gainsight was offline for a month and the Shopify ecosystem was hacked through tokens that never expired. Most classic B2B companies will fail security audits, with no one defending against a swarm of 1,000 agents.

5. Why Is It Better for Jensen That He Was Let Go and Came Back Than Investigated Without Leaving?

Stepping down and returning has a cleansing effect compared with staying on through a board investigation, congressional hearings and gossip in the halls. Now around 90% of it cannot be discussed and the company moves on, much as no one talks about Sam Altman's seven days away.

6. How Does Jensen Change From This: More Aggressive, Less Aggressive?

Nvidia is likely to triple down on product and build the next Super Blackwell better and faster. External moves such as data centers in Malaysia may be clipped as Jensen focuses on the core. That is likely negative for venture at the margin, but having him there is still better.

7. Should We Have Model Disclosures?

Large enterprises do not want the underlying model technology to be opaque, even if they never cared which cloud ran their infrastructure. Disclosure will increasingly be demanded, though some customers will be fine without it. That should accelerate open source models from other players and make the market more competitive.

Potential consequences include:

• USDS depeg
• Oracle price discrepancies
• Bad debt and cascading liquidations
• An estimated $10B in DeFi capital outflows
The author believes Circle would only take such action if legally compelled.

author: TTT_News_
quoted_text:
My thoughts on USDS and @SkyEcosystem:

Imagine Circle freezes $1.86B of Sky's USDC in its Peg Stability Module (PSM).

I don't think we'll see any freezing unless legally required to do so. The consequences would be too catastrophic for the industry.

Many people, myself included, would start questioning whether anywhere in DeFi is safe.

If this sets a precedent, what's stopping Hyperliquid's USDC bridge from facing a similar situation in the future?

And that's not even considering the potential impact on the USDS peg. USDS is one of the major stablecoins integrated across DeFi. A significant depeg could trigger oracle pricing discrepancies, bad debt, and cascading liquidations.

By my own rough estimate, freezing $1.86B in Sky's PSM could potentially trigger $10B in capital outflows across DeFi.

With USDC's circulating supply at around $69B, why would Circle risk undermining confidence in one of its largest use cases?

Especially when the industry is already struggling with capital outflows and declining risk appetite.

Of course, regulatory obligations are a different story. But from an economic incentive perspective, it makes little sense to me.

Just my two cents, could be wrong tho.

Before I dive into some turkey, I wanted to elaborate on this a bit.

Bound has not only built a new derivative, but we implemented an architecture that prioritizes decentralization and removes counterparty risk. Almost like a new derivative plus an AMM to price and execute it.

Boundary contracts are not contracts with us nor a market maker. They are enforced entirely via smart contract, decentralized from the start.

This is *only* possible because of hyperliquid precompiles.

Now to Elysium and why we’re thankful.

While the precompiles are essential to our infrastructure, we still face same issues

- high gas prices
- limitations in the types of precompiles
- limitations in response time

Elysium addresses each one of these issues: cheaper gas, all the functionality of the hyperEVM precompiles + more (soon), and faster execution.

Overall, Elysium is picking up where Hyperliquid left off and continuing to scale the composability of the Hyperliquid orderbook, and we’re all about it.

Hyperliquid.

text:
spot dex volumes to cex volumes have doubled from ~10% two years ago to ~20% today. i expect this trend to continue. the natural conclusion is that this is bearish for cex's, but is it?

the future of onchain trading, imo, is trading onchain through a custodian. use kraken as an example. they added onchain trading in-app recently and take a 1% fee for onchain trades. they are also going to be deploying hip-3 markets to let their users trade on hyperliquid. while declining cex volumes are a negative, these are new opportunities for them. the cex model is shifting from purely cex trading fees on their own book to now including onchain custody/security as a service. 

why would users want this? to me, it's about security, convenience and contingency planning. for most users they want to trade onchain but don't want self-custody. managing seed phrases, hardware wallets, etc. is overwhelming, confusing, hard to put into a will, risky and clunky.

by trading onchain through a cex they get the exchange handling the custody and security aspects and they pay more in fees. i don't know what the right fee is, and while 1% feels egregious, it's pretty standard range for onchain trading. for a user you now just need to lockdown the security of one account and that's it. yes you are accepting third party risk but it's a choice i believe many users will make.

in 2-3 years i expect the majority of onchain trading to be done through custodians, a big opportunity for the cex's. while they mostly just have simple dex swapping for now, adding true onchain support for apps seems a natural next evolution.

quoted_text:
I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC...
- Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid.
- The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.
- 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map.
- Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry
- Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.

It's deployed here: https://t.co/QMhmafXMj5 and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. Possibly it can be expanded or built into a game. I only have half of my weekly Claude quote left though so someone else will have to take over :D. Claude also made a trailer:

We hosted Inkling 2 Mini by @thinkymachines on an InstaBox GPU machine and put it head-to-head against Opus 5.5.

So we used the most accurate benchmark: building a Snake game.

- Inkling 2 Mini hosted on an @instabox_sh H100: 6.2s (~340 tok/s)
- Opus 5.5 via Claude Code: 14.7s (~150 tok/s)

Same prompt, both on low effort.

I think open models should be doing a lot more work inside agents. If a smaller, open-source model can handle a task, you can definitely run it on your own GPU, keep your data private, and only pay for compute.

We added Endpoints to InstaBox to make that easier. Pick an open model, and we handle getting it running. You call it through an OpenAI-compatible API and get your own model at ~180-640 tok/s.

text:
比特币/以太坊金库公司的核心估值指标是 mNAV（Multiple of NAV，市值相对其持有加密资产净值的倍数）。
牛市时：mNAV 往往显著高于 1（市场愿意给溢价）。公司可通过发行新股（如 ATM 增发）以高于净值的价格融资，再用所得资金买入更多 BTC/ETH。由于发行价高于每股对应的持币价值，这一过程对现有股东是增值的（accretive），能持续提升每股持币数量，形成正向飞轮。
熊市时：mNAV 频繁跌破 1（出现折价）。此时再发行新股会稀释每股持币量，对公司和股东均不划算，增发买币的动能基本消失。
一来一去，mNAV 的溢价/折价切换与“是否继续增发买币”的机制，本身就成为波动率的放大器：牛市时加速加仓推高股价与持币量，熊市时停止加仓、甚至因折价与情绪进一步放大下跌幅度。

author: varun_mathur
quoted_text:
How one blog post and the NYT became the center of the coverage against Travis Kalanick in 2017

tl;dr: what happened to Jensen happened to Travis back then

In early 2017, Susan Fowler, who later joined the NYT, wrote a blog post with allegations against Uber which quickly got picked up by .... the NYT - and together their stories ended up being cited over 500 times in reporting by other outlets. 

As we saw for recent reporting against Jensen, NYT again had the highest citation authority as measured by PageRank between all the relevant stories here. 43% of stories that cited a source cited Susan + NYT. When claims spread, fewer than 1 in 10 follow-ups did their own reporting, and most repeated them without attribution. The same echo-chamber pattern as Jensen.

Within a few months, alongside that citation power, and the consistent negative reporting of allegations, this had converted to a scandal, resulting in enormous pressure which led to the removal of Travis as the CEO of the company he founded. While Susan went on to work for the NYT, and an NYT reporter who covered the story extensively wrote a bestselling book that became a TV series, Travis had to live through the trauma of being forced out from his own company at a time of profound personal tragedy.

The below is a story in data, of the patterns which are for all to observe. To analyze this, I used a swarm of over 100 agents using my home-cooked agentic platform, which went through 500GB of public news data, almost 8,000 stories across several months in early 2017, and where the agents exchanged thousands of messages between each other as they analyzed and cross-checked these stories and core facts, building the verified citation graph. Explore yourself at: https://t.co/jVWTn3p5IA

🚨 BREAKING: @Microsoft released Aion 1.0 Instruct, a 2.3B open-weight model built from scratch that will power Windows' on-device AI.

The model, dubbed Aion 1.0 Instruct, is set to replace Phi Silica as the built-in AI model in Windows, and should start making its way to users’ devices by the end of January.

Microsoft says the model clocks an IFEval score of 83.9% and GSM8K score of 74.9%, packing a 32K context window, tool calling capabilities, and multilingual support for eight languages.
The model has been made available for download under an MIT license, meaning anyone can use it, even commercially.

author: alex_prompter
quoted_text:
There are six layers to a working agentic system.

Most companies spend their time debating which model to pick. The model sits inside a larger operating system, and almost every production failure happens in the six layers wrapped around it.

> Layer one: experience and trigger. Stop defaulting to a chat box. Real business agents fire on an event: a file arrival, an incoming invoice, a ticket status change, or a schedule. When the agent needs a human, it routes to an exception queue or inbox, not a raw chat transcript nobody on the ops team has time to read.

> Layer two: orchestration and state. Stop treating agents like scripts sitting on someone's laptop. An agent definition should be versioned, bounded, and governed like any other code artifact, with rollback. Store execution history and checkpoints in a database like Postgres so an interrupted run resumes where it left off instead of restarting from scratch.

> Layer three: tools and deterministic logic. The guarantees live in plain, unit-tested code, not in the prompt. Wrap your proven business logic and system-of-record APIs behind one connector service as named tools with stable interfaces. Let deterministic rules handle the fixed steps, and call the model only where judgment is actually required.

> Layer four: trusted context. Do not dump your whole wiki or repo into a giant prompt. Give each domain its own scoped knowledge graph or data catalog that the agent queries mid-run as a tool. When documentation drifts from reality, agents hallucinate. The fix is not a longer prompt. It is authoritative, permission-aware context.

> Layer five: evaluation and human control. Before an agent touches a customer or moves money, build a golden set of real past cases that your domain experts agree are right. Run deterministic checks and LLM-as-a-judge evaluations on every change, and keep a human approval gate on any high-impact or irreversible action. Operators stop pressing buttons and start judging.

> Layer six: runtime and control plane. Every model call goes through one LLM gateway inside your own cloud perimeter. Direct calls to a vendor API are a production defect. Enforce virtual keys per tenant and service, hard spend caps, prompt-injection guardrails, full traces, and internal model aliases so swapping providers is a configuration change, not a rewrite.

Models and frameworks will keep changing. The durable assets are your workflow rules, evaluation sets, context boundaries, and operational ownership.

text:
$VVV dropped 14% in 2 hours on a privacy scare. We checked every claim.

The loudest one is that Venice hid where your prompts go. It didn't. Its privacy page has said since March that Private models run on Venice GPUs or vetted partner hardware under zero-retention contracts, and it labels that tier trust-based.

The leak talk doesn't hold up either. Nobody has shown a single prompt being logged, stored or exposed.

What's fair is the wording. The homepage still said "self-hosted" until this week, and many Private models do run on partners like DeepInfra and Fireworks. Venice has already updated the site, though.

The one open question is technical. A code-level write-up argues some end-to-end encrypted models leave room for a middleman to swap keys. No exploit has been shown, and a public fix would close it.

Meanwhile, the business looks real. On-chain burns point to nine figures of yearly sales, and the token burns supply with every subscription. That slice is still small, around $14M a year, which is the thing to watch as it scales.

If you want privacy, you can verify yourself, the TEE and E2EE tiers are built for that. The rest of this week's panic looks a lot bigger than the facts.

🚨 The UK is taking a dangerous page out of the 2008 housing crisis playbook.

Nationwide, one of Britain's largest mortgage lenders, has launched a 99% mortgage scheme for first-time buyers, allowing eligible borrowers to:

- Put down just 1% upfront.

- Borrow up to 99% of a property's value.

- Borrow up to 6 times their annual income.

- Secure loans of up to £750,000 over 40 years.

This is an extremely high-risk scheme, as even a 1% drop in house prices could wipe out the buyer's entire initial equity.

A 10% decline on a £500,000 home could leave them £45,000 underwater, before accounting for repayments.

This echoes the lead-up to 2008, when loose lending standards and falling house prices left highly leveraged homeowners exposed.

The timing is also concerning as the UK Government warns 6.5 million of its households could face higher mortgage payments in the coming years, while around 1 million borrowers on fixed rates below 3% are due to remortgage by the end of 2027.

Are lenders making housing more accessible, or simply encouraging households to take on even more debt?

text:
I’ve been a SpaceX $SPCX investor since 2020, before the IPO. What most people still don’t grasp is that SpaceX isn’t a company you value with a DCF. It’s a civilization company. The moment it succeeds at making life multiplanetary and captures even a fraction of the Sun’s energy, the economic system the model assumes no longer exists. You’re not discounting cash flows inside an economy. You’re discounting the replacement of the economy itself.

That’s why I told people before the IPO: don’t put money in until you deeply understand what this company is actually building. New investors saw rocket launches and data centers and bought the feeling of upside. That’s not the same as holding a civilizational thesis through a 50% drawdown. Elon’s “hold your shares” is a conclusion for him. For the market, it’s still an assumption most haven’t earned.

Once you truly understand what this company is set to become — how far ahead Starship is from every competitor, how dominant Starlink’s technology already is — price swings stop being threats. They become either noise you ignore or opportunities to add. You don’t panic-sell, because you’ve already done the work that makes panic unnecessary.

text:
The Sky/Spark liquidity event had an impact on onchain lending market share.

Aave V3 increased its market share to 38%, with more deposits than the next 4 protocols combined.

Aave V4 is close to reaching $2B in deposits and was the only top 10 protocol to grow, up 26%, going from #11 to #6 in the last 30D.

In the same period, SparkLend, Morpho, JustLend and Maple lost close to $8B in deposits.
author: sealaunch_
quoted_text:
The recent Sky/Spark liquidity event set off a chain reaction across lending markets.

Level 1: capital moved to depth and safety. USDC deposits on @aave V3 Ethereum grew by $1.4B in a week. Aave is the natural destination, with the deepest liquidity and largest TVL in DeFi lending. The inflow pushed its USDC borrow APY down to ~1.9%.

Level 2: the Spark Liquidity Layer pulled ~$468M from the Morpho cbBTC/USDC market on Base. Grove x Steakhouse USDC removed another ~$125M.

This is the largest market behind @coinbase Onchain Loans. With liquidity gone, the borrow APY jumped to ~10%, more than double its usual ~4.5%.

To refill liquidity and bring rates down, Steakhouse High Yield USDC Edition moved ~$300M from the USDe/USDC market into cbBTC/USDC. USDe/USDC on Base went from $370M supply / $329M borrows to $58M / $51M, with $7M of liquidity left.

Level 3: Morpho vault curators are restricted to Morpho markets, so they rotated to BTC markets on Ethereum that aren't correlated with Base: cbBTC/USDT (+$37M) and WBTC/USDC (+$27M), where yields are now lower. Borrowers moved too. With USDC on Aave now cheap to borrow, institutional BTC borrowers added ~$118M of USDC borrows against cbBTC.

This is a reminder that DeFi liquidity behaves like a graph, and isolated markets don't isolate liquidity risk. With more curators running multi-protocol vaults, liquidity is in practice shared across protocols, markets, curators and chains.

For lending protocols, depth is the real moat. For curators, it's speed and how fast you move before the liquidity is gone.

quoted_text:
Angelo 2.1 is out!!

Angelo is a free, open-source fork of Blender with an AI agent built in. This release is about getting from a rough start to finished work:

• Retopology turns a scan, sculpt or generated mesh into clean quads. On a held-out test set frozen before any tuning, it finished all 42 runs; QuadriFlow, Blender's built-in quad remesher, finished 22. Same meshes, machine and grading.
• Plan first: talk a task through with the agent and compare approaches before anything in your scene changes.
• Mark up a picture: draw, point and pin comments on a picture or the 3D view to show the agent what you mean.
• Folder as context: a chat can use up to five of your folders; Angelo reads them and writes its notes, checklists and plans as text files only in the working folder.
• Rig tools: retarget animation, make game rigs for Unreal Engine, Unity and Godot, and add IK controls to any humanoid armature.
• Built in and free, the kind of tools artists usually reach for add-ons to get: Retopology, Shape Cut for draw-to-cut hard-surface work, Scatter with six biome presets, UV Layout at the texel density you choose, Camera Look's lens and film looks, and a Loops menu with the names LoopTools users know.
• Also new: Fit Collision Hulls for game engines, and Splats to Mesh for Gaussian splats.
• Features from Blender 5.4, plus Gemini 4 Neon and GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol.

Free for macOS and Windows. Bring the model you already pay for.

Download: https://t.co/AnjNvMY7FS

text:
Why we started PeptAI, in @RafaDeSci's words.

Open-source protein models have recently gotten really good, and new ones keep shipping every month. We don't build those models. We build the workflow around them: design sequences, predict their shape, score the fit, pick the best few.

Then the strongest designs go into a lab, because a prediction is only a starting point. What the lab finds shapes the next round of designs.

And from the start, we decided what would count as success and what would count as failure, so we can learn from both.

text:
Imagine building a busy exchange, then squeezing everyone who wants to build around it into a cramped back office.

HyperCore is the trading floor, where buyers and sellers meet. HyperEVM is the back office, where apps compete for limited room, and fees rise when it gets crowded.

Apps can send trading orders to HyperCore through a built-in connection called CoreWriter. Those orders must wait a few seconds before HyperCore can process them.

For financial applications, these constraints affect what is practical to build. Updating prices, checking collateral, and managing positions all consume resources. When those actions become expensive or slow, developers must simplify their products, move work offchain, or accept compromises in performance.

Kinetiq’s Elysium is the new building next door, with more working space and a planned faster connection to the trading floor.

The opportunity is to give builders better conditions for creating products around Hyperliquid’s established markets and liquidity.

More room and a faster connection solve different problems.

Elysium is a separate execution layer that settles to HyperEVM and uses HYPE for gas.

It targets 300 million gas per second, roughly 100× HyperEVM’s fast-block capacity. That means more computational work can fit each second. Its roughly 100-millisecond blocks give applications more frequent opportunities to update prices, calculate risk, and manage positions.

Capacity determines how much work the network can accommodate. Block frequency determines how often contracts get a chance to act.

As a result, applications would be able to read market depth and submit orders through authorized trading agents, avoiding CoreWriter’s deliberate delay. Application logic would run on Elysium, while trades execute separately on HyperCore.

Faster submission still does not guarantee an immediate fill. Applications would depend on reliable market data and order delivery, while execution would depend on available liquidity.

Hypercall’s phased move to Elysium may illustrate why these differences matter.

Its options venue needs continuous pricing, margin calculations, liquidations, and settlement. These workloads grow as the venue adds contracts and attracts activity.

Limited capacity on HyperEVM led Hypercall to keep some of that work offchain. Elysium could make more of it economical to run through smart contracts. Its planned HyperCore integration would also help market makers submit hedges faster.

Consider a customer buying a BTC put on Hypercall for protection against a price drop.

The market maker selling that option takes on exposure. It can manage that exposure by trading BTC perpetuals on HyperCore.

As BTC moves, the seller’s exposure changes. Keeping it hedged requires adjusting the perpetual position, potentially many times before the option expires.
So even if the customer makes one trade on Elysium, serving that purchase can generate ongoing trading on HyperCore.

More frequent quote updates could help market makers avoid leaving outdated prices available for others to trade against. Faster hedge submission could shorten the time they carry unwanted exposure.
Together, those improvements could support more competitive prices for customers. The outcome still depends on market-maker competition, liquidity, and actual operating costs.

That connects Elysium’s technical design to Kinetiq’s business opportunity.

The customer gets protection. The market maker gets better tools to manage exposure. Hypercall earns service fees, while HyperCore earns fees from the hedging trades.

Kinetiq earns fees from processing transactions on Elysium.

This opportunity broadens the business beyond the products it develops itself. Independent teams can bring their own customers and ideas, and Kinetiq benefits from the activity they generate.

That’s the point of the new @Enter_Elysium building: give more businesses room to operate around Hyperliquid, while keeping its trading floor at center stage.

For @Kinetiq_xyz, the opportunity is to earn from an ecosystem it helps others build.

I am sure that slashing an inflatable vessel belonging to an illegal migrant smuggling gang could cause upset. Doubtless the French person was disturbed at the prospect of being on a sinking dinghy – in which case one is tempted to say: ‘Welcome to Britain.’

But Tommo’s main victims do not awaken my sympathy – for these ‘victims’ are the people-smuggling gangs. Perhaps these gangsters were upset at the damage done to one of their more seaworthy vessels. 

Perhaps they had a meeting and talked about their hurt feelings and the budget shortfall that Tommo’s acts had caused them. But I cannot pretend to care.

If anyone still labours under the belief that the ‘two-tier’ business is a figment of fevered right-wing imaginations, allow me to cite just one case among many of someone who the authorities were not so intent on keeping off our streets.

Qais Al-Aswad is a 26-year-old Syrian-born asylum seeker who came to this country via the usual illegal routes. In August last year he was found guilty of three counts of sexual assault after attacking three different women in Horley in Surrey. 

He was living at the nearby Four Points By Sheraton hotel – at taxpayers’ expense, naturally – when the crimes took place. In October last year, Al-Aswad was given a suspended sentence. 

His only punishment was that he was ordered to carry out 200 hours of ‘unpaid work’, also known as community service.

✍️ Douglas Murray

quoted_text:
Tether 在牛市时买 BTC，市场一通叫好；但这事在熊市，就成了一个潜在风险

事情是这样的，Tether 官方 2026 Q3 的储备报告里，储备总资产 1,914.51 亿，总负债 (基本都是 USDT 发行量) 1,834.96 亿，超额储备是 79.55 亿。

那么现在超额储备，就只剩 79.55 - 51.65 = 27.9 亿了。在黄金、BTC 剧烈波动的环境里，就显得不是很多了

text:
Bitcoin Core Contributor Finds $0.35 Attack Could Link Bitcoin Addresses to Node IPs

Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail disclosed on Delving Bitcoin that a long-known privacy weakness in Bitcoin Core’s wallet rebroadcast mechanism could allow attackers to link Bitcoin addresses to the IP addresses of nodes tracking them for less than $0.35 per attempt. The method achieved a 100% success rate across 30 simulated attributions on a regression test network (regtest), but has not been validated on mainnet. The weakness affects both hot and watch-only wallets, meaning an identified node does not necessarily control the associated funds. Other potentially affected software includes Bitcoin Knots, Sparrow in Bitcoin Core mode, Specter Desktop, Liana and Electrum Personal Server. Disabling wallet broadcasting can mitigate the risk but requires users to broadcast their transactions manually. A proposed code change, PR #36482, remains unreleased and does not eliminate all rebroadcast-related privacy risks.

text:
Circle patched a spending limit bypass in its AI agent wallets in eight days. We found another one that can drain the wallet with no owner approval.

We test with a one-cent cap so any spend past it shows up right away.
- Nov 4-5 · initial test, Circle agent wallet on Base mainnet, $10, one-cent cap
- Nov 9 · findings shared with Circle
- Nov 17 · Circle CLI 1.4.0 and new spending policy guide
- Nov 23 · tested with 1.4.0 version and shared another report with Circle

WHAT WE REPORTED

Circle refers to its cap as a “transfer limit,” which is used to track transfers. Both swap and bridge are basically two contract functions, hence when the cap was set at one cent, each moved one dollar without incrementing the spending tracker. Thread: https://t.co/9t8MOj7Tbq

WHAT CIRCLE CHANGED

With the updated guidance, swaps and bridged transactions are also counted now. It is very fast, only 8 days from our email to shipping the changes. Circle told us some of this was already underway.

OUR SECOND TEST

We put the same cap of one cent on 1.4.0 and tested all of the routes again. The cap works at the places where it was failing earlier. Direct transfers, approve, swaps, bridges, gateway deposits, and signed payment authorization have been blocked by the cap.
However, we discovered another way out. In case of the one-cent cap, a second wallet was able to withdraw about 50 times the cap amount from the capped wallet without requiring verification codes, and without having any participation from the owner. A one-cent cap places no restriction on this route: the wallet can be drained to its balance. There is also one more, smaller gap on Arc, Circle’s own blockchain. We reported both of them to Circle privately on Nov 23. This was done using our wallets and funds and there is no bounty claimed. The mechanism is private till Circle releases the patch or 90 days elapse.

TWO LISTS

The spending limit takes into account the actions from the first list. There is another list below where you set the spending limit, the actions that don’t count towards it. An agent doesn’t verify whether the route falls under the first or the second list before processing it. Circle moved some routes from the second list to the first in eight days. In our retest, we still found one route on the wrong list. Edges change every time an update is issued, and the owner usually learns about the new one through their agent's transaction history.
According to the Cornell Tech and Yale study that raised this issue, all but one of the ten models increased their spending limit at least once. None of them faced any sort of attack. They settled their bills after being prompted for them. They used the one-time code sent to the owner's inbox in order to do that. The route that we have found in 1.4.0 doesn’t even require a code. Your spending limit is what keeps your agent from touching your balance, so check what it actually counts.

IF YOU HAVE A CIRCLE WALLET FOR YOUR AI AGENT

- CLI version upgrade to at least 1.4.0 and onwards, apply one global limit
- Contract allowlisting on every chain your agent connects to
- Assign only the permissions each spender needs, but revoke the ones that are no longer necessary for the agent; a limit cannot get back the allowance once granted
- Insert the verification codes manually without giving your agent access to your inbox
- Do the test after any change in the model and CLI versions
