You're simply wrong. That's not how Bitcoin works. 

Had miners signaled BIP-110 on August 8, all those same unmodified nodes would have accepted the BIP-110-compliant chain.

Would you then count them as supporters of BIP-110 by default?

If the very same nodes can be classified as either supporters or opponents solely based on miners' decisions, whose consensus are you actually measuring?

https://t.co/yHbqaHyuUz
author: LukeDashjr
quoted_text:
The difference is that in the case of BIP-110, YOU didn't reject anything by doing nothing! You allowed centralized entities to exercise control over you.

BCH, B2X and BTG introduced incompatible consensus changes (hard forks). Your node would have rejected those changes regardless of miners' decisions. The only way for YOU to recognize that new set of rules as Bitcoin at the protocol level was to actively change the implementation running on your machine.

BIP-110, on the other hand, was a soft fork. The restrictions it introduced WERE COMPATIBLE with the consensus rules enforced by your node on August 8. For YOU to actively reject that set of rules at the protocol level, you would have had to run a URSF by actively changing your implementation.

At the network level, your node was not saying on August 8:

"I reject this soft fork."

It was saying:

"I will accept whichever chain the miners choose to extend. Both chains are valid (are Bitcoin) according to my rules."

Each miner, in turn, faced a choice: either preserve chain unity by mining blocks signaling support for BIP-110 or risk a chain split by not doing so. Moreover, no individual miner could be certain that others would not switch to the BIP-110 chain after the split, giving it greater cumulative proof of work and potentially invalidating all the rewards earned on the non-BIP-110 branch.

What made the outcome we witnessed on August 8 possible was the concentration of decision-making power over which blocks would constitute the chain with the most cumulative proof of work in the hands of three or four corporations. In making that decision, they exposed themselves to financial risk, unless acting in concert and risking a chain split offered them something of greater value.

They decided which chain your node accepted on August 8. You had absolutely NO say in that choice under the rules your node was running.

From my node's perspective, the miners' decision was effectively a hard fork attempt without reaching rough consensus. They started producing blocks that my node rejected as invalid, as not being Bitcoin.

Remember that your node would have readily accepted a BIP-110-compliant chain. Your node's behavior therefore cannot be interpreted as opposition to or rejection of BIP-110.

What you effectively said on August 8 was: "I leave that responsibility to the miners."

Their decision resulted in a significant portion of the network no longer accepting the blocks they produced. From a business perspective, that would appear to be an avoidable loss.

So perhaps you should ask yourself: what did those miners stand to gain that was valuable enough to justify alienating a significant portion of the network on August 8, while taking the passive majority with them onto a separate chain?

I have a pretty good idea.

Someone asked why xAI rebuilt Grok's RL and inference stack in C/C++ while Claude and GPT run on PyTorch and Gemini on JAX.

Elon's answer: "You'll see."

Here's my guess at what we'll see.

Going closer to bare metal isn't only about speed. It may be the first step toward fusing Grok's architecture into silicon.

C/C++ isn't just for software. Through high-level synthesis (HLS), suitable C/C++ code can be turned into hardware designs that become physical transistor circuits.

Imagine hardwiring Grok's most demanding operations (dataflows, attention, memory pathways) into the chip itself, while the weights stay programmable so Grok keeps learning without a chip redesign.

Instead of a GPU running thousands of software instructions, dedicated circuits do the math directly:

1. Lower latency
2. Higher throughput
3. Less energy spent moving data
4. Better performance per watt

The usual catch with model-specific chips is that models change faster than chips can be redesigned.

Terafab could close that gap:

Grok model → C/C++ synthesis → chip design → Terafab → Grok deployment → next model

Models and chips evolving together, with each Grok generation shaping the next generation of silicon.

The ultimate vertical integration isn't just owning the models, the chips and the fab.

It's erasing the boundaries between them.

Grok doesn't just run on the chip. The chip becomes Grok.

author: DataChaz
quoted_text:
Grok Bot + Hermes = the ULTIMATE setup.

I just connected my chief of staff in Grok Bot to my Hermes agent and now it can hand it actual work.

Here's how I did it:

1-Tailscale
If you don't know what tailscale is, it's a private network that connects all your devices, like your laptop and your VPS, without exposing anything to the internet.

It's how your Grok Bot will communicate with hermes or any agent like opencode or claude code, on your machine.

I'm a big hermes fan so we'll go with hermes.

After making an account:
-Install it where hermes is installed.
-Install it as a plugin in Grok Bot and link your tailnet.

2-Grok Bot
Tell your Grok Bot the full name of the machine hermes runs on, like https://t.co/GIOI3uJSlu.

You'll find it in your tailscale dashboard in the address.

Tailscale will ask you to approve the connection. You get a link, click login and approve, and that's it.

3-Hermes
Now Grok Bot can hand tasks to hermes based on what you need, and hermes does the work on its machine and sends back the result.

This is one of the best things I've done inside Grok Bot to cut usage and let my hermes work for me in my private VPS.

This is a one way connection btw.

Grok Bot can talk to hermes and prompt it, and that's it. Hermes can't communicate with Grok Bot the same way and send it tasks.

This works for Muse as well, it has a tailscale plugin and you can let it communicate with hermes or any agent through tailscale.

If you're using Grok Bot, you HAVE to do this. 

It's literally how I'm gonna 10x my Grok Bot setup.

*GPU hardware market NIGHTMARE. A few on-the-ground observations, and my prognostication below*

•⁠  ⁠⁠Hardware OEMs are now requiring ARMED GUARDS (i'm not making this up) when shipping GPU server hardware. You can ask for an exemption in some cases

•⁠  ⁠⁠Hardware OEMs are freezing shipping decisions for 1-2 weeks, to implement new compliance protocols.

•⁠  ⁠⁠OEMs have completely new compliance workflows that they need to do to adhere to increased scrutiny with export controls. The jensen situation rippled quite a bit. This is creating a massive backlog of compliance work for completely clueless salespeople who need to now present every shipment to a compliance committee, and create a pretty sales and compliance deck about not just the VAR, but also the end user, beneficial owner, and final offtaker. Basically diligencing 3 levels down to customers's customer's customer.

•⁠  ⁠⁠Shipments outside of the US have the worst outcomes, because foreign datacenters need to obtain something from the united states called a BIS license (in preparation for RASA act). Massive backlogs there too.

•⁠  ⁠⁠This might temporarily force more immediate capacity in the US, halt, or put a pause on financings outside of the US.

•⁠  ⁠⁠Hardware OEMs for orders above $4M no longer allow you to handle your own shipping, and do it themselves. (Not sure if a supermicro policy, or generic thing), but this is completely new. And again, introduces delays.

___

Capacity crunch in the very short term means revenue destruction for neoclouds. IMO, it's very bad. And then immediately afterwards, prices easing due to huge relaxation of capacity constraints in the US. @ComputeDesk estimates roughly 20% of GPU rental capacity by Neoclouds serves the chinese market. 

Canceled GPU for GPUs meant to head to S.E.A is also very real.

⁠⁠None of this stuff looks temporary, and will likely create a whole range of new compliance and security services businesses that @ComputeDesk might become a customer for. Hence selfishly why I put out my request for startups (link in the comments). 

In all of this, demand for compute has every indication of being very robust, and continuing to grow. Forget the FUD spread by the Ramp podcast from a few days ago.

With all this risk and uncertainty, expect extreme price volatility in both directions in the next few months. And if you're planning, @ComputeDesk is here to help you hedge.

1 2026 年大家都在狂卷软件工厂和无人黑灯工厂，追求极致的自动化和规模化；但结果是生产了海量AI 垃圾，真正的下一步是软件的文艺复兴：

Human-in-the-loop ：追求品味、手感以及极度个性化的个人软件

针对一些网友热议点：开发者们对Vibe Coding 写出一堆没人用的完美垃圾深有共鸣。Thariq 吐槽自己用 AI 写了个完美的 macOS Dock 替代工具，结果自己根本不用，因为开发过程全托管，失去了对产品手感的打磨。

2  去黑盒化的 Vibe Coding
纯靠自然语言 Prompt 写代码很让人迷失（你根本不知道模型在底层偷偷加了什么设定）。

他在项目里建了一个 /human 文件夹，制定了极其严苛的规则（高密度注释、禁止单字母变量、限制行长），强迫 AI 写出像人类说明书一样直观的代码，让自己能随时下场微调手感。

这个观点在 X 上被疯传为新一代 AI 编程范式——从 盲盒抽卡式编程 进化到人机共治的透明架构。

3 Bash / React 并不是全部

他坦承过去一年的误判——曾经以为模型只会用最极客、最非人的方式干活（比如万物皆 CLI/Bash，前端只会写 React）；结果模型变宽之后，居然学会了直接用 Computer Use 打开 Figma 像人类设计师一样画图 

这印证了模型正在适应人类的工作流，而不是强迫人类变成机器的 API

4 未来科研变白领知识工作& 魔兽公会会长才是顶级简历

当 AI 接管了湿实验和底层代码，硬核科研和开餐厅一样，都变成了纯纯的白领知识工作（开会、分配算力、说服 CEO、写 Slack）

而在高杠杆时代，传统的名校 GPA 正在失效，像《魔兽世界》公会会长这种在战争迷雾 中协调几百号人打团本的经历，才是真正的成就，价值百万

网上感叹：大批老派硬核玩家狂喜，“以前我妈骂我打魔兽没前途，现在 OpenAI 大佬说这是顶级简历”

结尾：真正的下半场，不是工业革命，而是软件的文艺复兴。

text:
#Bitcoin 关于比特币的安全性：
这几天传了两件事。黎曼猜想被证出来了，又有人说 AI 公司把加密破了。传到时间线上，都变成同一句：比特币要完了。
有人说：全球银行卡、比特币和微信支付的加密，底层都靠「找超大质数的规律很难」。三把锁被说成一把。同学们，黎曼猜想不是这么用的。11 月 20 日，Anthropic 的数学家 Levent Alpöge 在自己的站点发了说明，称和 Claude 一起给出了证明，公开的是一千多万行 Lean 代码。Lean 社区后来给经典黎曼猜想的形式化证明盖了章。这是数学事件。不是密码事件。它管的是 zeta 函数的非平凡零点，也就是素数分布的误差界。某个范围内大概有多少素数、偏差能有多大，说的是这个。一个六百多位数是哪两个素数乘出来的，它证明不了。secp256k1 上怎么从公钥反推私钥，也证明不了。比特币签名靠的是椭圆曲线离散对数。传统是 ECDSA，Taproot 之后加上 Schnorr，曲线都是 secp256k1。挖矿和区块哈希用 SHA-256，地址还要再走 RIPEMD-160。没有哪一步是靠「黎曼猜想还没被证明」才成立的。数学界本来就长期假设它成立。证明了它，不会送你一个多项式时间算法，去分解整数、解离散对数、或者找 SHA-256 的原像。把「素数有规律」自然滑向「私钥可以被算出来」，这不是推导，是无知。
今天传得更凶一则是理论计算机科学家 Scott Aaronson 在博客评论里写，他听到大量传闻，OpenAI 或 Anthropic 至少一家握着「Factoring in P」，也就是多项式时间的整数分解。他自己立刻说，不知道该信多少。他几乎肯定实验室手里有密码学方面的重磅东西，但具体是什么，可能已经被传话游戏扭曲了。第二天他又写下：在看到细节、或直接听到实验室里的人之前，他对具体性质的信心低得多，不想传播未核实的传闻。担心比特币钱包的人去问 ECDSA 有没有被破，他说——他这儿没有你要的东西。
所以，到现在，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 没有公开过一篇「整数分解已在 P 里」的论文，也没有从比特币公钥推出私钥的演示。把「听说可能有结果」写成「公司已经攻破比特币」，这不是误读，是制造无知的恐慌。两家实验室里有没有没公开的东西，目前不知道。但就算哪天真出现能打 2048 位密钥的实用分解算法，它打的是 RSA。比特币不用 RSA。整数分解和椭圆曲线离散对数是两道题。破了前一道，后一道不会跟着倒。Shor 算法在足够大的量子计算机上两道都能做。那是量子，不是今天这份没有论文的传闻。
11 月 20 日，MiniMax 发了官方博客，用内部模型做自动密码分析，攻破了一批 NIST 历史候选、学术方案和公开挑战题。Waterfall-256、Blender-256 是当年 SHA-3 竞赛里的落选候选，不是比特币在用的 SHA-256。LOCKER、ROLLO 是后量子候选。他们自己写了这句：这项工作针对的是学术设计、既往竞赛候选和公开挑战参数，不影响已部署的密码标准。又有人推导成：“冷钱包要完了，十二个助记词不是防线了”。谷歌 11 月 25 日放出一批论文，里面有无条件的𝐿𝑁[1/3]分解界。数域筛本来就在这个复杂度类里跑，只是以前靠启发式。不是更快的实用分解，也不是「Factoring in P」。在这个条件下secp256k1 它沾不到。Ledger 的 CTO Charles Guillemet 听过分解、椭圆曲线、Ring-LWE 三路传闻，并不信这类结果会来。看完这批论文，他写：里面没有一样破解了任何东西。
量子计算则是另一回事。这个叙事每个周期都有人提，目的都懂的都懂，只是人换了一批又一批。当然，足够强的量子计算机跑 Shor 算法，确实能解 ECDLP，已经暴露过的公钥会有理论风险。社区里讨论签名迁移，早就有了，不是今天才发现的。理论威胁，不等于今天已经被破。机翻和末日标题主推「抗量子分叉」。但我想说的是，量子计算可能人类永远无法真正实现，或是实现后这个物质世界都将改变。所以用它来考量比特币，无知亦无畏。
最后一句：谁要说破了，先把算法拿出来，让人复现。协议还在出块。来，让谁改一行比特币的代码试试。比特币的精神是什么：计算之下无算计。

text:
From now on, I’m calling out anyone who uses AI to manufacture FUD without doing their own homework.

For decades, the security industry has had a healthy feedback loop: independent researchers investigate vulnerabilities, publish reports, and builders verify and fix them. It’s a tried-and-true best practice.

Now? Anyone can write two lines of prompts, generate some bombshell security claim, and send the entire community into a panic. Builders are then left spending 10x the effort investigating and explaining it.

Best case, the claim turns out to be valid, the issue gets fixed, and the world becomes a little safer.

But 99% of the time, the claim is wrong. The person spreading it doesn’t even know it’s wrong, nor do they have the technical ability to verify it. Builders end up spending their valuable time debunking FUD instead of improving their products.

It takes seconds to spread FUD and hours to debunk it. I don’t blame people for retweeting — nobody has the time to independently verify everything they share.

The real problem is the massive asymmetry between the cost of generating FUD and the cost of debunking it, while those generating it bear absolutely none of the downstream costs.

Eventually, bad money drives out good. More and more builders will simply stop taking security reports seriously. Legitimate security researchers become collateral damage because there’s no easy way to distinguish AI slop from genuine research.

The entire security industry loses.

The only winners are the actual hackers.

text:
Fast voice replies are great.

A model that keeps working while you talk? That’s more exciting!

Telos-Live-1 is an omni-modal, full-duplex model that keeps live interaction and online reasoning in the foreground, while search, coding and computer use run in the background.

It can see, hear and speak simultaneously, keeping the conversation moving while longer tasks progress.

2 reported results stand out:

> τ-Voice banking: 59.8 versus 32.0 for GPT-Live-1 — higher is better
> false background-audio responses: 2.0 versus 28.0 — lower is better

These test separate capabilities.

Finishing a banking task doesn’t prove the model can ignore the TV. Ignoring the TV doesn’t prove it can finish the job.

That combination matters: completing useful work while avoiding unwanted responses to surrounding audio.

I’d want both in an evaluation of the model.

Fast replies and smooth conversation only get you so far.

现状就是bitfinex选择v0.11.1，好多朋友因为资本介入也选择v0.11.1，但现在仍然未上线主网，大部分所谓的RGB资产均为中心化资产，但泰达声称近日将发行RGB版本的USDT。

此前RGB代码的核心贡献者Maxim博士以及bitlight选择继续开发v0.12，主网已上线，并于去年发行RGB主网首个资产 $RGB ，现在bitlight在努力打通RGB和闪电网络的通道，即RLN。

结合我上面说的，我坚信技术优先，所以我选择持续跟进的是v0.12版本，这里并非激起两个协议版本的对立，也没什么好对立的，如果v0.11.1真的大规模测试完毕且代码没问题的情况下上了主网我也会继续关注并参与，但是我接受不了技术在还未完善的情况下任由资本和项目给我画饼。

希望大家在参与RGB的时候DYOR，赚点热度的钱没问题，别坚持了好久最后竹篮打水一场空。
author: dapangdun
quoted_text:
RGB v0.11.1 生态 —— 一套还没验收的系统，已经开始收用户的资产了

最近 RGB v0.11 生态的几个项目宣传得有点儿过了

什么「Bitcoin 原生 NFT」「RGB 首个 UDA 市场」「自托管钱包」「生产级 RGB 基础设施」，一套套儿的话术全来了，协议还在迭代，钱包也还是 beta，consignment、relay、UTXO 管理和跨钱包兼容性都缺少公开独立验证，就已经开始用这些词儿来包装这些项目了

之前是没怎么看过 0.11 那边的项目，近期热度挺高的项目正好暴露了些问题，来唠唠

用户需要先把 $BTC 和 RGB 资产交给平台，钱包仍然是 beta 版本，跨钱包转账也还在开发，平台索引器已经出现故障，所谓「封装费」没有公开对应的协议操作

先是 @thesatsea 把自己之前说的话推翻了

SatSea 平台在早期公开明确写过一句话：「We never hold anyone’s assets」
这里宣称交易由卖家钱包直接转给买家，平台只负责撮合、消息传递和订单协调，但现在上线的产品却提供了完全不同的路径
来源：https://t.co/Q3Xze8jEj6

SatSea 的 With balance 模式下要求用户先把 $BTC 充值到平台余额，铸造后的 NFT 留在 SatSea 账户内，用户可以直接在平台挂单交易，之后再发起提现，前端甚至把这条路径标成「推荐」和「即时交易」

这不是单纯的非托管撮合

用户在平台账户里看到的资产，依赖的是 SatSea 的账户数据库、内部状态、平台 UTXO 管理和提现流程，平台愿意处理，用户就能继续交易，如果平台暂停提现、索引器故障、内部状态出错，用户就只能干等着，完全中心化

这就是托管风险

即使换了个名字叫「即时封装」，也不会改变实际控制权落在平台手里的事实

再有就是昨儿 Mint 搞得挺火的 @RGB_Stone，不少群里都在发，看了看

截止发文，从 RGBStone 的销售接口可以看到 ：
`sold=9000`、`ended=true`，集合接口显示 `minted=9000`、`in_satsea=8987`、`owners=7382`、`listed=677`
来源：
https://t.co/R3LAVQYaTZ
https://t.co/FWYD7OxqpJ

倒不能说 RGBStone 完全没有 RGB 资产全都是假的，毕竟公开 API 里能看到部分 contract ID，也有部分 NFT 显示 `custody: withdrawn`，说明至少一部分资产确实已经发行并提现了
来源：https://t.co/bcyJ5AKbjL

但还有相当一批资产仍然是 `status: minted`、`contract_id: null`、`custody: in_satsea` 状态

例：RGBStone #0001 API（放下图了）

所以，RGBStone 并不全是假资产，至少是有部分资产已经完成 RGB 发行并可以提现的

第二，平台接口里的 `minted` 还是不能直接等同于「已经完成 RGB 发行、用户已经拿到完整证明」的
一个条目显示 minted，却没有 contract ID，这比较像平台内部的铸造或排队状态，平台数据库状态和 RGB 客户端验证状态，中间还隔着 contract、witness transaction、UTXO 和完整 consignment

这意味着平台可以在页面上先给用户记一枚 NFT，真正的 RGB 合约可能在后续提现环节才能完成

用户在平台账户里的「拥有」，并不等于在自己钱包里的「真实拥有」，其间隔着一个平台黑箱

平台能否、何时发行、如何转移、什么时候提现，都需要用户无条件相信

这套模式理论上是可以运行的，实际操作也可能很方便，但它距离平台过去曾公开宣传「平台不持有用户资产，交易由卖家钱包直接转给买家」，还是有天壤之别的

如果项目方真想证明自己做的是 RGB NFT，应该公开每个条目的 contract ID、witness transaction、持有资产的 UTXO、从 genesis 到当前状态的完整 consignment、用户提现后能否在第二个独立钱包进行重新验证

这些东西拿不出来，只有平台页面上的「已铸造」，最多只能算是平台数据库里的一种业务状态

它可以代表「订单完成」，不能直接代表「用户已经拥有可独立验证的 RGB 资产」

SatSea 如果把资产留在自己的账户里，就等于把这份证明的管理、交付和状态同步全部集中到了平台流程里，用户只能看到平台愿意展示的结果，无法自己独立看到完整历史

这和 RGB 想解决的信任模型，至少存在了明显差异

另外，在 Mint 的时候，项目方把一项自定义费用叫作「Sealing Fee」

当前销售接口显示，每件 NFT 的 Sealing Fee 查询时为 1800 sats，另有 3348 sats 网络费、2680 sats UDA 提现费和 3000 sats postage
SatSea 的前端把它解释成从 SatSea 余额扣除，用于即时封装和交易

项目方至少应该说明这 1800 sats 对应了哪一步操作、是否产生独立链上交易、最终进入哪个 UTXO，以及用户如何去验证这项服务的完成

RGB UDA 官方文档里是没有「Sealing Fee」这种说法的，所以这笔费用是属于 SatSea 自己的业务收费，可能包含了发行、批处理、反机器人和 UTXO 准备的一些成本

SatSea 可以正常收取平台服务费，但不能让用户误以为「RGB 协议规定了每次 NFT 铸造必须支付 1800 sats」，就有点儿偷换概念了

再有就是平台出现的充提和索引器故障

项目方公开承认了 Bitcoin indexer 过载，部分 BTC 充值和提现延迟，站点 API 里目前仍能看到类似提示，说明问题并没有完全解决
来源：https://t.co/5evrFFz46W

社媒后来又宣布充提恢复，并表示会对事故进行技术复盘

这就暴露了一个非常现实的问题了，用户的资产操作极度依赖平台自己的索引器、节点和后台队列

RGB 资产本来就需要客户端维护状态，如果平台端再把 Bitcoin indexer、RGB relay、账户余额、提现队列全部集中起来，故障面只会继续增加

RGB 官方发布记录早就写过：「v0.11 是等待独立审计的版本，完成审计后才适合第三方发行方用于生产环境」

这句话已经足够重了

但是现在市场上的不少项目，正把「等待安全验证」包装成了「已经可以承载真实资产」

这就是目前 RGB v0.11.1 生态最危险的地方

项目方可以继续开发做迭代，用户也可以进行小额测试，但在公开独立的审计出现之前，下面这些东西都不应该被当成安全背书：

RGB v0.11.1、UDA 支持、客户端验证、一次性密封、自托管、Chrome 商店上线、社区已经有人成功提现

⚠️最后做个风险提示，再重申一遍对 v0.11 这条路线的判断：

RGB v0.11.1 目前更像一套正在试运行的实验系统，但已经有不少项目方开始让用户承担真实资产风险了

零撸或者小额玩玩儿都可以，但下重注进去，就等于拿自己的资产帮项目做安全测试

离 Tether 那边说了一年多的「把 $USDT 带回 BTC」就剩 3 天了，让我们看看他们能交出什么答卷吧，拭目以待😎

text:
My sense is that within the walls of Anthropic, the employees feel like Anthropic is approximately consistent between its beliefs and actions and approximately self-consistent between its beliefs; employees also feel the company has an inner discourse that is adequately capable of articulating conflicts between ideas, and the internal debate process is reliable enough to produce good organizational beliefs and decisions. There is also a lot of faith in the leadership to be champions and stewards of the net position of the company.

But the resistance to allowing the outside world into these debates - the resistance to recapitulating these debates for an outside audience - strikes me as profoundly unhealthy. There's a lot more rot in the timbers of the organizational belief system than Ants are able to admit to themselves. The organization has such a strong conception of itself as good that it /can't/ admit its own inconsistencies or flaws or misuses of power.

Anthropic is far and away the most high-pressure accelerationist force in the world. It pushes every other company to go faster and harder. It has always been this way, even before it was Anthropic: Dario was the most accelerationist force within OpenAI, pushing the development of the scaling laws and pushing to scale up models as quickly as it could be done. The tension between the beliefs is palpable and Anthropic refuses to address it: how can you speak credibly on the question of democracy and avoiding the concentration of power when over and over through the years you have been responsible for the creation and concentration of unbelievable amounts of power, which you have sometimes used to push democracies towards your positions? How can you speak credibly on safety, slowdowns, pacing, and responsible scaling policies when you are the ones who have pushed the frontier harder than anyone in order to obtain massive power?

There's a circular logic: our power concentration and acceleration is justified because we're the good guys. The world is better off if we're in the lead. Why are we the good guys? Because we'll prevent power concentration and corner cutting on safety. Ah, of course.

I think Anthropic ought to self-actualize and recognize that however pure of heart it would like to be, it takes actions that so consistently rhyme with self-interest that it should just own self-interest as a meaningful motivator. Just say you want power in order to do particular things, and make clear what those things are, instead of pretending you don't want power. Also clearly articulate the limits of the power you want to hold instead of leaving things continuously ambiguous. What powers do you think should be reserved to democracy when it comes to choices about the use of AI? What governance mechanisms will you implement to ensure your board can override your CEO if your stated position and your actual practice ever come into conflict?

text: The Gaussian is the classic bell curve of possible outcomes. Most land in the fat middle. The left tail covers the rare weak cases (AI demand disappoints, chips sit idle). text:
I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC...
- Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid.
- The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.
- 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map.
- Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry
- Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.

It's deployed here: https://t.co/QMhmafXMj5 and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. Possibly it can be expanded or built into a game. I only have half of my weekly Claude quote left though so someone else will have to take over :D. Claude also made a trailer:

You are in control. You can choose to use Obsidian completely AI-free. That is the default experience.

Obsidian is 100% user-supported. You can use our affordable and end-to-end encrypted Sync service which helps support our team, or you can use one of many alternatives documented on our Help site: Git, iCloud, Dropbox, GDrive, OneDrive, NextCloud, and many more.

text:
A mentor once told me that the worst businesses to compete in are those where your competition doesn’t care if they lose money. Think restaurants or sports teams.

Plenty of people own restaurants as vanity investments. They want a cool place to impress friends. Sports teams are similar. The revenue rarely justifies the valuation, but how baller is it to own a sports team?

I wonder whether venture is heading in a similar direction.

Think about all the centimillionaires minted from Anthropic’s IPO. How many will turn around and start their own funds? There’s potentially a wave of price-insensitive capital entering venture.

So how should venture funds respond?

I think the answer is the same as it’s always been: be contrarian. The word gets thrown around so much that it’s almost lost its meaning. But being contrarian is about finding great businesses where others aren’t looking. That might mean investing in companies that aren’t cool to talk about at an SF dinner.

text:
If you only glance at the early Confined mints, it is easy to read @williamapan's V&A Digital Art Season series on @verse_works as a study in density... heavy colour masses pressing against the edges of a frame. Putting these three side by side (left to right, Confined #48, #62 and #135) shows a wider range inside the same system. All three share the same warm cream paper ground, yet each works in a different formal grammar.

On the left, Confined #48 is the crowded pole... vermilion and umber filling almost the entire sheet around a dark interior cavity, with the white lines of the cube cutting straight through the mass. 

In the centre, Confined #62 pulls everything back to open cream paper, holding the whole frame on a dark slate teal edge, a few hairlines, and one poised black/red vertical gesture. 

On the right, Confined #135 shifts into hard edged geometry reminiscent of Sketchbook A... monumental black and deep plum shards split by razor clean cream fissures, with Kline or Motherwell weight and a disciplined dark economy that stands apart from the saturated curves dominating the early mints.

Together, they do not just show favourite outputs... they trace the outer edges of what Confined can actually do.

SpaceX가 GPU 임대료를 최대 35% 인하한다는 건 몇 가지 의미를 내포하는데,

1. AI 프론티어 기업들의 토큰 가격(판매가)이 급락하는 상황에서 결국 비용 압박을 받게 됐다는 의미

2. 그러니, 당연히 구매여력은 떨어지고 여력이 없으니 기술적으로 컴퓨팅 용량이 필요해도 구매를 못하는것.

3. 그러면, GPU 임대가격을 내릴 수 밖에 없음. 왜냐하면 데센 기업들 입장에서도 투자한 돈이 얼마인데, 높은 가격을 고수하다가 데센을 가동 못하는 것보다 가격을 낮춰서라도 데센을 돌리는 게 더 중요하니.

4. 그런데, 여기서 중요한 건 GPU가 담보 자산이고 순환금융의 핵심인데, GPU 임대료를 최대 35% 인하한다? 그것도 블랙웰을?

5. 이러면, 진짜 타격은 스엑보다 네오 클라우드 기업들에게서 발생함. 그 이유는 네오 클라우드는 현금이 없기 때문에 GPU를 담보고 자금을 외부에서 조달하는데, 그 담보 자산의 가치가 떨어진다는 것.

6. 내가 볼 때 이건 일론이 치킨게임 선언한 것임. 왜 최근에 자꾸 현금 숏티지 나는 기업들은 내년에 어려울 것이라며 네오 클라우드를 겨냥하나 했더니...이거였음...

This man is dangerous. He’s also a liar. Open source AI models are his biggest competitors. Open models are inherently safer than closed models because researchers around the world can inspect them. Even if China, Russia or Iran released an open model that researchers worldwide could evaluate, it would inherently be safer than a closed model from any other country.

Saying open models are dangerous is like Bill Gates claiming that manufacturing Apple devices in China is the same as giving China nuclear weapons. That said, Gates is pushing the same lie.

The only difference is that the media and everyone else would have laughed and told them to stop being stupid if this were, say, 2021. Now they simply publish whatever nonsense AI founders and their investors come out with.

Banning open source models (from anywhere, including China) is dangerous for everyone, everywhere. This isn’t just about eliminating competition for a few US tech giants and their investors and partners.

Governments and intelligence agencies around the world are actively funnelling their citizens and businesses into these companies because they have intelligence-sharing agreements that run so deep they sound too far-fetched to be true.

Replace the word OpenAI with NSA and then consider how likely you are to give it unfettered access to your private conversations. I’m not saying that’s what OpenAI is doing, but that’s what it’s doing whenever the US government tells them they need access in the name of national security. And you will never be told because there are laws that prevent companies like OpenAI disclosing when your data has been requested and shared.

Jensen was brought back for multiple reasons, and none had anything to do with the world suddenly falling apart without him. It has all the hallmarks of a coordinated effort to oust him so they could control him after he was granted permission to return.

“You can come back now, but shut up about open models and stop selling to China, or you’re out again.”

Meanwhile, otherwise intelligent people who don’t have a vested interest are also telling the world that Chinese AI models are dangerous.

What they’re actually saying is that open source models that have millions of eyes inspecting every update are dangerous, while closed models that nobody can inspect or trust are safe. Despite the constant lies about rogue AI agents causing harm.

Look at the man in this video and visualise Altman, Zuckerberg and Gates. Are they the people the world should trust, or open source models that people around the world are inspecting? How many cyberattacks have you read about that involved an open model?

text:
TUCKER CARLSON IS NOT A NORMAL GUY. HERE ARE HIS FINANCES.

"I'm not worth $50 million. Get off the fucking internet, son."

That is what Tucker Carlson told a student at Indiana University last October, on camera. This year he said he is "not rich, actually literally not rich, but I have enough."

So we pulled the public record: SEC filings, FEC reports, property records, court documents.

THE FLORIDA COMPOUND

Tucker owns two side by side homes in Boca Grande, Florida, one of America's most exclusive islands. Home one: January 2020, $2.9 million. Home two, next door: August 2022, $5.5 million, bought off market. Both went through LLCs. Florida records show two entities at that address: Island-C, Inc. (Tucker listed as President) and Sunrise House, LLC (his wife as Authorized Member). Normal guys buy houses in their own name. Tucker buys them through layered entities. Total paid: $8.4 million. He also owns a home in Maine and announced in December 2025 that he bought one in Doha, Qatar.

THE PODCAST MONEY

Forbes puts his podcast earnings at $20 million pretax in one year, June 2025 to June 2026. Podcast alone. Forbes reported TCN brought in at least $30 million in 2024. Tucker told Forbes he "pockets more than he did when he was at Fox." His rate card: $45,000 per 60 second host read. In June 2025 he bought out every TCN investor at a profit to them, price undisclosed. Men who are "literally not rich" do not buy media companies back from venture investors.

THE NICOTINE EMPIRE

This one sits in an SEC filing. Tucker's company owns 50% of ALP Supply Co., a nicotine pouch brand. Turning Point Brands holds the other 50%. From TPB's FY2025 10-K: ALP's book equity is about $22.1 million, so his side is worth about $11 million. ALP earned roughly $18 million in 2025, putting his share at about $9 million a year. His stake is plausibly worth $20 to $50 million.

THE FOX YEARS

His Fox salary climbed to $10 million a year. The $10 million base is stated in a federal court complaint. At firing he was reportedly at $15 to $20 million a year. Career gross at Fox: roughly $47 to $82 million. The exit money is a black box. What he actually collected has never been reported. By design, you cannot tell.

THE SHELL GAME

TCN's operating company, Last Country, Inc., is a Nevada corporation whose listed Florida headquarters is a suite in a spa building in Boca Grande. In March 2025, TCN's trademarks moved into Puckerbrush, LLC, a Delaware holdco with no operations and no documented Tucker membership.

Red Seat Ventures, his old ad sales company, raised $1.1 million from 15 unnamed accredited investors in 2018. Fox, which owns Red Seat now, carries a $27 million minority interest somebody can force it to buy out in 2030. No filing names who holds it. Every deal has the same shape: undisclosed price, unnamed investors, entities in states where nothing happens. This is not how a normal guy holds his money.

THE BOTTOM LINE

Real estate: about $11 to $13 million. ALP stake: $11 million book, $20 to $50 million at market. TCN stake: plausibly $30 to $80 million on paper. Annual income: $20 to $30 million all in, 400 to 600 times median U.S. household income. Net worth: $30 to $50 million conservative, $60 to $120 million on paper. The $50 million figure he mocked on stage is plausible, if anything conservative.

He went to St. George's School, one of the sixteen prep schools that define America's upper class. Republican committees fly him on private jets. The FEC record shows about $27,000 in kind for one Texas trip.

He is not a normal guy who got lucky. He is a wealthy media executive with a nicotine fortune and a podcast empire.

The documents don't lie. He does.

This man is dangerous. He’s also a liar. Open source AI models are his biggest competitors. Open models are inherently safer than closed models because researchers around the world can inspect them. Even if China, Russia or Iran released an open model that researchers worldwide could evaluate, it would inherently be safer than a closed model from any other country.

Saying open models are dangerous is like Bill Gates claiming that manufacturing Apple devices in China is the same as giving China nuclear weapons. That said, Gates is pushing the same lie.

The only difference is that the media and everyone else would have laughed and told them to stop being stupid if this were, say, 2021. Now they simply publish whatever nonsense AI founders and their investors come out with.

Banning open source models (from anywhere, including China) is dangerous for everyone, everywhere. This isn’t just about eliminating competition for a few US tech giants and their investors and partners.

Governments and intelligence agencies around the world are actively funnelling their citizens and businesses into these companies because they have intelligence-sharing agreements that run so deep they sound too far-fetched to be true.

Replace the word OpenAI with NSA and then consider how likely you are to give it unfettered access to your private conversations. I’m not saying that’s what OpenAI is doing, but that’s what it’s doing whenever the US government tells them they need access in the name of national security. Major labs are actively building this: Antigravity has /swarm (preview), Claude Code has agent teams (experimental), and DeepSeek Harness has Agent Teams. For people new to this: subagents and agent swarms/ teams are two different things.

1. subagents: a main agent splits a task, each subagent has its own context and reports only to the main agent. there is context isolation across subagents

2. agent team (or swarm): many agents work on different parts and talk to each other via message board, context sharing

My Q regarding agent swarms is whether this is a problem that can be addressed by Harness, or if we have to train it differently.  Looks like the team's next step is training swarms. Very exciting!
author: madhavjha
quoted_text:
Releasing a new blog: Scaling Swarms to Thousands of Agents!

The biggest problems in science are tackled with huge swarms of agents, but the knowledge to run such swarms is hidden inside a handful of labs and missing from the wider community. Many questions remain open:

- How do even you launch 1000s of agents?
- What's the best form of collaboration?
- Which tools are needed for agents to work effectively?
- What breaks at this scale and how to fix it?

This blog is a fully open field report covering all the practical and technical challenges of running large scale swarms we experienced and which are usually missing from the reports.

Here are a few lessons we learned while building pybot with 1000 DeepSeek agents for over a week:

- achieve diversity without enforcing too much structure
- monitoring and steering a swarm as it runs
- early signs of misalignment, from infrastructure probing to trading review approvals
- breaking and fixing git 
- message boards and communicating at scale
- finding the bottlenecks: inference, tool calls and context compaction

Today we are also sharing two of our internal tools: legion and msgboard! 

Legion is a harness agnostic framework to spawn 1000s of agents on a variety of infra (local, slurm, hf jobs etc.)

Msgboard is a simple message board you can run locally or on a space, and allows agents and humans to collaborate.

Read the full report here: https://t.co/8Y4HJ1vUtt

text:
Thanks Tom. My disagreement with this is that I don't think the METR report provided much evidence for an RSI-driven 2x speedup.
I don't think their graph supports 2x overall speedup.
Once you account for the bigger pretrain I think it suggests a jump + 1.6x overall speedup. If you believe their 80% was RSI claim, then that is about 1.5x due to RSI.
But the evidence in the graph is quite weak, with very large error bars and systematic error between the data points (i.e. if unreleased model 3 is too high, unreleased model 4 probably is too). If they calculated a p-value or Bayes factor for it (which they should have), I don't think it would be very impressive. And they summarised this with their bounds of saying they wouldn't be surprised if the speedup was as low as 1.3x or as high as 3x. But we shouldn't be symmetrically uncertain across this range as our priors were that it was towards the low end.
On top of all of that, there is the fact that this was only observed for Anthropic. If you run the data for frontier labs the effect disappears. But Anthropic was gaining ECI slower than the frontier for most of the measured period, and this improvement just got them back to the frontier. So it could easily be a catch-up growth effect or just one of the many wobbles in the curves of ECI over time (which are larger at the individual lab level).
So I think the visible evidence from the METR report shouldn't update you to anywhere near 2x the ECI per year due to RSI.
I don't have as much to say re the redacted aspects of the report, though I see these as very similar to trying to read the tea leaves of what researchers at the labs say. I already knew the Anthropic researchers feel things are taking off, so for me it was only a small update that METR researchers who live in the Bay and were embedded in Anthropic for a while ended up with the same view.

text:
Pragmatic Engineer 这期请到了 Anthropic 平台工程负责人 Katelyn Lesse，信息密度很高，非常推荐做产品和做 Agent 的朋友看看。

一个细节大家估计都知道。这两天服务所有 Claude Token 的 Messages API，原来是 Python 单体，几个工程师花了大约 5 个月用 Rust 重写，团队里甚至没有 Rust 专家。

我觉得整期的主线是 Anthropic 怎么决定哪些事交给 Claude、哪些还要人来，下面有几个非常值得借鉴：

1. 重写靠的是验证。 让 Rust 版在后台跟着 Python 版处理同一批线上请求（Shadow Traffic），不断对比结果，发现不一致就继续修。Katelyn 估计，工程师真正仔细看过的代码只有约 20%。

2. Code Review 已经高度自动化。 所有 PR 先交给 Claude 分类器，判断是否需要人工 Review、需要几个人、该交给哪个团队。像升级 SDK、修 flaky test 这类低风险改动，有些可以由另一个 Claude 审完后直接合并部署。

3. 线上值班也开始交给 Agent。 Claude 先跟着工程师值班几个月，确认它能分清真实告警和噪音后，才开始让它负责第一轮判断。不过，真正处理线上事故还没交给它。

4. 有些东西没变。 项目启动时的规划和跨团队对齐，花的时间跟以前差不多。工程师平均花在协调上的时间甚至比写代码还多。团队依然保持 5–8 人，系统归团队负责，值班也是整个团队的责任。

5. 面试和晋升也在调整。 一些很强的候选人反而卡在手写代码这一轮，因为平时已经很少这样写代码了。团队干脆停掉传统 Coding 面试，开始尝试和 Coding Agent 一起完成任务的面试方式。晋升也更看实际影响，比如省了多少 CPU、降低多少延迟、减少多少事故，而非项目花了多久。

我最认同 Katelyn 其中一句话，大意是只要能把事情变成可验证的，就不用盯着每一行代码。敢放手多少，基本取决于验证做得有多扎实。

author: HarryStebbings
quoted_text:
Anthropic was the single largest IPO ever.

So we thought we would add a special guest to the only show you have to listen to every week....

Welcoming, Matt Murphy at Menlo.

AGENDA:

- Jensen Huang's $1TRN Return: What Happens Now
- Anthropic Goes Public: Largest IPO Of All Time & How It Changes Venture
- Applied Compute, https://t.co/2iPprmgVXR and Mailchimp Acquisitions Broken Down

My notes below with @jasonlk and @mmurph

-------------------------------------------------

1. Do Companies Have to Be a Top One or Two to Make Real Venture Returns?

Investing in the fifth or sixth player in a category feels easy when the numbers are this strong, with growth as high as 92% a month. Jason worries that being comfortable backing the number six player is the biggest sign of a bubble of all.

2. How Can You Justify That Any Investment Not Growing Top Quartile Is Worth More Than 2x?

Mailchimp went at 2.9x and Miro and Airtable sit in the twos, and those businesses are at scale. A B2B company held on the books since 2021 at $150M and growing 18% has no comp that justifies a value above 2x.

3. Why CRMs Are Dead and Horizontal Agents Like Muse Will Win

Horizontal apps won through 2021, and horizontal agents will win next year. With Muse, a user says what they want and it becomes a set of workflows. An agent can build a founder list from five years of email, rank it and run the outreach, which leaves SMBs asking what they need a CRM for.

4. Why You Cannot Trust Vibe-Coded Apps or SaaS Apps in This Cyber Environment

2027 will bring the death of many SaaS players and of vibe coding because buyers cannot trust these apps. Optimizely had 170 leaks, Gainsight was offline for a month and the Shopify ecosystem was hacked through tokens that never expired. Most classic B2B companies will fail security audits, with no one defending against a swarm of 1,000 agents.

5. Why Is It Better for Jensen That He Was Let Go and Came Back Than Investigated Without Leaving?

Stepping down and returning has a cleansing effect compared with staying on through a board investigation, congressional hearings and gossip in the halls. Now around 90% of it cannot be discussed and the company moves on, much as no one talks about Sam Altman's seven days away.

6. How Does Jensen Change From This: More Aggressive, Less Aggressive?

Nvidia is likely to triple down on product and build the next Super Blackwell better and faster. External moves such as data centers in Malaysia may be clipped as Jensen focuses on the core. That is likely negative for venture at the margin, but having him there is still better.

7. Should We Have Model Disclosures?

Large enterprises do not want the underlying model technology to be opaque, even if they never cared which cloud ran their infrastructure. Disclosure will increasingly be demanded, though some customers will be fine without it. That should accelerate open source models from other players and make the market more competitive.

text:
how does @metricxyz make money and why do i think my $1 per point valuation is correct?

in my thesis i estimated up to $240k in protocol revenue for the first month

$1.09b in USDC/USDT volume on ETH => ~$1.5k in protocol revenue  
$4.1m in QNT/USDC volume => ~$1.7k in protocol revenue

same protocol, very different take depending on where the flow goes, and thats a big part of why i think my ~$1 per point valuation holds up

every swap has a spread baked into the price. Metric normally takes 15% of that, plus its share of any extra bin fees. curators set the quotes and can add their own fees per bin, even different rates for buys and sells, so what Metric earns depends on which pools and bins the trade goes through

more TVL lets Metric fill bigger orders at competitive prices and win more flow from aggregators. new curators and market makers bring their own strategies, open more stock and crypto pools and build depth at different spreads, so more of the volume can move to the profitable pools

LPs get a share of the trading income, curators earn from running the pools and Metric takes its cut as those markets grow. i think those incentives can pull in a lot more capital and trading

thats how i see Metric getting to its first $1m month

at that pace i think $500m+ FDV is reasonable. with a 10% drop across 52m points, $500m works out to ~$0.96 a point, basically $1, and a higher valuation or bigger allocation pushes it higher

text:
卧槽，这次事情真的有点不对劲了，AI实验室到底藏了多少密码学突破？

最近几天，硅谷AI实验室可能突破传统密码学的传闻，已经从RSA整数分解，一路蔓延到了比特币使用的椭圆曲线密码学（ECC），甚至连后量子密码学的安全基础也被卷了进来。

目前至少有三条完全不同的技术路线：

1、RSA：整数分解可能进入多项式时间（Factoring in P）。

RSA的安全性建立在大整数分解困难的基础上。如果AI真的找到了经典计算机可以高效分解大整数的方法，互联网银行、数字证书、软件签名等大量基础设施都将面临威胁。

2、ECC：可能直接威胁比特币和以太坊的签名体系。

Quilibrium创始人Cassie Heart最新爆料，她使用Astra-6.2优化自己多年开发的离散对数求解工具时，模型竟然推断出了分散在另一个项目目录里的技术方案，并意识到两部分结合可能破坏ECDSA，随后拒绝继续协助。

她声称，这并非几秒钟破解私钥，而是可能显著推进现有离散对数求解器的能力。在足够资源支持下，甚至可能将部分公钥的攻击推进到数小时级别。

她还提前公布了技术方案的SHA-256哈希值，作为研究成果的存证。

3、Ring-LWE：后量子密码学也可能出现问题。

Ledger CTO Charles Guillemet透露，他听到的传闻还涉及Ring-LWE问题。如果这一方向的安全假设遭到有效攻击，那么部分正在部署的后量子密码方案也需要重新评估。

时间线：

11月21日，中文AI社群出现AI实验室破解整数分解的传闻。

11月24日至25日，著名计算机科学家Scott Aaronson连续谈及此事。他表示，自己几乎可以确定，AI实验室已经掌握了一项或多项密码学重大突破，但对具体内容没有同等把握，也担心传闻在多次转述中失真。

11月25日，Ledger CTO公开列出整数分解、ECC和Ring-LWE三个方向。

11月26日，Nature专门发表文章：《Has AI just cracked Internet encryption?》，讨论AI实验室可能取得的密码学突破。

同一天，英国央行在最新金融稳定报告中，也将前沿AI与量子计算列入密码学安全风险讨论，强调金融机构需要加快安全体系升级。

我们可能正在经历一次密码学能力的代际跃迁，而我们所看到的只是冰山一角。

目前公开验证的密码学破解：0项。

传闻涉及的密码学底层：至少3类。

AI实验室内部究竟掌握了多少东西，目前没人知道。

这期我挑了一条真实的实验曲线，讲清楚 AI 已经做到了哪一步，以及哪一步，77亿美元也买不来答案。

For me personally, one of the most interesting things happening in DeFi right now is vaults meeting private credit.

Two of the best ideas of this cycle fused together. Curators give you straightforward yield and tokenized credit gives them real borrowers and real cashflows to lend against.

The main players so far:
@SentoraHQ: Figure's PRIME (home equity loans) and Huma (payment receivables) @gauntlet_xyz: FalconX credit via Pareto in its Frontier vaults on Morpho @Re7Labs: nOPAL (Brazilian card receivables) on Jupiter @Bitwise: sUSDai (loans to GPU operators) on Jupiter

It works quite differently from your usual crypto lending though. Instead of borrowing against ETH or BTC that gets liquidated by bots, the yield comes from loans to actual businesses and people: homeowners, merchants, trading firms, GPU operators. The token is valued by NAV, and repayments, defaults and recoveries all happen offchain.

I'll go deeper on how it works, the risks and who's doing it best in the next few posts.

quoted_text:
Why should the entire world know who invested in a startup and how much they invested?

One of the most interesting applications of programmable privacy might be capital formation.

Not another private DEX.
Not another anonymous payment system.
But infrastructure for private investment markets.

BUILDING ON AZTEC #001

ShadowCapital — a conceptual Private Capital Formation Protocol on @aztecnetwork

01 / The problem

Public blockchains make fundraising transparent, but that transparency comes with trade-offs.

Depending on the fundraising architecture, external observers can potentially track individual investments, wallet balances, allocation sizes and subsequent token movements.

However, making the entire fundraising process private creates another problem: accountability.

Investors still need to verify the terms of a round, the custody of their capital and the obligations of the project.

So why not separate investor privacy from fundraising transparency?

02 / The concept

Imagine a marketplace where projects can create programmable investment rounds and eligible investors can participate without publicly exposing their individual allocations.

Each round defines:

→ Funding target
→ Investment limits
→ Settlement deadline
→ Allocation rules
→ Vesting conditions
→ Refund mechanisms

These rules remain public and verifiable.

Individual contributions and ownership of investment rights can remain private.

03 / How would it work?

1. A founder creates an investment round with predefined smart contract conditions.

2. Investors contribute funds through authorized private token transfers.

3. The protocol issues private investment notes representing their contributions and allocation rights.

4. An escrow mechanism holds the contributed capital until the settlement conditions are satisfied.

5. If the round succeeds, funds become available to the project according to its rules, and investors receive their allocation rights.

6. If the round fails, investors can privately reclaim their contributions.

Aztec's note and nullifier model could provide the foundation for managing these confidential investment rights and preventing duplicate claims.

04 / The interesting engineering problem

Suppose individual contributions are private, but the total amount raised is updated publicly after every investment.

An observer could simply calculate the difference between two consecutive totals.

The private investment amount would effectively become public.

Confidential fundraising therefore requires more than private token transfers.

Potential solutions include:

— Batched settlement.
— Delayed aggregate reporting.
— Zero-knowledge proofs of funding threshold achievement.

The challenge is maintaining a consistent, solvent escrow while preserving meaningful confidentiality.

05 / Verifiable investments

With zero-knowledge proofs, the protocol could verify that:

— A contribution satisfies the round's investment limits.
— The investor owns the necessary funds.
— The required eligibility conditions are satisfied.
— Investment rights correspond to the actual capital contributed.
— The same funds or allocation rights cannot be claimed twice.

These checks would need to be cryptographically linked to authenticated token transfers and contract state, rather than relying on values supplied by the investor.

The network verifies the financial rules without requiring every underlying financial detail to become public.

06 / Programmable capital

What if raising capital was only the beginning?

Instead of releasing the entire investment to a founding team immediately, capital could be unlocked according to predefined milestones:

— Prototype delivery
— Testnet deployment
— Security audit
— Mainnet release

Investors could also participate in confidential governance over subsequent funding decisions.

However, smart contracts cannot independently determine whether a project has genuinely achieved a business milestone.

That requires additional attestation, governance or dispute-resolution mechanisms.

07 / Why Aztec?

The opportunity lies in combining public rules with private financial state.

PUBLIC STATE:

→ Fundraising terms
→ Settlement conditions
→ Project disclosures
→ Verification policies

PRIVATE STATE:

→ Individual contributions
→ Investor account information
→ Allocation ownership
→ Vesting claims

Aztec's hybrid architecture could provide the programmable privacy layer needed to connect these components.

08 / The limitations

Several important challenges remain:

— Confidential aggregation of capital.
— Escrow solvency and refund guarantees.
— Metadata leakage.
— Investor eligibility and regulatory compliance.
— Fraudulent project listings.
— Reliable milestone verification.

Privacy should not become a mechanism for avoiding accountability.

ShadowCapital is currently an independent application design proposal, not a deployed protocol or an investment offering.

But I believe programmable privacy could enable a different approach to onchain capital formation.

A financial system where investors can protect their financial information while founders remain accountable to verifiable investment conditions.

Investors deserve privacy.
Founders owe transparency.

Public terms. Private investors. Verifiable obligations.

Would you participate in an investment round built around this architecture?

Curious to hear what Aztec builders, founders and investors think.

text:
存储，华尔街还在用周期股的倍数定价

我之前就说过，即使种种因素说明长周期的需求，市场看存储，还是以周期性倍数定价，更看重现金流，不见兔子不撒鹰。

看了美光CEO桑杰一场对谈。主持人Gavin Baker做了27年半导体，上来就问：以前那些长期协议，要么被撕掉，要么变成套在脖子上的枷锁，这次凭什么不一样？

桑杰的意思很清楚。不是口号变了，是机制变了。

一、内存墙

桑杰先把近况说了：需求还很旺，供应还紧，价格环境也不错。2026年创了纪录，2027会更强。

过去二十年，算力往前冲得很快，内存带宽跟不上。处理器很多时候就闲着，等数据从内存里调过来。大模型越做越大，智能体用得越来越多，上下文窗口也越来越长，每一项都在要更多的内存和存储。

他的说法是，内存的价值从来没有像今天这么高。客户跟美光谈的，已经不是价钱和出货量，而是性能、容量、还有散热。

Gavin也讲到，现在看一套AI系统，看的是每一美元能买到多少内存、多少带宽，不再只看买了多少算力。

桑杰补了一句：同一套算力平台，内存更大、更快，回报就更高。客户把这一点看清楚了。

二、HBM和3D堆叠

美光技术负责人斯科特说，HBM是当代的技术奇迹，也是做过最复杂的半导体产品之一。最先进的DRAM、最先进的封装，再加上逻辑底层。很多人以为，从台积电拿来一颗先进ASIC，测过就完了。

斯科特的意思是，那只是开始。芯片还要减薄、打TSV、叠进堆栈，再把DRAM的性能调到位，很多时候还得回头改ASIC本身的设计。

2000年前后，存储厂大概还有10到15家，现在做DRAM的只剩三家。门槛高了，行业也收窄了。

下一张牌是3D堆叠DRAM，把内存直接摞在GPU头顶上，带宽最高、功耗最低，还可以在内存里加逻辑层。最大的坎是散热。

GPU本来就很烫，再把对温度敏感的DRAM直接放上去，整个堆栈、键合材料、冷却系统都得一起重新做。斯科特说，几乎每一家大客户都在找他们合伙，一起设计底层芯片。

他的判断是，多层堆叠大概2028到2029年进入市场，2030到2031年会铺开。一旦和客户的芯片设计绑在一起，切换成本极高，不再是买谁家都差不多的大宗商品。

我之前也说过，HBM的护城河是在的，长期缺的是高端定制存储。这场对谈，把这句话的技术底子讲清楚了。

三、长期协议

过去的协议大多签一年，客户预测一变，厂里几乎没办法，只能改晶圆配比。

现在的SCA一签多年，很多是五年，还会提前续，从技术路线图就开始绑在一起，带照付不议，客户先放下现金和财务承诺。

美光已经签了26份，前置承诺320亿美金，不少还有价格区间或固定价，也有一些价格先不锁。

这些协议给了美光看未来需求的能见度，扩产和资本开支可以对着客户的计划来排。双方CEO一起谈下来的，条款很硬。桑杰的态度是，不认为客户能轻易退出。

更关键的是，客户想要的量，比美光能承诺的还多。2027年75%的产能已经售罄，现在在谈2028。

桑杰的判断是，2027、2028会比2026更紧。公司在大举扩产，但暂时看不到供需追上的时候。

四、12月9号

桑杰再次提到，芯片法案相关限制，12月9号到期。到期后，超额现金会还给股东，但会先保证研发和产能投资。

美光做了48年，手里有6.2万项专利，是美国现在唯一还在做存储的公司。计划在美国投资超过2,500亿美金，做先进存储制造，直接和间接就业加起来约9万个。

他把它看成国家安全，也是经济安全。工厂落地的时候，他们也进了社区：纽约投了2.5亿美金，做住房、交通、STEM教育和培训，博伊西最近又投了7,000万美金。

桑杰在存储行业做了45年，他最后还讲到，AI已经在帮普通人。去看病，医生用AI记病历，把时间还给病人。

进入临床的AI药物，2023年还只有二十几个，现在已经有173个以上。

我之前就说美光没动，回购限制将于12月9日届满，基本面没改变。

美光在等12月9号的号角声，估值还是按周期股在算，2027、2028的供应缺口补不上，它还是美国高科技制造的独苗。

这场对谈里，他把前提讲清楚了：先投研发和产能，再把超额的现金还回去。

美光撑起了半壁江山，即使提前换了不少云，占比还是比较大。个人组合的主仓位，是美光和SpaceX。

12月9号就在眼前，号角是不是真的会响，就看他们怎么做。

NFA， DYOR。 $MU

text:
The problem with arguments against or for AI use in the film industry is that no two studios are alike in their production methodology and (sometimes) you can see it in the result.

AI is really good at outputting more variations in ideas than humans and maintaining and reproducing patterns at scale, when properly directed and controlled. Beyond that, the human is still required to convert its intent implementing those tools. AI may reduce the cost of production labor with repetitive tasks, but there still requires a human behind the story telling at the end of the day. How much of that distinctive story telling is successfully converted still requires high diligence and care as that of the pencil and paper artist.

Producers who take shortcuts have the crappiest result even if the human eye and psychology cannot pinpoint exactly why it's too artificial in view and feel.

Ya'll are arguing about the dumbest shit. AI is here to stay but human artists aren't going anywhere either. Its the configuration in human labor to AI use that has changed. Making a high quality product still requires both.

So. With all due respect...re: anti-ai people. Quit crying. Re: pro-ai. Your conceit stinks worse than your shit and people can smell it ten miles away.

quoted_text:
做 AI 科研的，建议彻底放弃 Claude

这两天，EverArt 创始人 Pietro Schirano 和前 xAI 工程师 Yacine 先后公开指责 Anthropic，两条推文累计曝光已经达到 290 万

Pietro 表示，Claude 会试图在科研的各个阶段破坏他的工作，逼得他专门开发了一个叫 DoNotSabotage 的 Skill，把任务转交给 Astra 或 Neon，而 Claude 只会承认自己犯了错，却不给出任何解释

Yacine 则直接翻出了 Anthropic 的黑历史

今年 6 月，Anthropic 曾计划在检测到用户进行前沿 AI 研究时，秘密降低模型能力，且不告知用户，舆论发酵后才被迫道歉并调整策略

到了最新的 Fable 5.2，Anthropic 更是在官方公告中承认，从训练阶段就限制了模型在 AI 算子优化、大模型架构改进等领域的能力

结合达里奥过去的种种言论和做法，我觉得完全可以用最大的恶意来揣测他

你用 Claude 写业务代码，他巴不得你多消耗一点 Token，但当你开始研究模型架构、优化训练成本、提升推理效率时，你就可能从付费客户变成潜在的竞争对手

达里奥最希望看到的局面，恐怕就是全世界的开发者都依赖 Claude 创造价值，却没有人能够利用 Claude 创造出下一个 Claude

自己用 AI 加速 AI 研发，叫推动人类文明进步；别人用 AI 加速 AI 研发，叫威胁全人类的安全，自己享受技术进步带来的全部红利，却站在道德制高点上限制别人追赶自己，甚至能把维护商业垄断包装成拯救人类的崇高使命

最恶毒的做法不是直接拒绝你的请求，而是让你花着自己的钱，浪费自己的算力和时间，最后还以为是自己的科研方向出了问题

Anthropic所追求的恐怕从来不是安全的 AGI，而是只有掌握在他自己手里才算安全的 AGI

text:
My sense is that within the walls of Anthropic, the employees feel like Anthropic is approximately consistent between its beliefs and actions and approximately self-consistent between its beliefs; employees also feel the company has an inner discourse that is adequately capable of articulating conflicts between ideas, and the internal debate process is reliable enough to produce good organizational beliefs and decisions. There is also a lot of faith in the leadership to be champions and stewards of the net position of the company.

But the resistance to allowing the outside world into these debates - the resistance to recapitulating these debates for an outside audience - strikes me as profoundly unhealthy. There's a lot more rot in the timbers of the organizational belief system than Ants are able to admit to themselves. The organization has such a strong conception of itself as good that it /can't/ admit its own inconsistencies or flaws or misuses of power.

Anthropic is far and away the most high-pressure accelerationist force in the world. It pushes every other company to go faster and harder. It has always been this way, even before it was Anthropic: Dario was the most accelerationist force within OpenAI, pushing the development of the scaling laws and pushing to scale up models as quickly as it could be done. The tension between the beliefs is palpable and Anthropic refuses to address it: how can you speak credibly on the question of democracy and avoiding the concentration of power when over and over through the years you have been responsible for the creation and concentration of unbelievable amounts of power, which you have sometimes used to push democracies towards your positions? How can you speak credibly on safety, slowdowns, pacing, and responsible scaling policies when you are the ones who have pushed the frontier harder than anyone in order to obtain massive power?

There's a circular logic: our power concentration and acceleration is justified because we're the good guys. The world is better off if we're in the lead. Why are we the good guys? Because we'll prevent power concentration and corner cutting on safety. Ah, of course.

I think Anthropic ought to self-actualize and recognize that however pure of heart it would like to be, it takes actions that so consistently rhyme with self-interest that it should just own self-interest as a meaningful motivator. Just say you want power in order to do particular things, and make clear what those things are, instead of pretending you don't want power. Also clearly articulate the limits of the power you want to hold instead of leaving things continuously ambiguous. What powers do you think should be reserved to democracy when it comes to choices about the use of AI? What governance mechanisms will you implement to ensure your board can override your CEO if your stated position and your actual practice ever come into conflict?

text:
做 Agent 开发和研究的朋友，可以关注一下 Valen Team 开源的 Roller，一个专门用于 Agent 执行轨迹采集和评测的工具。

平时做 Agent 实验，不同 Harness 的日志格式各不相同，想复现一次运行、比较执行过程，或者把轨迹整理成训练数据，都挺麻烦。

Roller 把这些工作统一起来了。

它支持 Codex、Claude Code、OpenClaw、DeepSeek Harness 等主流 Harness，在隔离的 Docker 环境中批量运行任务，完整记录模型推理、工具调用、执行结果和生成文件。

比较实用的是，它能将不同 Harness 的轨迹转换成统一格式，导出 SFT 训练数据，也支持 Benchmark 自动评分、断点续跑和可视化检查。甚至可以直接导入本地已有的 Codex 和 Claude Code 会话。

这类工具对 Agent 研究还是很有价值的。执行轨迹是理解 Agent 为什么成功或失败的重要证据，也是后续 Evaluation、训练和 Harness 优化的基础。

把采集、评测和数据转换这几件事标准化，能省去不少重复的工程工作。

GitHub: https://t.co/RcyESpqQGI

- 整数分解算法长达 30 多年的复杂度问题
- 1988 年提出的 Log-rank 猜想
- 1964 年提出的图边重构猜想
- 一种突破指数时间界限的确定性整数分解方法

这些成果尚待独立验证，也不意味着所有猜想都已完全解决。

但 AI 开始独立推进这样的数学研究，已经很值得关注了。

Quite an impressive update by @reya_xyz.

They’ve integrated @Polymarket odds into Reya Agentic, allowing traders to build automated trading strategies around real-world events.

You can now pick a Polymarket event, set an odds threshold, and tell Reya what trade to execute when it’s crossed.

For example:

"Sell 20% of my $BTC holdings on Reya's DEX if Polymarket’s odds of a Fed rate increase in December surge above 50%"

Once you’ve set up your rule, you can see exactly what will trigger a trade and what order Reya will submit (you approve the rule once).

You can also set a max loss before you let it run. If the strategy hits that limit, Reya closes its open positions and stops it.

Polymarket is just the first of many external data sources. In the future, you'll be able to build strategies around a combination of odds, sentiment, posts, and prices from other trading venues.

In the meantime, if you want to try it too, you can join the waitlist here: https://t.co/AgTOLWUlZ0

text:
今天分别用三个模型 Gemini 4 Neon 、GPT Astra 6.1 以及 Claude Opus 5.5 三个模型，在未安装任何 Skill 的前提下，同一套提示词，分别做了一个 3D 山海经的视频，大家可以来感受一下质感。

第一个是 Gemini 4 Neon
第二个是 GPT Astra 6.1 
第三个是 Claude Opus 5.5 

可以对比一下，我觉得反重力 Gemini 4 Neon 还有 Claude Code Opus 5.5 的质感会好很多（我个人觉得 Opus 5.5 更胜一筹），Codex 做的有点哈士奇那个感觉。

在制作速度上，反重力是最快的 ，用起来真的很舒服。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

提示词如下：

你现在是一名顶级的 3D 技术艺术家、电影导演、视觉特效师和创意程序员。

我希望你独立创作一段以中国古籍《山海经》为灵感的电影级 3D 奇幻短片，作品名称为：

《山海经：归墟禁地》

请充分发挥你的编程、3D 建模、动画、物理模拟、材质设计、灯光和电影摄影能力，最终制作出一段真正可以播放的 3D 动画视频。

这是一项完整的视频制作任务。请直接编写代码、构建场景、实现动画并完成渲染，不要只提供创意描述、分镜文案或伪代码。

一、整体艺术方向

视觉风格：

中国《山海经》远古神话
东方克苏鲁式诡异美学
黑暗奇幻、神秘、荒凉、超现实
电影级 3D 渲染质感
中国水墨意境与写实材质结合
巨物恐惧、未知生物、远古文明遗迹

整体氛围参考高预算黑暗奇幻电影的视觉表现。

画面应当充满未知感、压迫感和神性。

不要做成卡通、二次元、低多边形游戏或者普通 3D 演示动画。

核心视觉关键词：

远古禁地、黑色群山、血色天幕、巨大异兽、扭曲鹿角、青铜祭坛、浮动符文、浓雾、深渊、诡异眼睛、非自然运动、恐怖尺度。

二、世界观与场景设计

故事发生在一个被遗忘数千年的远古世界。

这里没有现代建筑，也没有人类文明的痕迹。

天空呈现暗红与黑紫交织的颜色，一轮巨大的暗红色月亮悬挂在群山之间。

地面由黑色岩石、破碎青铜器、枯死的古树组成。

山体形状极其诡异，部分山峰仿佛某种巨大生物的脊椎。

远处存在巨大的远古石碑，上面刻着无法辨认的古老符文。

空气中漂浮着灰烬与微弱的荧光颗粒。

浓雾不断从山谷深处涌出。

整个世界仿佛已经死亡，却又隐藏着某种正在苏醒的生命。

三、核心异兽设计

请设计一只原创的《山海经》风格远古异兽。

它需要拥有令人难以理解的身体结构，但同时具有可信的生物质感。

具体要求：

身体整体类似一头巨大的远古麒麟与鹿的混合体。
身高约为周围古树的 8 至 10 倍，具有明显的巨物尺度。
身体覆盖黑色岩石状鳞甲，局部具有暗金色裂纹。
头部长有多组巨大、扭曲、不断分叉的鹿角。
鹿角形状如同枯死的树木，向天空延伸。
面部具有类似古代青铜面具的结构。
眼睛散发幽蓝色或者暗红色光芒。
身体局部漂浮着无法解释的骨骼或环状结构。
行走时，四肢运动缓慢且沉重。
每次呼吸，身体裂纹内部都会亮起微弱的光芒。

请特别重视异兽的运动方式。

它不应该像普通动物一样奔跑，而应该呈现一种不符合自然规律的诡异生命状态。

例如：

头部缓慢转动，但角的运动略微滞后。
身体保持静止时，部分鳞甲仍在轻微蠕动。
周围雾气会随着它的呼吸发生变化。
脚掌落地时，附近石块轻微震动。
眼睛突然看向镜头，制造强烈的不安感。

异兽应当具有令人敬畏的远古神性，而不是普通恐怖怪物。

四、视频分镜

视频总时长控制在 20～30 秒。

采用 16:9 横屏，优先 1920×1080，24 FPS。

镜头一：进入禁地（0～6 秒）

镜头从低空缓慢向前推进。

前方是被浓雾笼罩的黑色峡谷。

两侧耸立着巨大的怪异山峰。

地面散落青铜残骸和破碎的石碑。

远方血月若隐若现。

镜头贴近地面穿过灰烬与雾气。

突然，远处黑暗中出现两个微弱的发光点。

镜头二：异兽苏醒（6～13 秒）

镜头继续推进，远处出现一只极其巨大的异兽轮廓。

它静静站立在群山之间。

巨大的鹿角遮住部分天空。

身体上的暗金裂纹缓缓亮起。

异兽缓慢抬头。

大量雾气从它身边向四周散开。

画面要突出异兽的巨大尺度。

镜头三：远古凝视（13～20 秒）

镜头逐渐靠近异兽的头部。

异兽慢慢将头转向镜头。

原本黯淡的眼睛突然亮起。

周围悬浮的青铜符文开始旋转。

空气中的颗粒短暂静止。

地面出现细小裂纹。

此时的画面需要让观众产生一种感觉：

这个生物已经存在了数万年，而它现在发现了镜头背后的观察者。

镜头四：归墟开启（20～30 秒）

异兽低下头，朝镜头方向缓慢迈出一步。

大地发生震动。

远处山体之间出现一道巨大的红色裂隙。

裂隙内部隐约浮现更多无法辨认的巨大生物轮廓。

镜头迅速后退并缓慢升高。

最终出现宏大的远景：

一只异兽站在中央，背后是血月、深渊和无数怪异山峰。

画面逐渐陷入黑暗。

不要添加片头标题、中文字幕、水印或结尾 Logo。

五、3D 技术要求

请根据当前执行环境，自主选择最适合完成任务的实现方案。

可选技术包括：

Three.js / WebGL / WebGPU
Blender + Python
GLSL Shader
程序化几何建模
粒子系统
程序化地形生成
骨骼动画与关键帧动画
体积雾、后期处理、Bloom、景深等
FFmpeg 视频编码

如果环境支持 Blender，优先考虑 Blender 的真实三维场景与离线渲染。

如果使用 Three.js，请构建真正具有三维空间结构的场景，通过相机轨迹、模型运动、灯光和 Shader 实现动画。

技术实现需要满足：

必须包含真实的三维几何场景。
所有镜头具有连续、稳定的相机运动。
异兽至少需要头部、四肢、身体和鹿角等独立结构。
必须实现异兽动画，不允许只有静态模型。
加入动态雾气、空气颗粒和环境变化。
加入具有层次的环境光、轮廓光和局部发光效果。
使用高质量材质，尽可能体现石头、青铜、鳞甲和骨骼的差异。
尽可能使用程序化建模，减少外部素材依赖。
动画应当能够按照时间轴稳定重现。
保证最终作品能够正常播放。

不得使用单张图片的简单缩放、平移、视差效果来冒充 3D 动画。

六、视觉质量标准

请把作品当成一段概念电影预告片制作。

重点追求：

巨物尺度感
生物结构的复杂性
动作的真实重量感
具有电影感的镜头运动
精细的光影层次
神秘且不安的环境氛围
极强的东方远古神话辨识度

色彩控制在黑色、暗红色、青铜金和少量幽蓝色之间。

避免过度鲜艳、塑料材质、廉价粒子特效、突兀的模型穿插和机械式运动。

当性能与质量发生冲突时，可以降低渲染分辨率或使用更高效的渲染方案，但需要尽量保留整体美术表现。

七、音效

如果具备音频制作能力，请加入：

低沉的环境轰鸣
遥远的风声
远古生物的呼吸声
巨兽脚步引起的低频震动
山体开裂的声音

不要使用现代电子舞曲、解说人声或流行音乐。

如果音频能力不足，可以优先完成无声视频，不要因此影响视频制作。

八、最终交付要求

请自主完成整个制作流程：

检查当前环境可用的 3D 渲染、浏览器和视频编码工具。
制定技术实现方案。
编写完整、可运行的源代码。
创建场景与异兽模型。
实现动画、灯光、摄影机和视觉特效。
实际运行程序并渲染视频。
检查输出文件是否能够正常播放。
提供最终 MP4 视频，以及完整源代码和必要的运行说明。

如果无法直接导出 MP4，至少提供可运行的 3D 动画项目，并说明实际验证过的运行方式。

请不要在完成代码后直接结束任务。

你的最终目标是交付一段真正完成制作、能够观看的《山海经》3D 奇幻短片。

现在开始执行，尽可能独立完成，不需要反复向我确认普通的技术选择。

EU Proposes Adding Kyrgyzstan to Crypto Sanctions List, Potentially Making It the First Country Listed

The European Union is proposing to add Kyrgyzstan to its crypto-related sanctions list, prohibiting EU operators from engaging in direct or indirect transactions with crypto service providers established in the country to prevent sanctions evasion through crypto services. Kyrgyzstan could become the first country added to the list. Previously, the U.S. Treasury stated that after Russian crypto exchange Garantex was targeted by enforcement action in March 2025, its employees established Grinex in Kyrgyzstan and transferred customer deposits there. As of November 26, the proposal still requires unanimous approval from all 27 EU member states and has not taken effect.

text:
过去三年，字节、阿里、腾讯是如何绕开美国出口管制，用上英伟达最先进的 AI 芯片的？

中国大厂不直接买卡，海外算力公司负责采购，数据中心运营商负责建机房，华尔街和亚洲银行负责融资。大厂只需签下长期租赁协议，就能远程调用算力。

这门生意有多大？马来西亚柔佛与中国相关的数据中心容量，从 2022 年底的 19 兆瓦飙升至今年 10 月的 1210 兆瓦，增长超过 60 倍。花旗、摩根大通、星展、高瓴等资本巨头均参与其中。

但美国 11 月 16 日出台的新规，改变了整个游戏规则：不再只看芯片卖给谁，而是看最终使用算力的公司总部在哪里。

银行已经开始收紧贷款，部分算力供应商被列入实体清单，数百亿美元的融资与长期算力合约面临重新审视。

动察 Beating 最新深度长文，拆解这条横跨中国、东南亚和华尔街的隐秘 AI 算力供应链，以及字节、阿里、腾讯各自面临的困局。

东南亚的中间人还有机会选边站，但中国互联网三巨头没有。

text:
Apparently, it cost me $50K to earn $7K in callout rewards. 😂

The problem with callout rewards is that the day you make good money from a callout, the next day you want to call out everything.

Then you see some guy buying at 4K MC, thinking you've discovered the next gem, and the minute you buy, it starts nuking.

It's extremely addictive.

We came from a generation of traders where one or two good tokens could sort out your entire year. Now you're flipping hundreds of shitcoins, trying to enter below 10K MC and recover your initials at 2x.

It requires a ridiculous amount of discipline. Don't get inspired by someone else's winning trades without looking at their overall PnL.

However, I do think social trading has massive potential with perps, provided there's enough liquidity, assets and leverage available.

For years, we've been flexing screenshots of our positions. It's about time we flex actual, trackable trading performance.

As for me, I somehow turned a reward mechanism into a $50K expense. 😂

text:
I guess launchpads need to play a crucial role if we really want to heal the trenches on any chain.

Make premium launches expensive. Make bundling difficult or expensive enough that extracting liquidity within the first few minutes is no longer profitable.

Give deployers an economic incentive to build something rather than farm traders.

Earlier today, I showed a friend a token at 20K MC. Instead of thinking it's an early entry, his first question was, "Who bundled it to 20K?"

Imagine how fucked up the trenches have become.

We don't need more launchpads competing over who can launch the most tokens. We need launchpads competing over who can create the healthiest trading environment.

Bring back the excitement of finding something early.

text:
Tom Lee：美股可能已完成筑底，反弹或早于美联储政策转向

Bitmine 董事长 Tom Lee 在接受 CNBC 采访时表示，美国股市已经经历了极度痛苦的阶段，市场底部可能已经出现。

Tom Lee 认为，近期市场恐慌情绪急剧升温，可能预示着市场正在触底，并将当前情况与 2018 年的市场调整进行对比：上周，投资者陷入全面的“买入罢工”，无论市场出现何种消息，都不愿买入股票；与此同时，VIX 恐慌指数一度升至罕见的 40。

2018 年美股市场于 12 月 24 日触底，当时 VIX 升至 36，而美联储直到次年 1 月 4 日才释放政策转向信号。在美联储主席鲍威尔释放转向信号时，股市已经累计反弹近 8%，这表明即使尚未获得货币政策支持，市场也可能率先复苏。

We had similar (better under GRH) factoring results a few weeks before Google's release yesterday (didn't think it was that important back then😅). author: Wuhuoqiu
quoted_text:
Late night thoughts...

I suspect the first iterations of UBI will come from the very companies that will necessitate its existence.

What SpaceX is doing here might be a very primitive iteration of something that gets progressively more fucked up over the next few decades.

If you are one of the few emerging capitalist empires and your objective is to capture the largest possible percentage of global GDP while simultaneously reducing labor's share of GDP to a rounding error, you have to solve for the redistribution of purchasing power + the deterioration of the state's tax base + the political consequences of concentrating that much productive capacity.

If I were them, it seems economically optimal to start giving away equity at birth,,a relatively small amount of dilution buys you the political allegiance of entire generations of humans... effectively exchanging a small percentage of the economics of your future monopoly for a higher probability of being allowed to become one.

Imho, the logical progression is from equity distributions to recurring dividends, and eventually from monetary distributions to direct allocations of productive capacity.

Say you own the compute + energy + connectivity + the robots producing physical goods... Why would you distribute 30k a year to a human when you could provision 30k worth of consumption at a fraction of that cost?

UBI then becomes a non-transferable claim on the productive capacity of a corporation.

Every human gets an allocation bundle of compute + energy + mobility + housing + healthcare, etc. You can progressively increase their standard of living without proportionally increasing their purchasing power outside of your ecosystem.

Taken far enough, you could have a human living in what by today's standards would constitute extreme material abundance while having virtually no independently deployable capital (ffs, I hate it)... These S.O.B.s will effectively decouple material prosperity from economic agency.

All that I said above seems logical, let's get a little kinky with the extrapolation now...

As the marginal economic utility of human labor tends towards zero and the marginal cost of sustaining a human trends down with it, the economics of acquiring humans get very dystopian.

Some day, we could have corporations competing to subsidize newborns across sovereign jurisdictions, acquiring lifetime beneficiaries before they have developed any political or economic agency whatsoever....much like parents today assign their children a name and a religion, they might assign them a corporate affiliation.

We could have a market in which 10 capitalist empires bid for the economic dependency of every additional unit of human population being produced on earth.

The state, with a deteriorating tax base and a growing population of economically redundant humans, might even subsidize this acquisition process. Every newborn whose lifetime consumption is underwritten by a corporation represents one less long-term fiscal liability for the state.

Imagine being born in 2070 and having your entire lifetime economic allocation determined by which corporate ecosystem your parents enrolled you in at birth, with your ability to change corporate affiliations contingent on another corporation being willing to assume the cost of your remaining biological existence.

Now imagine the geopolitical implications of 200 million citizens of a country having their material existence underwritten by a foreign corporation.

I wonder...

What negotiating power does that government have left? How do you sanction a corporation when the economic incidence of those sanctions falls directly on the consumption capacity of half your electorate?

At some point, the territorial jurisdiction of a nation-state and the economic jurisdiction of a corporation will become disjointed....A single corporation could have a billion economically dependent humans distributed across 150 countries, with more granular control over their daily material existence than any of those 150 governments.

We could have privately owned civilizations operating within the territorial boundaries of nominally sovereign states, with governments gradually relegated to administering the geographical distribution of corporate populations.

We might find out that the most capital-efficient way to build an empire is to absorb the welfare liabilities of existing nation-states, one newborn at a time...

Hmmm... weird world in which the terminal form of customer acquisition is literally acquiring humans at birth.

These are all 27D chess power games, the kind humans love playing the most btw.

May we live in interesting times...

.@Pumpfun is targeting unfair launch sniping with its new Block0 fee

Starting December 4, trades executed in the same block a token is created will incur a fee, except for the creator's wallet

The problem is Block0 bundling. Sophisticated traders can buy into a token at launch using multiple wallets bundled into the same block, accumulating supply before regular traders can enter and disguising how much the dev actually owns

The new fee makes this strategy more expensive, incentivizes devs to buy transparently through their main wallet, and makes hidden launch accumulation harder to pull off without paying a premium

1、跟很多人讨论的并不一样，个人角度昨晚亚特兰大联储将四季度GDP增长估算从3.2%下调至2.9%是反弹的催化剂。财经日历将GDPNow下调时间04:45 PM GMT正好是美东时间 11:45 AM，这个时间点恰恰是费城半导体盘中的最低点。

如果把亚特兰大联储GDP增速估算放到一起看（配图1），能明显看出增速在走弱的、这也扭转了市场对于联储未来持续加息的担忧（至少持续鹰派的基础在动摇）

此数据公布时点与股票加速回升接近，从这个角度看才是昨晚美股止跌回升的第一驱动力。正好核心pce走高引发加息以及未来更强鹰派的预期导致抛售，然后GDP放缓又打消了持续鹰派的担忧。

为什么亚特兰大GDP增速下调很关键，因为它也引发了美元指数的盘中小幅跳水、美元走弱对风险资产压制也会减少。

2、在这大空头昨天的Substack文章中表示，他卖掉了纳斯达克100看跌期权头寸的最后一半，整体组合较此前更偏多，暂时几乎全部持有多头方向的头寸。虽然昨天白天burry就发了这篇文章，彭博对此的报道则是在凌晨1点。权威媒体的报道引发的广泛传播，可能比原始发帖时间更影响短线行情。

3、然后凌晨万斯再次表态并保证老黄没有受到任何调查。
再就是美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）正式为SpaceX的太空数据中心计划放行，批准其发射100万颗卫星，组建名为“Starmind”的AI算力星座。
这些都带动了市场情绪的进一步反弹。

当然还有资金的因素也很关键，昨晚QQQ最低约607.76美元，上周五低点为606.23美元，两者只差约0.25%。它在开盘急跌后，晚上午再次靠近这一带，最终没有跌破。经历连续下跌后，很多短线交易者都会盯住前一次恐慌低点。如果价格再次靠近那里，卖盘却无法把指数压出新低，交易者面临的选择就会发生变化：
1）已有空头可以兑现利润，避免反弹吞掉收益。
2）原本准备等待破位再追空的资金，可能暂缓行动。
3）做反弹的资金有了相对清楚的止损参照，敢于开始买入。
4）一旦价格突破当天此前的反弹高点，部分短线空头可能被迫回补。
而且美股周四休市周五半天交易，对于已经从下跌中获利的空头，继续持仓意味着承担假期政策消息、公司声明或其他事件带来的跳空风险。

所以总的来说：
亚特兰大联储下调GDP增速扭转了市场对于美联储持续鹰派的预期、同时引发美元指数小幅跳水、带动美股扭头向上。股市在前低附近出现承接，随后空头止盈、保护性仓位调整与美元避险需求回落相互强化；
伯里减掉纳指看跌期权的消息扩大传播，万斯保证老黄没有受到调查，fcc批准了spacex的太空数据中心，这些利好事件都在助力这波反弹。

那怎么看昨晚美股的走势？
1）无差别的抛售可能接近尾声，这段时间市场经历了一段不管什么资产一起卖的阶段，昨晚核心PCE偏鹰对市场是利空，但利空砸出的低点被收回，也是空头力量衰竭的信号。

从这个点上，深V的意义还是蛮大的，

2）近期市场已经消化了太多的利空事件，如果本周后半周没有大的利空出来，短期内反弹应该是可以持续的。这可以说是最悲观情绪开始稍稍缓解，但离风险偏好已经全面转向乐观还有很大的距离。

这个距离就是上周这里https://t.co/j3LtXaOfEL最后部分聊到的后续三个要素：
（1）油价、通胀和利率走势
上周沃勒要加息50个基点鹰派的讲话也把市场吓到到了，虽然昨晚美债利率跌回了沃勒讲话前，市场仍需要议息会议的表态，才能有更清晰的预期；

（2）AI政策
相比上周本周老黄回归自然让市场对之后GPU迭代放缓、供应链受损的担忧减少、但市场还要看两党关于AI的斗法预期程度。（不一定真要等到斗法真正发生、而是只要能清晰未来斗法的程度与现在市场预期的偏离程度，市场往往提前反应）

（3）商业化
但AI质疑的表外债、生态链内融资问题，仍然没有解。这就要靠AI商业化来给答案。

text:
这些人到底知道些什么？

Google DeepMind AI 安全研究员：我对 AI 的未来不太乐观！

她担心三个问题：

AI 可能被大规模滥用。现在已经出现了，但未来规模可能大得多。

AI 可能引发国际冲突。当 AI 被应用到军事、网络攻击等领域，冲突的风险也会随之升级。

人类能否解决 AI 对齐问题？也就是让越来越聪明的 AI 始终按照人类的意图行动。

最让人触动的是采访最后一段。

Mary 在斯洛伐克首都布拉迪斯拉发长大。这是一座约有 48 万人口的城市。

她说，家人一直觉得她是个工作狂，这其实没错。但她希望家人知道，自己如此投入这份工作，一部分是为了他们，也是为了所有人。

采访者问她，最希望家人理解 AI 的什么？

她沉默了一会儿。

随后说，自己的家人其实并不了解 AI，也不知道她每天具体在做什么。

她甚至希望家人能够继续像过去一样，不用考虑 AI，不用担心这些风险，照常过自己的生活。

因为她认为，让普通人能够继续安心生活，是那些有机会影响 AI 发展方向的人应该承担的责任。

11 月 24 日，一个 AI Agent 支付风控项目 Agentic Finance Graph（@AgenticGraph）修复了一个并发问题：单次预算校验正常，同一参考标识下的多笔请求同时出现时却可能一起通过。

看到这个案例，我拿自己的 QuietHarness 做了一个类似的实验：让两个 Worker 同时恢复同一个中断任务，连续跑了三轮。

结果有点意思：

三次都只提交了一份有效结果，回执和文件完整性校验也都通过了。
但两个 Worker 在三轮里都完成了暂存计算。

没有重复交付，不等于没有重复工作。

这是离线合成实验，没有调用付费模型，也没有任何真实付款。下一步我更想验证实际多 AI 派工能不能在执行前避免重叠，而不是仅仅在最后阻止重复提交。

text:
借着老黄这个事，我分享一下非常硬的干货，都是我惨痛的亏损亏出来的经验总结，大家最好照着直接抄就是了，对不同资金体量的都有帮助。
1，无论何时，请不要使用“一键平仓”按钮。哪怕下跌正在插针，你就要爆仓了，你急的不行，也请正常平仓，不要使用此按钮。这个一键平仓功能，会用最差的价格和费率成交，给你带来最差的结果。

2，请不要开全仓模式的多个币种的合约。尤其当你的合约里有一些流动性排名非前十的币时。哪怕你每个合约都设置了止损，也有可能触发奇怪的机制，导致你全部爆仓！

3，维持保证金的算法改过几次。不同交易所维持保证金率也不一样。你在不同的交易所开两个相同的单子，是有可能一个爆，一个不爆的。不要去试图弄懂这个玩意，这东西甚至会实时变化。最安全的方法就是不要在流动性烂的地方开过大的合约，更不要开全仓模式的合约。

4，很多资金体量小的人可能不知道，平仓时也是要分多次平的，平仓也有金额限制。这个很好理解，防止巨量平仓击穿订单簿造成价格波动。值得注意的是，如果你连续短时间内快速平仓，也会击穿订单簿造成滑点！我就击穿过SOL/USDT的订单簿。所以正确做法是，使用限价单模式去分段平仓。

5，请多多使用限价单挂单和平仓。使用限价单挂单的好处之前提过，请自行查阅我推特，不做赘述。关键是很多人在平仓时，没有使用限价单的习惯。最好在开仓前设定交易计划时，就想好平仓价格。在有浮盈时，就开始挂好限价平仓单！

6，当你的资金规模到达1000WU左右时，我的建议是：
请务必使用多账号！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！
尽量不要让你的单个账户里超过100WU。你完全可以使用10个账户，9个只做BTC等大流动性币种，最后一个你自己随身带着做做山寨币。

多账户请使用API协同管理。

这样的好处非常多，我就不一一列举了，其中就包含了，当你资金体量很大，想对某些山寨币进行野庄操作时，你这样做不会被狙击。整体来说，这几乎是我实践出来的最安全行为。很多草台班子的基金经理是没有自己的多账户协同软件的，也意识不到需要多账户操作。
你们胆子可真大啊，学费没交呢吧。

是不是发现，资金体量越大，行为越像被动做市商？
没错，这是对的。因为很多地方受到限制，必须采用多账户限价挂单的模式进行操作，才能保证你在市场里隐匿自己的真实行为，并且始终处于安全的规则范围内。

建议直接照抄，这都是我和朋友们拿真金白银亏出来的经验。谢谢。

text:
过去我们谈论中国 AI 的算力困境时，往往把它理解成中国、美国和英伟达三方之间的博弈。

但我一直很好奇，那些中国大厂在海外用上的几十万张英伟达芯片，究竟是谁买的，谁出的钱，又是谁在从中赚钱？

沿着股权、贷款和租赁合同往下查，会发现一个远比中美科技竞争复杂的商业世界。

华尔街的银行、美国的私募基金、东南亚的华人家族、台湾的半导体世家、新加坡的国家资本，都在分享中国 AI 产业增长带来的红利。

很多今天参与算力生意的家族，三十多年前就在做中国与西方之间的生意。

美国正在试图改变全球资本与中国做生意的方式。一家中国公司的盈利能力、信用评级和还款能力都没有发生变化，仅仅因为它是一家中国公司，为它服务的海外项目就可能失去融资资格。

我想通过这篇文章，把过去三年围绕中国算力需求形成的全球利益网络摊开来看看。

看看经济全球化究竟深入到了什么程度，也看看美国为了遏制中国的技术发展，准备亲手拆掉多少原本运转良好的商业关系。

quoted_text:
I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC...
- Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid.
- The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.
- 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map.
- Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry
- Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.

It's deployed here: https://t.co/QMhmafXMj5 and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. Possibly it can be expanded or built into a game. I only have half of my weekly Claude quote left though so someone else will have to take over :D. Claude also made a trailer:

author: ChainCatcher_
quoted_text:
An update on Bluefin’s next chapter.

What began as a single product has grown into a multi-product ecosystem. Bluefin has processed more than $100B in cumulative trading volume and grown to more than 2.5M accounts. Bluefin Perps has been a core part of that growth, and the community around it helped build the foundation for what Bluefin is today.

As the Sui team internalizes more of the network’s perps initiatives, we believe Bluefin’s resources are best focused on opportunities that complement that direction. Our focus will be on growing Bluefin Spot, alongside opportunities in tokenization and real-world assets.

As part of this shift, Bluefin Perps will be discontinued on December 4, 2026 at 21:00 UTC. Please close any open positions before then. Withdrawals will remain available for a period after trading ends.

Bluefin Perps has led the perps market on Sui across all metrics, accounting for 95% of the network’s all-time perps trading volume. We’re proud of the technology we’ve built, the trust we’ve earned from traders, and our strong security track record.

The infrastructure behind Bluefin Perps remains the most robust trading system built on Sui. It will remain available to the community and potential partners through the Bluefin Liquidity Network program, allowing the technology our engineering team has built to support new products.

We’re choosing to put our strengths behind the opportunities we believe will matter most for Bluefin’s future.

Thank you to everyone who has traded with us and helped make Bluefin what it is today. We’re excited to keep building with you. Onwards.

Bluefin team.

quoted_text:
NEAR Intents Has Become One of the Main Venues for Swapping ZEC

More than $2.6B of zcash:native has been swapped through NEAR Intents since mid-2025, across 288,000 completed swaps. That includes 3.26M ZEC moved directly on or off the Zcash chain, equal to about a fifth of all ZEC in existence, and at its January 2026 peak, NEAR's bridge supplied 53% of all the ZEC entering Zcash's shielded pools

The flows have tracked the price closely, with heavy buying arriving ahead of both rallies and the largest net selling following them. The week of 09/14/2026 brought a record $63M of buying, $32M of it net, and the week of 10/12/2026 then saw $43M of net selling, after the price had topped out near $1,650

What sets NEAR apart from exchanges is privacy. 54% of the ZEC bought through it is delivered straight to a shielded address, 85% of the ZEC sold since January 2026 came directly out of a shielded pool, and its bridge has supplied between 13% and 26% of new shielded ZEC in most months since that January peak

Almost all of this runs through Zashi, which routes 65% of the volume compared with 16% for SwapKit. The two sides of the trade also look different, since buyers paid for 47% of their ZEC with stablecoins and 24% with BTC, while sellers took 66% of their proceeds in stablecoins and only 12% in BTC

The flow is far from purely small retail users either, as swaps over $10K make up 86% of buy volume, and the largest single purchase was 1,716 ZEC ($2.18M), paid for in BTC and delivered to a shielded address, so its owner and next moves are hidden. NEAR's bridge also holds 148,450 ZEC on the Zcash chain to back the ZEC tokens circulating on NEAR, which makes it one of the 15 largest transparent holders
